d: 搬 bān (to move heavy things; to transport) + 进来 jìnlái (in-coming; into this space). The directional complement 进来 specifies both the direction (in) and the orientation toward the speaker (来). The 把 construction signals the chair is a definite, specific object being moved as a deliberate act.

e: to finish the homework (do it through to completion)
d: 做 zuò (to do) + 完 wán (to finish; to exhaust; resultative complement). The 完 is the result , the homework has been completely done. Without 完, the sentence would be ungrammatical: *把作业做. 完 is one of the most common resultative complements in the 把 construction.

e: hegemony; domineering; the way of force
d: 霸 bà (hegemon; overlord, one who rules by force rather than virtue) + 道 dào (way; path). Classically: governing through coercion rather than moral example, the antithesis of 王道. Colloquially in modern Mandarin: overbearing, domineering (of a person's behavior).

e: hegemon lord — power exercised without moral mandate
d: 霸 bà (dominate by force) + 主 zhǔ (lord, master). Mencius drew the sharpest formulation of the distinction between 王 wáng (true kingship through moral virtue) and 霸 bà (hegemonic dominance through military and economic power): 以力假仁者霸 "one who uses force while pretending to benevolence is a hegemon" (…
白 bái (white) + 菜 cài (vegetable). The pale-stalked cabbage that anchors northern winter cooking. So cheap and plentiful that 白菜价 "cabbage price" means dirt cheap.

e: white tea — minimally processed; wither and dry
to eat for free; to freeload
white down — the fine hairs on young buds

d: 白 bái (plain; white; clear; spoken) + 话 huà (speech; talk) + 文 wén (written text). Writing that matches how people actually speak. 白话 literally = "plain speech," the ordinary spoken language as opposed to the elevated classical register.

e: baijiu — the spirit most often paired with a hotpot meal
White-Robed Guanyin — the most common home altar image
d: 白衣 báiyī (white robe) + 观音. The seated figure in a white robe, often with a willow branch and a small vase, depicted on or near a lotus throne. This is the Guanyin of domestic altars across Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, and Southeast Asian Chinese diaspora communities.

e: percent; out of a hundred parts
d: 百 (hundred) + 分 fēn (parts, divide) + 之 zhī (of, possessive particle). Literally: "out of a hundred parts." Chinese writes percentages as 百分之X , 百分之五十 (50%), 百分之百 (100%).

e: all kinds of goods; department store
d: 百 (all kinds of) + 货 huò (goods, merchandise). 百货公司 (bǎihuò gōngsī, "all-goods company") is the standard Chinese term for a department store.

e: a hundred schools; all schools of thought

d: 百 (all) + 科 kē (branch of study, department, subject). The term for encyclopedia: 百科全书 (bǎikē quánshū, "complete book of all branches of knowledge"). 百度百科 is the major Chinese-language wiki encyclopedia.

e: a hundred years; a full generation; a lifetime
d: 百 (hundred) + 年 nián (year). A century, but also a metonym for a full human span or a generational unit of history. 百年大计 (bǎinián dàjì, "a great plan for a hundred years") means a long-term fundamental strategy.

e: The hundred-day mourning period following a death
d: The hundred-day mourning period following a death. During this time the bereaved family observes restrictions on celebration and festive activity. A commemoration ceremony at the end of the hundred days formally closes the mourning period.

百 (hundred; all) + 姓 xìng (surname). The full range of surnames = everyone who is not nobility. The warm, slightly literary word for "the people." 老百姓 (lǎobǎixìng) adds 老 (old, familiar) for a more affectionate, colloquial tone. Political speeches say 人民; everyday speech says 老百姓.

e: to be defeated; to suffer a loss
d: 败 (bài, to be defeated, to lose) + 北 (běi, to flee , the original meaning). The classical military compound where 北 carries its original "flight in defeat" meaning. Used in formal and literary contexts for losing a battle, an election, or a competition.

e: to venerate the gods; to pay respect at a deity's altar
d: 拜 bài (to bow; to worship; to pay respects) + 神明. The standard verb for the act of ritual veneration , burning incense, bowing, presenting offerings. Common in Taiwan, Fujian, and diaspora communities. The word 拜 is secular enough (拜访 = to visit) that 拜神明 does not sound archaic or overly formal.

拜 bài (to bow; to pay respects) + 堂 táng (hall; the family hall). The three bows of the traditional Chinese wedding: first bow to Heaven and Earth (一拜天地), second bow to the parents (二拜高堂), third bow to each other (夫妻对拜). Each bow ratifies the marriage before a different authority.
两班倒 (liǎng bān dǎo) is two rotating shifts; 加班 (jiābān) overtime. Shifts and headcount tell you real capacity better than a capacity figure does.

e: a way; a means; a solution
d: 办 bàn (to handle; to manage) + 法 fǎ (way). The practical way to get a concrete thing done or to solve a problem at hand: 想办法 "to think of a way," 没办法 "there's nothing to be done."

Half. Follows the measure word when added to a whole quantity (一个半, one and a half) and precedes it when alone (半个小时, half an hour). Also in 半天 (bàntiān, "half a day"), the standard exaggeration for "ages."

A hand gift: a gift brought in hand when visiting someone, the material expression of having thought of the host. Turning up empty-handed (空手 kōngshǒu) to visit someone's home, especially a first visit, is considered poor form. The 伴手礼 need not be elaborate; the gesture matters more than the object.
绊 bàn (to trip) + 脚 + 石 shí (stone). The foot-tripping stone. Both literal (a stone in the path) and figurative (an obstacle to progress).
帮 (assist) + 忙 (busyness): to take on someone's busyness. The polite request is 帮个忙 or, upgraded, 帮我一个大忙 (do me a big favor). Direct objects go on bare 帮.
帮 bāng (to help) + 手 shǒu (person; hand). A helper , someone who lends a hand. Also 帮忙 bāng máng (to help out , the common spoken form) and 帮助 bāngzhù (to assist , more formal).
For your interpreter, or for the English-speaking salesperson when the engineer goes too fast. Using an interpreter for one hard passage and Chinese for the rest is common and costs no face.

e: give me a hand; help me out
d: A model of 一下 as a politeness softener. The bare 帮我 ("help me") is blunt; adding 一下 frames it as a small, quick favor and sounds far friendlier. Note that 一下 can follow the object here (帮我一下) because 帮 takes a person directly. The same softening works across requests: 看一下, 等一下, 问一下.

e: role model; good example to follow
d: 榜 bǎng (a posted list, a board) + 样 yàng (model). A person held up as a pattern for others: 树立榜样 "to set an example," 学习的榜样 "a model to learn from."

棒 bàng (staff, blow) + 喝 hè (shout, roar). Two of the most distinctive Chan teaching methods: a sudden shout (associated especially with the master Linji 临济, whose shout 喝 became the name of the Rinzai school) and a strike with a staff (associated with Deshan 德山).
To wrap, to enclose , the verb for making dumplings (包饺子), as well as the root of 包子 (stuffed bun). Also means "to guarantee" or "to take responsibility for."

彩盒 (cǎihé) is the retail colour box, 内盒 the inner box, 外箱 (wàixiāng) the master carton, 装箱数 the units per carton. 唛头 (màitóu), from English "mark," is the shipping mark printed on cartons. 跌落测试 (diēluò cèshì) is the drop test.
饱 (full) + 餐 (cān, meal): to eat heartily, to feast. Often appears as 饱餐一顿 (bǎocān yí dùn, to have a good filling meal), with a faint literary warmth.
饱 (full) + 含 (hán, to hold inside): to be charged with, brimming with. Used for tears, feeling, or meaning, as in 饱含深情 (bǎohán shēnqíng, brimming with deep feeling).
饱 (full) + 和 (hé, to mix, to combine): saturation. A technical term for a solution, market, or air that can absorb no more, as in 市场已经饱和 (shìchǎng yǐjīng bǎohé, the market is already saturated).
饱 (full) + 满 (mǎn, full to the brim): plump and rounded, or figuratively brimming with vigor. Describes grain, fruit, and spirits alike, as in 精神饱满 (jīngshén bǎomǎn, full of energy).
The general term for an NDA. NNN协议 is the China-specific form. Ask for it to be signed and sealed before you send drawings, not after.

e: to preserve intact; to keep safe and whole
d: 保 bǎo (to protect) + 全 quán (intact). To keep something whole and unharmed through a threat: 保全性命 "to preserve one's life," 保全名誉 "to keep one's reputation intact." The intact sense made active.
报 (to requite) plus 仇 (chóu, enmity): to pay back a wrong. The dark twin of 报答, turning the same logic of return toward vengeance.
报 (to requite) plus 答 (dá, to answer): to answer a kindness with thanks made real. Reserved for repaying gratitude, a warmer word than the neutral 回报.

报 bào (to announce; to report; newspaper) + 道 dào (way; path). To map and announce the course of events: journalism as the act of charting what has happened. Used both as a noun (a report, a piece of coverage) and as a verb (to report on something).
报 (to announce) plus 告 (gào, to tell): to deliver an account formally, and the document that delivers it. Works as both the act of reporting and the written or spoken report itself.

报价 (bàojià) is both the verb "to quote" and the noun "quote." Ask for it in writing, line by line: 分项报价 (fēnxiàng bàojià) is an itemised quote that breaks out the product, packaging, tooling, and printing.

e: to call the police; sound an alarm

d: 报 (to report) plus 名 (míng, name): to report your name onto a list. The standard verb for signing up or enrolling for a class, a contest, or an exam.

报 bào (newspaper) + 社 shè (an agency, office). The organization that produces a newspaper, both the institution and its premises: 在报社工作 "to work at a newspaper." The 社 here is the institutional body, not a club; the same slot gives 出版社 "publishing house" and 杂志社 "magazine office."
报 (the thing announced) plus 纸 (zhǐ, paper): the daily report rendered on paper. The everyday word for a printed newspaper, and the head noun behind titles like 《人民日报》.
暴 bào (violent; cruel) + 力 lì (force). Force used to harm, the dark side of 力: 家庭暴力 "domestic violence," 暴力行为 "violent behavior." Here strength has turned destructive.
悲 (grief at suffering) + 悯 mǐn (pity; compassion for the unfortunate). A literary compound for the quality of being moved by others' misfortune , closer to pity or sympathy than the more active 慈悲.

e: the seven stars of the Big Dipper
d: 北斗 (the Northern Dipper) + 七星 (seven stars). The seven bright stars of the Big Dipper, central to Chinese astronomy, navigation, and Daoist ritual.

e: Beigang Chaotian Temple — Taiwan's great Mazu shrine
d: The Chaotian Temple (朝天宫) in Beigang, Yunlin County, Taiwan, is one of the oldest and most revered Mazu temples on the island, traditionally dating its founding to 1694 CE. With Dajia's Zhenlangong, it is one of Taiwan's two dominant Mazu pilgrimage centers.

北 (north) + 京 (capital). The Northern Capital , counterpart to 南京 Nánjīng (Southern Capital). Beijing has served as the capital of the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, and of the People's Republic. The name dates to 1403 when the Yongle Emperor moved the Ming court north from Nanjing.

Beijing dialect: the basis of standard Mandarin (普通话 pǔtōnghuà). Beijing speech is characterized by heavy retroflex consonants and the 儿化 (érhuà) suffix that makes 这里 → 这儿, 哪里 → 哪儿. A strong Beijing accent is audible and distinct.

e: back; to carry on the back

d: 背 bèi (back of the body; to turn one's back on) + 后 (behind). The space behind a person's back , the zone they cannot see. In figurative use, 背后 means to act covertly, without someone's knowledge or consent. 在背后说人坏话 (to speak ill of someone behind their back) is a strong social criticism.

e: got hit; was beaten (by an unspecified agent)
d: When the agent is unknown, irrelevant, or deliberately omitted, the 被 construction works without naming who did the action. The 被 alone signals passive and adversarial meaning.

e: to have one's views "represented" without consent
d: 代表 dàibiǎo (to represent; a representative). 被代表 = someone else speaks for you without your authorization and claims to represent your interests or views.

Discovery can be neutral or positive in English (a new species was discovered), but in Chinese the 被 frame typically implies the subject was caught or uncovered against its will or to its disadvantage. 被发现 often implies that someone was hiding something that has now been exposed.

Misunderstanding, misrepresentation, and mistreatment are quintessential 被 territory. The speaker's intention or the subject's nature is distorted by someone else's interpretation. The adversarial quality is strong , no one wants to be misunderstood.

e: to be "suicided" — killed and declared a suicide
d: The most striking 被XX neologism. 自杀 zìshā means "to kill oneself" , a self-directed, voluntary act. Making it passive (被自杀) creates a grammatical impossibility that points to a political reality: a death classified as suicide that was, in the speaker's understanding, not self-chosen.

e: to dash; to run hard; to gallop
d: 奔 (bēn, to rush; to gallop) + 跑. A more vivid and literary form than plain 跑. 奔 originally described the gallop of a horse; 奔跑 carries that sense of full-speed exertion.
Materia medica: the traditional term for the pharmacological literature and its subject matter.
Twelve chapters chronicling the central line of power: the legendary sage-kings, the Xia, Shang, and Zhou, the Qin, and the Han emperors down to Wu.

e: originally; at first; (it goes without saying that)
d: 本 běn (root; origin) + 来 lái (come). What was the case from the start, before things changed: 我本来想去 "I originally meant to go (but didn't)." It often carries a quiet sense that the original state was the natural or proper one.

e: oneself; the person in question; I (formal)
d: 本 běn (this; one's own) + 人 rén (person). The very person concerned, as opposed to a representative or a rumor. On forms and in formal speech it means "I myself": 本人同意 "I personally agree."

e: ability; skill; what one is capable of
d: 本 běn (root; one's own) + 事 shì (matter). The capacities a person carries in themselves, their real skill rather than their luck or connections: 有本事 "to have what it takes." A close synonym is 本领 běnlǐng.
本 běn (root; origin; this) + 土 tǔ (soil; native place). Native, local, domestic, contrasted with 外来 wàilái (from outside) or 进口 jìnkǒu (imported). 本土品牌 = domestic brand. 本土文化 = local culture.

本 běn (root, origin) + 性 xìng (nature). The nature one is born with, deep and hard to change: 本性善良 "good-natured at the core." Often invoked when surface behavior gives way to what a person really is, as in 本性难移, that one's nature is hard to alter.
本 běn (volume) + 子 zi (suffix). A blank or ruled book to write in. Here 本 takes the toneless noun-suffix 子, exactly as in 桌子 and 房子.
笨 (bèn, stupid, clumsy) + 蛋: a fool or dimwit. Among close friends it softens into teasing, even affection, but aimed at a stranger it lands as a real insult.

"For example" or "like, for instance." Introduces a concrete illustration of an abstract point. Among the most useful phrases for explaining anything. The shorter 比如 works identically; 比如说 just adds a beat of preparation.

笔 bǐ (brush; pen) + 画 huà (to draw; stroke). The individual strokes that make up a character. Chinese characters are analyzed by stroke count (几画 jǐ huà "how many strokes?") and stroke order (笔顺 bǐshùn).

笔记 bǐjì + 本 běn (a bound volume; classifier for books). Originally: a bound notebook for handwritten jottings. Now also: laptop computer (笔记本电脑 bǐjìběn diànnǎo), the device that replaced the paper notebook for many people, while keeping the name.

Pen name: a literary pseudonym. Many Chinese writers and poets are better known by their pen names than their given names. Lu Xun (鲁迅) was born Zhou Shuren (周树人); his pen name is how he is universally known.

e: brush and ink; brushwork as a concept
the present writer; this author (formal self-reference)
d: 笔 (brush; pen; writing) + 者. Used in formal written Chinese as a modest self-reference: "the one holding the brush," meaning the author of the text you are reading.

必 bì (certainly) + 定 dìng (settled; fixed; determined). A speaker's confident prediction about the future or about something not yet observed. The certainty is in the speaker's judgment, not a rule or law. Closer to "I am certain that" than to "you are required to."

必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 然 rán (so; thus; naturally so , the word for "naturally" or "as it must be"). Together: that which is naturally and necessarily the case, which could not have been otherwise. The register is philosophical, historical, or scientific.

e: certain to win; victory is assured
d: 必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 胜 shèng (to win; to overcome). A morale-building formula rather than a measured prediction. Used in sports, military contexts, and competitive settings where the declaration of certainty is itself motivational. The certainty is willed, not merely predicted.

e: one must admit; it must be acknowledged that
d: A common rhetorical move in essays and serious conversation, conceding ground before pivoting. The 必须 here is not commanding the listener; it is the speaker acknowledging an inescapable point. English equivalent: "it has to be said that," "one must concede that."

e: must comply with; must abide by (rules, laws)
d: The standard pairing in legal, regulatory, and policy language. 必须遵守法律 (must comply with the law). The phrase carries the formal-rules register that 必须 lives in: every Chinese workplace handbook, public notice, and company memo will use this collocation rather than its softer alternatives.

e: necessary; required; essential (for a given purpose)
d: 必 bì (certainly; without exception) + 要 yào (to want; to need; required). Necessity defined by a purpose or goal: if you want the outcome, this is what the outcome requires. The conditionality is built in.

毕 bì (to finish; to complete) + 业 yè (studies). To complete one's course of study: 大学毕业 "to graduate from university," 毕业典礼 "graduation ceremony." A separable verb, so the object slots in the middle: 毕了业 "have graduated."

避 bì (to avoid; to deflect) + 雷 léi (thunder/lightning) + 针 zhēn (needle; pin). Lightning rod. Literally: the needle that deflects the thunder. Metaphorically, a 避雷针 is a person or thing that absorbs blame or controversy on behalf of someone else , a lightning rod in the political sense.
边 (biān, border; edge) + 关 (guān, pass; strategic gate). The fortified checkpoints through the wall where military control, taxation, and passage were managed.

变 biàn (to change) + 成 chéng (to become; to complete; to succeed), the directional complement. The standard compound for completed transformation: X has fully become Y. 成 is the result complement, indicating the transformation has landed somewhere definite.

e: to change the laws; political-legal reform (historical term)
d: 变 biàn (to change) + 法 fǎ (law; method; the Dharma, depending on context). The classical Chinese term for fundamental legal and institutional reform: changing the very rules by which a state operates.

变 biàn (to change) + 革 gé (to reform; leather, the image of tanning a hide and stripping away the old surface). 变革 carries more structural weight than 变化: it implies change to systems, institutions, or fundamental arrangements, not merely surface conditions.

e: changing hexagram; colloquial: to change one's mind, go back on one's word
d: In the 易经, 变卦 biànguà is the technical term for the resultant hexagram, the second hexagram produced when changing lines (爻 yáo that have reached their extreme) transform. The 变卦 reveals where the present situation is moving.

变 biàn (to change) + 化 huà (to transform; to dissolve into something new). The most general and most frequent word for change in modern Mandarin. Where 变 alone is the verb of transformation, 变化 is the noun: change as a thing that happens, can be observed, measured, discussed.
变 (to change) + 坏 (bad). To turn for the worse, whether food spoiling in the heat, weather souring, or a person's character degrading over time.
The basic request, best softened. 价格有点高 (the price is a bit high) states the problem without accusing; 还有空间吗 (is there still room?) invites a counteroffer without naming one.

e: to debate; to argue (a formal case)
d: 辩 biàn (to dispute, to argue points) + 论. To debate opposing positions, each side marshalling arguments to win. The standard word for a debate competition (辩论赛 biànlùnsài) and for adversarial argument generally.

e: a marker; a label; to mark
d: 标 biāo (to label, to mark out) + 记 jì (a mark). A marker or tag that identifies a thing, and the act of placing it: 在地图上标记位置 "to mark a location on a map."
标 biāo (to mark; label) + 题 tí (heading). The title line printed at the top of an article, book, or section: 新闻标题 "a news headline," 大标题 "a big banner headline." Literally the marked heading.

e: to express: to convey; to articulate (thoughts and feelings)
d: 表 biǎo (to bring to the surface) + 达 dá (to reach; to arrive at; to get through). To convey thoughts or feelings so that they reach another person clearly. The 达 element adds the sense of successful transmission: not just showing something, but getting it across.
表 (maternal/external) + 哥. An older male cousin on the mother's side, or through a paternal aunt. The 表 prefix marks cousins outside the father's patriline, distinct from 堂哥 (tánggē).

e: form: a table; a chart; a grid laid out for filling in
d: 表 biǎo (a chart; a surface where data is laid out) + 格 gé (a grid; a square; a cell). A printed or digital form, table, or grid: anything with rows and cells to be read or filled in.
表 biǎo (outer; to show) + 面 miàn (face). The outer surface of a thing, and by extension the surface meaning as opposed to the truth beneath: 表面上 biǎomiàn shàng "on the surface, ostensibly."

The finishing family: 抛光 (pāoguāng) polishing, 电解 (diànjiě) electrolytic polishing for liners, 喷涂 (pēntú) spray painting, 喷粉 (pēnfěn) powder coating, 丝印 (sīyìn) screen printing, 镭雕 (léidiāo) laser engraving. 涂层 (túcéng) is the coating itself; 掉漆 (diàoqī) is paint coming off.

e: outer skin: the epidermis; the outermost layer or rind
d: 表 biǎo (outer) + 皮 pí (skin; hide; rind). The outermost layer of a living thing: the epidermis of human skin, the rind of a fruit, the bark-like surface of a plant. A precise term used in biology, medicine, and everyday talk about peels and surfaces.

e: to express: to indicate; to show (a feeling, attitude, or position)
d: 表 biǎo (to bring to the surface) + 示 shì (to show; to indicate; to make manifest). To express or indicate an attitude, opinion, or feeling, often through a word, gesture, or symbolic act. 表示 frequently introduces what someone states or signals: 表示同意 (express agreement), 表示感谢 (express thanks).

e: to show; to display; (noun) performance, conduct, showing
d: 表 biǎo (outer; to express) + 现 xiàn (show). To make an inner quality visible on the outside. As a noun it is one's showing or conduct: 他今天表现很好 "he did very well today."

e: to perform: to act; a performance; a show
d: 表 biǎo (to show outwardly) + 演 yǎn (to act; to perform; to develop). To perform before an audience, and the performance itself: music, dance, drama, magic, acrobatics.

别 bié (other; different; another) + 人 rén. The default, everyday word for "other people" in spoken Mandarin. Neutral register, very high frequency. Used in advice, comparisons, complaints, and social commentary; the most natural choice whenever you mean "other people" in conversation.
宾 bīn (guest) + 馆. A house for guests, that is, a hotel. The word keeps the old hospitality sense of 馆 right on its sleeve.

e: military strategy; the art of war
is not in fact; really is not
d: 并 bìng (actually; emphatic) + 非 fēi (not). A firm, slightly formal "is not at all," used to push back against an assumption: 并非如此 "that is not the case," 并非不可能 "not in fact impossible."
并 bìng (side by side) + 且 qiě (further). Links two actions or qualities on an even footing, often joining verbs: 讨论并且决定 "to discuss and decide." Neutral where 而且 leans emphatic.
病 + 毒 (dú, poison): a "sickness poison," the standard word for a biological virus and, by extension, a computer virus. The same term covers the flu and the malware on your hard drive.
病 + 房 (fáng, room): the room where patients are kept, a hospital ward. It pairs naturally with 病床 (bìngchuáng, hospital bed), bringing the original sickbed of the radical 疒 full circle.

e: to die of illness; to pass away from sickness
d: 病 (bìng, illness) + 故 (here, to pass away). A measured, somewhat formal way to say that someone died of illness, used in obituaries, official notices, and dignified speech. The 故 draws on the deceased sense: the dead belong now to what has passed.
病 + 菌 (jūn, bacterium, fungus): a disease-causing germ. Where 病毒 names a virus, 病菌 names the bacterial culprit, the everyday word a parent uses when telling a child to wash their hands.
病 + 情 (qíng, situation, state): the state of a sickness, how the illness stands. Doctors use it to report whether a patient is stable, worsening, or improving.

病 + 人 (rén, person): a sick person, the general word for a patient in a hospital or clinic. It names the person by their condition rather than their role, unlike 患者 (huànzhě), which is the more clinical register used in medical writing.

打 dǎ (to hit) + 破 pò (broken; shattered , resultative complement). The 破 is the result that makes the sentence grammatical. Breakage is typically undesirable , a window, a vase, a screen. The 被 construction here makes the glass the focus: it is the thing that suffered the breaking.

e: the master qin player (Spring and Autumn period)

d: 博 bó (broad, extensive) + 物 wù (things) + 馆. The hall of broad things, where relics and specimens are kept and shown. 故宫博物院 uses 院 instead, but the everyday word is 博物馆.

e: to mend; to patch; to supplement
to remedy; to make good; remediation
pretty good, not bad; correct, right
d: 不 bù (not) + 错 cuò (wrong). Two readings from one shape: as praise, "quite good, not bad" (成绩不错 "good grades"); as confirmation, "right, correct" (一点不错 "exactly right"). Note the tone sandhi: 不 shifts to bú before the falling 错.

不 bù (negation) + 道德. The direct negation , applied to actions, behavior, people, and policies alike. Notably versatile in everyday condemnation: this is the word a person reaches for in an argument when something feels wrong without being illegal.

e: cannot but; have no choice but to
d: 不得不 (not-obtain-not) = double negation creates strong obligation: "cannot not do" = must do, compelled by circumstances. Stronger than 必须 bìxū in the sense of reluctant necessity. The speaker has no choice.

不 + 得了 déliǎo (can be concluded; can be over). "Cannot be concluded" → extreme beyond measure. Used after adjectives as a strong intensifier: 好得不得了 = incredibly good. Also standalone: 不得了！= This is unbelievable / It's a disaster! (depending on context).

e: not all; not every one (partial negation)
d: 不 precedes 都. The negation falls on the universal claim: "it's not the case that all of them do X." Some do, some don't. This is logically weaker than 都不 and much more common in careful, qualified speech.

e: might as well; no harm in

d: "However" or "but" (softer). The default conversational pivot. Lighter than 但是, which can feel direct or even adversarial in spoken contexts. 不过 carries a gentler "that said…" tone, ideal for adding a qualification.

e: embarrassed; sorry to trouble you; excuse me
d: Lit: not-good-meaning/face. The phrase used when imposing on someone, asking a favor, or causing mild embarrassment. One of the most important social lubricants in Mandarin. Not a strong apology, more like "I feel awkward about this" or "pardon the imposition."
"No way!" or "you can't be serious." Expresses disbelief, often at bad news or an unwelcome outcome. The 吧 softens it from an outright denial into an incredulous reaction.

e: to be missing, to have disappeared
not merely (formal pair for 而且)

d: The strong negation of 可: not merely "cannot" (unable) but "cannot be permitted to." Formal and classical in flavor. 不可 carries the weight of prohibition rather than incapability.

The flat negation, "impossible, no way." 这不可能 ("this is impossible"), 不可能的事 ("an impossible thing"). It is strong and absolute, unlike the softer 不太可能 ("unlikely") which leaves a sliver of chance. As an exclamation, 不可能！means "no way! / that can't be!"

不 bù (negation) + 快 kuài. The heart is not flowing freely , something is blocking it. Milder and more internal than 不高兴 (visibly in a bad mood); 不快 often describes a quiet dissatisfaction or sense of offense that hasn't been expressed.

e: not coming anymore; decided not to come
d: 不…了 is the negation of sentence-final 了 , it signals a reversal of an expected or prior state. The 了 here paradoxically signals a new situation: the new situation is "not doing X anymore." Extremely common for announcing changed plans, habits that have been given up, or states that have ended.

e: one who gains without working; one who reaps without effort
d: 不劳而获 (to gain without labor) + 者. A full predicate (verb phrase plus adverb) nominalized by 者. The resulting noun phrase can serve as subject, object, or object of a preposition. This is 者 at its most generative: even a four-character predicate can be converted into a noun phrase by appending 者.

Percentage of defective units; 良品率 or 良率 (liánglǜ) is the yield, its complement. 不良品 (bùliángpǐn) and 次品 (cìpǐn) are defective goods. Agree an acceptable rate in the contract and what happens above it.
不 bù (not) + 论. Functionally interchangeable with 无论 in most sentences, slightly less formal. Same grammar: an open element follows, and 都 or 也 marks the main clause.

e: otherwise; or else; if not so
d: 不 bù (not) + 然 rán (so). Literally "if it is not so," hence "otherwise." Warns of the alternative outcome: do this, 不然 the bad thing happens. Close to 否则 fǒuzé but more colloquial.

e: inhumane; callous; morally numb — also: physical numbness (limbs without sensation)
d: 不 bù (not; without) + 仁 rén (humaneness). The negation that reveals the concept's full weight: to be without 仁 is not merely to be unkind , it is to be morally deadened, incapable of feeling for others.

e: not taking it seriously; phoning it in
not as good as; would be better to
d: 不 bù (not) + 如 rú (as good as). Either ranks one thing below another (A 不如 B, "A is not as good as B") or proposes a better course ("we'd be better off..."). Context tells the two apart.

e: "not eating the smoke and fire of the human world" — otherworldly; too aloof to be of this world
d: Literally: "does not eat the smoke and fire of 人间." Originally said of immortals (仙 xiān) and deities, who subsist on pure air rather than cooked food and are therefore free of the desires and needs that tie mortals to this world.

e: is not; to not be; it's not that…
d: The negation of 是 , always 不是, never 没是 (unlike verbs of action, which can be negated with 没 for past tense).

e: it wasn't me who said it (correcting the agent)
d: The classic defensive use of 不是…的: denying agency for a known past statement or action. Both parties know something was said , the 不是…的 corrects the attribution. This is one of the most practically useful forms of the construction in daily social life.

e: it wasn't bought yesterday (correcting the time)
d: Time correction: both speakers know the item was bought , the correction is about when. 不是昨天 denies the specific time; the speaker may then supply the correct time with 是…的.
Unwell: "not comfortable." The all-purpose symptom, the polite sick-day excuse, and the doctor's opening question in negative form: 哪里不舒服?

e: not very; not too; not quite
d: 不 bù (not) + 太 tài (very). The gentle negative, softer than a bare 不: 不太喜欢 "don't really like it," 不太方便 "not very convenient." The standard polite way to decline or downplay.

Decide before the dinner whether you drink, and say it early with a reason that leaves no one at fault: health, medication, an early meeting, or driving. Once you have drunk one toast, refusing the next is harder.
Price is rarely negotiated at the table, but the boss may ask a soft question about volume or the future. Answer warmly and without numbers; numbers belong in the meeting room the next day.
不 bù (not) + 同 tóng (same). The standard word for "different": 不同的意见 "differing opinions." As a noun it names the difference itself: 两者的不同 "the difference between the two."

Negate with 不 before the verb. To soften, insert 太: 不太喜欢 ("don't really like") is gentler and more polite than a flat 不喜欢. For a stronger feeling, 讨厌 tǎoyàn means "to find annoying, to dislike intensely."

e: not OK; won't do; no good; (terminally) declining
d: 不 bù + 行 xíng. The everyday refusal: "no, that won't work." 行 on its own as an interjection means "OK, fine, that'll do" , and 不行 is its negation. Also extends to "not capable" (我数学不行 "I'm bad at math") and, in context of illness or business, "in serious decline" (他不行了 "he's failing / fading").

Grades by number: 201 is cheaper and less corrosion-resistant, 304 is the common food-contact grade, 316 adds molybdenum for better resistance to acids and salt. 材质 (cáizhì) is "material" in the sense of grade and composition.
"Not necessarily." A gentle pushback that leaves room for the other person's view to be partly right. Often used to introduce a qualification: 不一定吧, 也可能是… ("not necessarily, it could also be…").

Negates the obligation: putting 不 before 应该 says something ought not to be done: 你不应该对她说谎 ("you shouldn't lie to her"). Often it voices regret about the past, "should not have": 我不应该那样说 ("I shouldn't have said that"). Do not confuse with 应该不, where 不 falls after and negates a guessed event instead.

e: no need to; don't have to
don't know; I'm not sure; I have no idea
d: 不 bù (negation) + 知道. One of the most common phrases in conversational Mandarin: the honest, unadorned acknowledgment of not having found the path. As a standalone response, 不知道！is perfectly natural and socially acceptable (not rude) in most contexts.

不 (not) + 足 (sufficient). The negation of sufficiency. 时间不足 (insufficient time); 不足为奇 (not enough to be surprising , meaning "nothing to be surprised about"); 美中不足 (a flaw in an otherwise perfect situation , literally "not enough in the beautiful center").

Composition: the arrangement of characters and space within the seal face. Considered the most demanding aspect of seal design: the carver must balance the visual weight of characters with varying graphic complexity, distribute space evenly, and create a design that reads as a coherent unit when imp…
部 bù (unit) + 队 duì (team; formation). A body of troops under one command, from a single unit up to the armed forces in general: 参军入部队 "to join the army." Soldiers say 在部队 "in the service."

部 bù (section) + 分 fen (a share). A part of something larger, the everyday word for a portion: 大部分 dàbùfen "the greater part, most of," 一部分 yí bùfen "a portion." Note the second syllable goes neutral.
部 bù (section) + 门 mén (gate; category). One demarcated wing of a company or institution: 销售部门 "the sales department," 政府部门 "government departments." The standard word for an organizational unit.

e: radical (the section head of a character)
d: 部 bù (section, division) + 首 shǒu (head). The radical of a character: the head-element under which a dictionary groups it. 首 itself is a 部首. To look a character up in a paper dictionary, you find its 部首 first, then count the remaining strokes.
部 bù (ministry) + 长 zhǎng (chief; head). The head of a ministry or department: 外交部长 "the Foreign Minister." The 长 here is the leader-sense, read zhǎng, not the cháng of "long."
才 before a quantity expresses that the amount is smaller than expected or desired. This is the scarcity / insufficiency use of 才: the number is barely enough, disappointing, a minimum.

才 cái (talent) + 能 néng (capacity). The abilities a person actually possesses and can put to use: 发挥才能 "to give full play to one's talents." Note the toned reading cáinéng (the noun); the adverb 才 plus 能 (cái néng, "only then can") is a separate construction.

e: talent and wisdom; intellectual gifts; ability and discernment
d: 才 cái (talent; natural ability , the character shows a seedling breaking through the earth, raw capacity before cultivation) + 智 zhì (wisdom; discernment). The pairing of natural gift with cultivated understanding. 才智过人 cáizhì guòrén = talent and wisdom surpassing others.
财 (money, property) plus 富 (riches). The accumulated stock of wealth itself, the noun for what a rich person holds. Often paired abstractly, as in 精神财富 (spiritual wealth).

e: the Wealth God — most actively invoked deity in commercial life
d: Cáishén is not one deity but a cluster of wealth-associated gods, the most popular being 赵公明 Zhào Gōngmíng (a dark-faced general riding a black tiger) and the Five Roads Gods (五路财神 Wǔlù Cáishén). His image greets visitors at the entrances of shops, restaurants, and banks across China.

Betrothal gifts , the payment from the groom's family to the bride's family as part of the formal engagement. In contemporary China, the cash component (also called 彩礼钱) has become a source of social tension in areas where amounts have escalated sharply.
菜 cài (dish) + 单 dān (list; slip). The list of dishes a restaurant offers, and by extension the drop-down 菜单 of a computer program. 看菜单 "to look at the menu."

菜 cài (here: weak, lousy) + 鸟 niǎo (bird). A fledgling, hence a beginner who is still bad at something, especially in gaming and the workplace. Self-deprecating or teasing: 我是个菜鸟 "I'm a total newbie."

Cuisine system , the term for a recognized regional cooking tradition. The 八大菜系 (eight great cuisine systems) are the canonical eight, though culinary scholars recognize anywhere from four to dozens of regional traditions.

参 cān (to take part) + 观 guān (to view). To visit a place in order to see it: a museum, factory, school, or exhibition. Reserved for touring sites, not for visiting people, where 看望 kànwàng or 拜访 bàifǎng is used instead.
Silk thread , literally "silkworm thread." The raw fiber before weaving. 蚕 is the silkworm; 丝 is the thread.
原材料仓 raw-material store, 成品仓 finished-goods store. A tidy warehouse with labelled batches (标识 biāoshí) is a good sign of traceability.

e: Cao Cao — the archetype of cunning ambition
d: The warlord of the north, in the novel the great villain: a brilliant general, administrator, and poet, but ruthless and treacherous, the man who declares he would rather betray the world than let the world betray him.
草 cǎo (grass) + 地 dì (ground). Any stretch of ground covered in grass, from a park lawn to an open meadow. 在草地上 "on the grass."
草 cǎo (rough) + 稿 gǎo (manuscript). The first, unpolished version of a piece of writing or a plan. 打草稿 "to make a draft," to sketch something out before committing.
草 cǎo (rough; hasty) + 率 shuài (rate; rashly). Done quickly and without care, like grass thrown up overnight. 做事草率 "to do things carelessly."
草 cǎo (straw) + 帽 mào (hat). A hat woven from dried straw, the broad-brimmed shade of farmers and summer beaches. 戴草帽 "to wear a straw hat."

e: cursive script — the most expressive and wild form
d: 草 cǎo (grass; rough; draft) + 书 shū. "Grass writing" , like wild grass, cursive is fast, flowing, and irregular. Individual strokes merge; some characters are radically abbreviated. Legible mainly to trained readers. The style most associated with artistic expression and emotional intensity.
草 cǎo (herb) + 药 yào (medicine). Medicine made from plants, the leaves and roots brewed in traditional Chinese pharmacy. Often expanded to 中草药 zhōng cǎoyào, Chinese herbal medicine.
草 cǎo (grass) + 原 yuán (plain). A vast open plain of grass, the wind-rippled steppe of Inner Mongolia or the prairies of the world. 内蒙古大草原 "the great grasslands of Inner Mongolia."

e: the heart of compassion / commiseration — sprout of 仁 humaneness
d: 恻隐 cèyǐn: the feeling of alarm and pity , specifically the involuntary distress one feels at another's suffering. The child-at-the-well example demonstrates this sprout. It is the first beginning of 仁 rén (humaneness/benevolence), the master virtue.

e: to measure: to survey, to gauge with an instrument
d: 测 cè (to gauge, to fathom) + 量 liáng (to measure). The formal verb for taking precise measurements: surveying land, gauging distance, recording temperature or pressure with an instrument. 测量土地 (to survey land), 测量距离 (to measure distance).

e: to butt in; to insert oneself into someone else's affair
d: 插 chā (to insert) + 一 yī (one) + 脚. To stick a foot in where it wasn't invited , usually meddlesome but sometimes opportunistic. Cousin of English "to put one's foot in." Often pejorative.

e: wearing zhuyu sprigs — apotropaic plant, festival shorthand
d: 插 chā (to insert; to wear tucked in) + 茱萸 zhūyú (Cornus officinalis; Japanese cornelian cherry). The zhuyu shrub, with its fragrant berries and pungent scent, was believed to repel evil and disease. On Double Ninth, people wore sprigs tucked into their hair or carried them in small pouches.

Cha chaan teng: the quintessential Hong Kong casual restaurant, serving a fusion menu of Cantonese and Western-influenced dishes: milk tea, pineapple buns (菠萝包 bōluóbāo), egg tarts, congee, rice dishes, and Hong Kong-style French toast.

Teahouse: a social institution especially important in Sichuan and Guangdong, where one goes not just to drink tea but to play mahjong, listen to storytelling, or simply spend a morning reading the paper.

e: tea down — fine white hairs on young leaves
tea display dish — for showing the dry leaf

d: Teapot. The Yixing purple clay teapot (紫砂壶) is the prestige form, prized because it absorbs tea oils over time and improves with use.

e: theaflavins — the brightness compounds of black tea
tea tongs — for handling hot cups
Ancient Tea-Horse Road — the trade route that carried tea to Tibet
tea tray — the base of the gongfu setup
Tea leaves , the dry product before brewing
d: Tea leaves , the dry product before brewing. 茶 alone can refer to the beverage, the plant, or the leaves.

e: tea art; the art and ceremony of tea
d: 茶 chá + 艺 yì (art; skill, the same character as in 艺术 fine art). The performance and aesthetic dimension of tea preparation. 茶艺师 cháyìshī = tea master; a professional practitioner of the ceremony. 茶艺表演 = a tea ceremony performance.

e: a slip, an error; a mishap going wrong
d: 差 chā (off, deviating) + 错 cuò (error). A small slip or accidental error, and by extension an unforeseen mishap: 万一出了差错 "in case something goes wrong." Both halves mean "off the mark," doubling the sense of deviation.

e: to abdicate in favor of the worthy
d: The shàn reading's flagship: throne-yielding on the Yao-and-Shun model, the Confucian ideal of succession by virtue rather than blood, and the polite fiction wrapping most actual dynastic seizures.

e: Chan Buddhism — meditation, direct transmission, sudden enlightenment
d: The most distinctively Chinese Buddhist school. Chan (from Sanskrit dhyāna, meditation) rejected scripture-based study in favor of direct mind-to-mind transmission between master and student, the use of paradoxical dialogues (公案 gōng'àn, kōans), and the possibility of sudden enlightenment 顿悟 dùnwù i…

Output per day or month. 排产 (páichǎn) is scheduling an order onto the line; 旺季 (wàngjì) is peak season, when capacity disappears. In the months before Chinese New Year lines fill up and many workers leave early, so lead times stretch.

认证 rènzhèng (to certify, certification , 认 recognize + 证 proof/certificate). The system by which products are officially verified to meet standards. 3C认证 (China Compulsory Certification) is the mandatory certification for electronics, appliances, and vehicles sold in China.

质量 zhìliàng (substance + quantity → quality) is the standard word for quality in both the everyday and technical sense. 产品质量 is the fixed phrase for product quality , appearing in consumer protection law (产品质量法), manufacturing standards, and marketing.

Made on the production line with production materials, after tooling and before bulk starts. Hand samples can be perfect while line samples are not; insisting on a 产前样 catches the difference before thousands of units exist.

e: to produce; to give rise to; to emerge
d: 产 chǎn (to produce; output) + 生 shēng (arise). For abstract and concrete creation , ideas, problems, emotions, consequences arising. 产生影响 "to have an effect" · 产生误会 "to give rise to a misunderstanding."
The reduplicated 常. A common, conversational adverb for frequent action. Its negative is usually 不常 bùcháng "not often," since 不常常 is avoided.
常 cháng (constant; common) + 识 shí (knowledge). The basic knowledge that holds across a community, what one is expected to know: 生活常识 "everyday know-how," 缺乏常识 "to lack common sense."

e: to deliberately disagree; to sing a different tune
d: 唱 chàng (to sing) + 反调 fǎndiào (an opposing tune). To voice the contrary position on purpose, to be the one who always sings against the prevailing note. Colloquial and faintly critical.

唱 (sing) + 歌 (song). The social institution attached is KTV (卡拉OK), where 唱歌 is what colleagues, classmates, and business contacts do together; declining every song is borderline antisocial, and one rehearsed number is sound survival strategy.
唱 chàng (to sing) + 片 piàn (a thin flat piece). A singing-disc: the physical record that holds recorded sound. 唱片公司 chàngpiàn gōngsī is a record label. The word predates and survives digital formats.
Vocal style , the melodic and tonal patterns of a particular role type. Different roles use different vocal registers and melodic conventions.

钞 chāo (paper money) + 票 piào (slip; note). A banknote, paper currency, cash in hand. This compound shows 票 at its purest: a printed slip of paper that stands for money. Closely related is 支票 zhīpiào (a cheque), where 支 zhī (to pay out) marks the slip as an instrument of payment.

e: to surpass; to exceed; to transcend
d: 超 (chāo, to overtake; to exceed) + 越. The figurative summit of the family: surpassing a competitor, exceeding a limit, transcending a category. Used in business, sport, philosophy, and self-development contexts.

e: dynasty: a reigning house and its era
d: 朝 cháo (court, reign) + 代 dài (generation, age). The standard word for a dynasty, the span during which one ruling house held the throne. Chinese history is told as a sequence of 朝代, each with its own name, capital, and character.

e: youthful spirit: vigor, the lively air of a new day
d: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 气 qì (air, energy). The energy of morning seen in people, a fresh, lively spirit. Said of the young or of any group full of drive: 充满朝气 "brimming with vigor." Its opposite is 暮气 mùqì, the listlessness of dusk.

e: forward; toward the front; facing ahead
d: 朝 cháo (toward) + 前 qián (front). Directed at the space ahead: 朝前走 "walk forward," 朝前看 "look ahead." A close everyday counterpart to 向前.

e: the imperial court: the ruler and the central government
d: 朝 cháo (court) + 廷 tíng (court hall). The ruler together with the ministers and offices around the throne, the seat of central power. To act 代表朝廷 is to act in the name of the throne itself.

e: morning and evening: every hour, day after day
d: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 夕 xī (evening). The two ends of the day standing for all of it: from dawn to dusk, every hour. 朝夕相处 "to be together morning and evening," to live in close daily company; 只争朝夕 "to seize every moment."

e: to face toward; the aspect or facing of (a building)
d: 朝 cháo (to face) + 向 xiàng (toward). To face a given way, or the facing itself. Common in describing buildings: 这套房子朝向南 "this flat faces south," a prized aspect for sunlight in Chinese homes.

e: the morning sun: the rising sun, dawn light
d: 朝 zhāo (morning) + 阳 yáng (sun). The sun as it rises, and the fresh light it brings. Used figuratively for anything new and full of promise: 朝阳产业 "a sunrise industry," a sector on the rise.

e: toward; in the direction of (with sustained motion)
d: 朝 cháo (toward) + 着 zhe (the durative marker). The preposition with a sense of ongoing facing or movement toward something: 朝着大海 "facing the sea," 朝着目标努力 "to work toward a goal." Common in figurative aims as well as physical ones.

e: to mock; to ridicule; to jeer at
d: 嘲 cháo (to taunt; to deride) + 笑 xiào (laugh). To laugh at someone with scorn. This is the cruel edge of 笑: the same sound aimed downward at a target. Takes a direct object, the person mocked.
炒 (chǎo, to stir-fry) + 蛋: eggs broken into a hot wok and pushed around until they set in soft curds. The same 炒 powers most Chinese cooking, so 炒蛋 reads as plainly as English "scrambled eggs."
G-trains are the fastest, D-trains next. 检票口 (jiǎnpiàokǒu) is the boarding gate, shown on the screens next to the train number; 车厢 (chēxiāng) is the carriage, 座位号 the seat number.
Named by process: 冲压车间 stamping, 焊接车间 welding, 注塑车间 injection molding, 喷涂车间 painting, 组装车间 assembly, 包装车间 packing. 无尘车间 (wúchén chējiān) is a clean room.

e: travel ticket: a ticket for a bus, train, or coach
d: 车 chē (vehicle; car; train) + 票 piào (slip; ticket). A ticket for ground transport: a bus ticket, a train ticket, a coach ticket. The slip that proves you have paid your fare and may board. By the same pattern, 机票 jīpiào is a plane ticket and 船票 chuánpiào is a boat ticket.

e: carts made to the same track
d: Qin standardized the gauge of cart axles so that all wheeled vehicles fit the same ruts. The empire-wide road system, including the 直道 (zhídào, "straight roads") radiating from the capital Xianyang, depended on this.

车 (chē, vehicle) + 站 (stop): the place where buses or trains halt and passengers board. The base word for any ground-transit station; specify with 火车站 huǒchēzhàn (train station) or 汽车站 qìchēzhàn (bus station).

陈 (chén, to lay out; stale, old , grain stored too long; also the Chen state of the Spring and Autumn period) + 旧 (old). Old in the sense of having overstayed its usefulness: 陈旧的观念 (outdated concepts), 陈旧的设备 (obsolete equipment).
To weigh. 称一下 ("weigh it, please") hands the fruit to the vendor. The same character read chèn means "to fit," as in 称心如意, suiting one's heart's wishes.

Form of address, title, mode of address , the technical term for the entire system of address terms. 亲属称谓 (qīnshǔ chēngwèi) refers specifically to kinship terms. Understanding 称谓 is considered a basic social competency.

What the factory pays, as opposed to 价格 (jiàgé), what you pay. 原材料 (yuáncáiliào, raw materials) and 人工 (réngōng, labour) are the two cost lines you will hear cited when a price goes up. 利润 (lìrùn) is profit.

成 chéng (to accomplish; to become) + 功 gōng (achievement). Literally "to complete the achievement." Both verb (to succeed) and noun (success). One of the most common words in modern Chinese, the natural opposite of 失败 shībai (failure). 成功人士 = a successful person. 取得成功 = to attain success.

e: grades; results; achievement (in study or work)
d: 成 chéng (accomplished; finished) + 绩 jì (achievement; spun work). The measured outcome of effort, most often school marks: 考试成绩 "exam results," 成绩单 "a report card." The finished score that shows how the work turned out.

e: to start a family; to marry and establish a household
d: 成 chéng (to become; to accomplish; to complete) + 家 jiā. The moment a household comes into being, through marriage and setting up a home together. One of the defining life-stage transitions in Chinese culture, paired with 立业 (establish a career) in the famous set phrase 成家立业.

成 chéng (accomplished) + 就 jiù (to attain). The lasting result of effort, the achievement one can point to: 巨大的成就 "a great achievement," 学术成就 "academic accomplishments." Weightier and more public than a single completed task.

成 chéng (fully formed) + 熟 shú (ripe; cooked). Ripe in the literal sense for fruit and crops, and mature in the figurative sense for people, plans, and technologies: 成熟的苹果 "a ripe apple," 想法还不成熟 "the idea is not yet fully developed."

成 chéng (to accomplish; to become; to complete) + 为 wéi (to be; to serve as). The standard verb for transformation into a new state or role. Followed directly by a noun: 成为医生 (to become a doctor), 成为朋友 (to become friends), 成为问题 (to become a problem).

成 chéng (to become; set; established) + 语 yǔ (speech; phrase). Set phrases , the four-character classical idioms that are one of the most distinctive features of Chinese. 成语 are compressed narratives, mostly four characters, encoding a story from history or classical literature.

e: to grow up; to mature; personal development
d: 成 chéng (to become; to complete) + 长 zhǎng (to grow). The compound for the full arc of development: physical, psychological, and social maturation. 成长故事 = coming-of-age story. 成长经历 = formative experiences. Also used for adult development: 这段经历让我很成长 "this experience helped me grow a lot."

e: to admit, to acknowledge, to recognize formally
d: 承 chéng (to bear; to receive; to assume) + 认 rèn. To shoulder the recognition of something , a fact, a fault, a state's legitimacy. Spans personal admission ("I admit I was wrong") and formal recognition (one country recognizing another diplomatically).

e: integrity; honesty and trustworthiness; good faith
d: 诚 chéng (sincerity; genuine; true to one's heart , 诚 is itself 言 + 成 chéng, words that have been completed, words that have come to pass; sincerity as the alignment of word with reality) + 信 xìn (trustworthiness).

城 chéng (wall; fortified place) + 堡 bǎo (fort; stronghold). A castle or fortress, the walled stronghold of a lord. 城堡 is the standard translation for the European castle, and the word most readers meet first in fairy tales and fantasy.

e: the City God — divine magistrate of the underworld
d: 城隍 (lit. "city wall and moat") is the divine magistrate of a city or county, presiding over both the living city and its deceased residents in the underworld. He holds court in his temple (城隍庙 Chénghuáng miào), trying the souls of the recently dead to assign their afterlife fate.

城 chéng (city; wall) + 门 mén (gate; door). The controlled opening in the wall, the single point where the inside and outside of a city legally met. City gates were closed at night, manned by guards, and named individually; a walled capital might have a dozen, each a landmark in its own right.

城 chéng (city; wall) + 墙 qiáng (wall). The original sense of 城 made explicit. Where 城 alone once meant the wall, modern Mandarin pairs it with 墙 to specify the physical structure as opposed to the city it encloses.

城 chéng (walled settlement) + 市 shì (market). The most ordinary modern word for "city," and a fossil of how cities formed: a wall (城) for defense, a market (市) for exchange. The two together make the thing.
城 chéng (city) + 镇 zhèn (town). A collective term spanning the whole range of urban settlement, from large cities down to market towns, used especially in contrast to the countryside (农村 nóngcūn).
吃 (chī, eat) + 饱 (full) as a resultative pair: to eat until satisfied. The negative is 没吃饱 (méi chī bǎo, did not eat enough), and a question often takes 吃饱了吗 (chī bǎo le ma).

e: to be jealous (in love); to eat vinegar
d: 吃 chī + 醋 cù (vinegar). Eating vinegar: romantic jealousy. The origin story: a Tang dynasty concubine had to drink vinegar as punishment when she defied orders, giving rise to this vivid metaphor. Exclusively romantic jealousy (not professional envy, which is 嫉妒 jídù).

e: To eat a meal , literally "eat cooked grain
d: To eat a meal , literally "eat cooked grain." Used as a general term for eating any meal regardless of whether rice is served. 吃 means "to eat"; 饭 means cooked grain or, by extension, any meal.

e: to endure hardship; to eat bitterness
d: 吃 chī (eat) + 苦 kǔ (bitter; hardship). To eat bitterness , to endure difficulty without complaint. One of the most culturally loaded compounds in Chinese. 能吃苦 (able to endure hardship) is a major virtue. 吃苦耐劳 = endure hardship and labor without complaint.

e: to suffer a loss; to be at a disadvantage; to get the short end
d: 吃 chī + 亏 kuī (deficit; shortfall). To eat a shortfall , to come out worse, to be cheated or disadvantaged. 吃亏是福 chī kuī shì fú (suffering loss is a blessing) is a common proverb: the Daoist wisdom that accepting disadvantage builds character.

e: ate; has eaten (the action is complete)
d: The most basic post-verb 了 construction. The 了 immediately follows the verb and signals that the action was completed. With a bare monosyllabic object, the 了 sits between verb and object. With a quantified object, this placement is even clearer and more natural.
Eating people, man-eating , Lu Xun term for the cannibalistic logic he claimed to find underlying Confucian social morality.

就 in habitual statements describes characteristic immediate sequences , what this person always does right after something else. Often used with mild commentary (it might be a bad habit, or an endearing one). The 就 here encodes: no delay at all between finishing dinner and falling asleep.
Named after two old units of length, 尺 and 寸. 外径 (wàijìng) is outer diameter, 内径 (nèijìng) inner diameter, 壁厚 (bìhòu) wall thickness, 高度 height.

赤 chì (red; bare; naked) + 脚. Bare-footed. Famously the term in 赤脚医生 chìjiǎo yīshēng, the "barefoot doctors" of the Mao-era rural healthcare program , village paramedics with minimal training who made primary care available across the countryside.
充 chōng (to fill) + 分 fèn (measure; share). Filled to the proper measure, fully sufficient: 充分的准备 "ample preparation," 充分利用 "to make full use of." Note the fèn reading.

e: substantial; enriched; full (of a life or content)
d: 充 chōng (to fill) + 实 shí (full; substantial). Filled to fullness, with nothing hollow: 生活很充实 "a full, rewarding life." As a verb it means to enrich or strengthen: 充实内容 "to flesh out the content."

充 (chōng, to fill; to be full) + 足 (sufficient). Filled to sufficiency , not merely enough but abundantly enough. 阳光充足 (ample sunlight); 准备充足 (fully prepared); 充足的理由 (compelling reasons). Stronger than 足够 zúgòu (merely enough).

Recognizable by the small patch of white makeup 白粉块 báifěn kuài around the nose -- a marking that immediately signals comic status. The 丑 line includes male 男丑 and female 女丑 (also called 彩旦 cǎidàn, a comic older woman type).

e: to publish; to put out an edition
d: 出 chū (emerge; emit) + 版 bǎn (board; printing plate; edition). To emit a printing plate , to send a text out into the world as a published work. The metaphor is the woodblock or copper plate of traditional printing, the fixed form from which copies emerge.

出 chū (emerge; put out) + 产 chǎn (produce; give birth to; output). To yield products from a source , a region produces goods, a field yields a crop, a factory puts out units. Used for natural resources, agricultural yield, and manufactured goods. As a noun: the output, the produce.

e: to go wrong; to make an error
d: 出 chū (to come out) + 错 cuò (error). For an error to surface, often in a process or system: 系统出错了 "the system threw an error," 计算出错 "a miscalculation came up." Common in technical and procedural contexts.

e: to set out; to depart; to start from (a position or principle)
d: 出 chū (exit; emerge from) + 发 fā (to send out; to dispatch; to start moving). The moment of departure , leaving a point of origin for a destination. Physical: a train, a traveler, a team setting out.

e: to leave home; enter monastic life
to export; an exit; to speak
d: 出 chū (exit; emerge) + 口 kǒu (mouth; opening; port). Three interlocking meanings from the same compound. As trade: to export , goods going out through the port. As architecture: the exit of a building or tunnel. As speech: 出口成章 (words emerge perfectly formed , to speak with eloquence).

The refund of input VAT on exported goods, claimed by whoever exports them. A factory with its own export licence (自营出口 zìyíng chūkǒu) claims it directly; one without exports through a trading company (外贸公司 wàimào gōngsī), which adds a layer of margin.

e: a way out; prospects, future direction
d: 出 chū (to go out, to exit) + 路 lù (road). Literally "the road out." Used for both physical exit (the way out of a building) and, more often, figurative prospects: career options, an escape from a bad situation, the future of an industry. 没有出路 méiyǒu chūlù = no way forward, no prospects.

e: to go out; to leave home; to set off on a trip
d: 出 chū (to exit) + 门 mén (door). To step out the door, whether for the day or for a journey: 我出门了 "I'm heading out." Its opposite is 回家 huí jiā or 进门 jìnmén.

e: to become famous; to make a name for oneself
d: 出 chū (emerge) + 名 míng (name; fame; reputation). To emerge into collective naming , to become the person or thing that others talk about and recognize by name. The 出 marks the transition: previously unknown, now known. 出名 carries no inherent judgment of whether the fame is deserved or welcome.

e: to go out; to head outside
d: 出 chū (to exit; to emerge) + 去 qù (away from here). To exit and move away from the speaker's reference point. Contrast: 出来 chūlái (to come out , exiting toward where the speaker is). 出去 is used by someone inside sending someone outside, or by someone outside talking about leaving an enclosed space.

出 chū (emerge; stand out) + 色 sè (color; appearance; quality). "Emerging in color" , a vivid presence that distinguishes itself against its background. The color metaphor is apt: something outstanding has a quality that registers immediately, the way a saturated color stands out on a pale surface.

e: to enter trance; to be rapt

d: 出 chū (emerge) + 生 shēng (life; to be born; raw). Emergence into life: the original threshold crossing. 出生 is used for persons: 他在北京出生 (he was born in Beijing). The date is 出生日期 chūshēng rìqī (date of birth).

e: a problem occurs; something goes wrong
d: Here 问题 is unambiguously "problem": 出 chū (to emerge, arise) + 问题 = "a problem crops up, something breaks down." Used for malfunctions, complications, and things going wrong. Contrast 解决问题 (solve a problem) and 发现问题 (spot a problem).

e: to appear; to emerge; to come into view
d: 出 chū (emerge) + 现 xiàn (appear; manifest; current). To emerge into visibility , applicable to everything from a rainbow appearing after rain to a new problem appearing in a system. One of the most common verbs in news language and everyday description.

e: out of politeness; for the sake of courtesy
d: 出于 chūyú (proceeding from; out of) + 礼貌. Names the motivation behind a polite-but-not-sincere act: doing something not because you want to but because not doing it would be rude. Useful for marking the gap between social form and personal preference.

e: to stand out from the crowd; exceptional
d: 出 chū (emerge) + 众 zhòng (crowd; the many; multitude). To emerge from the mass of people , to be the one figure that rises above the surrounding level. Often used for talent, appearance, or personal quality that is genuinely rare rather than merely good.
除 chú (except) + 非 fēi (not). Literally "except if not," hence "unless." Often paired with 否则 fǒuzé or 才 cái: 除非下雨，否则我们就去 "we'll go unless it rains."
厨 (chú, cooking, the cook) plus 房. The room where food is prepared. One of the most frequent 房 compounds in daily life, and usually among the first room words a learner needs.

e: to handle; to deal with; to process
d: 处 chǔ (to manage; to dispose of) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). To take a matter in hand and see it through: 处理问题 "to deal with a problem," 处理数据 "to process data."

e: to be in (a state or situation)
to handle; to dispose of; the construction name

d: 川 chuān (Sichuan) + 菜 cài (cuisine). The cooking of Sichuan, famous for the numbing-spicy 麻辣 málà of Sichuan peppercorn and chili. 麻婆豆腐 and 回锅肉 are classic 川菜 dishes.

穿 (to pass through) + 过 (guò, across, a directional complement). The verb of moving through and out the other side, a crowd, a forest, a tunnel. 过 marks the full traverse, in one side and out the far side.

e: to put on (and have it on)
d: 穿 (to thread on) + 上 (shàng, up/onto, here a result complement). The complement 上 marks the garment as now in place. 穿上 stresses the completed act of getting it on, against bare 穿 which can describe the habit of wearing.

穿 (to bore through) + 透 (tòu, thoroughly/through). Two synonyms stacked for force, used for light, sound, water, or radiation breaking all the way through a barrier. The technical word in physics and medicine for penetration.

e: to put on clothes; to dress
d: 穿 (to thread through) + 衣 (yī, clothing). A verb-object pair, the plainest way to say "get dressed." 衣 is the general word for what covers the upper body, so 穿衣 frames dressing as passing the body into a garment.

e: to pass through; to cut across; (popular fiction) to time-travel
d: Cutting through a region. Also the standard verb for popular time-travel fiction (穿越剧, 穿越小说) where a modern character is thrown into a past dynasty.

穿 (to put on clothing) + 着 = the dressed state is in force. This is among the most natural uses of durative 着, because clothing occupies a position continuously. The same pattern applies to 戴着 (wearing a hat/glasses), 拿着 (holding), 带着 (carrying/bringing).

e: to disseminate; to spread; to broadcast; communication
d: 传 chuán (to transmit) + 播 bō (to sow, to broadcast). To spread information, ideas, or culture widely: 传播知识 "to disseminate knowledge," 大众传播 "mass communication." Also the academic field name, 传播学 "communication studies."

e: to convey; to pass on (a message); to communicate
d: 传 chuán (to convey) + 达 dá (to reach, to arrive). To deliver a message, an order, or a feeling so that it reaches its target: 传达指示 "to convey instructions," 传达上级的精神 "to pass on the leadership's intent." Stresses that the content arrives intact.

e: to pass; to relay; to convey; to transmit
d: 传 chuán (to pass on) + 递 dì (to hand over). To move something from one party to the next in a chain: 传递信息 "to relay information," 传递火炬 "to pass the torch." Stresses the act of handing along, often through several hands or steps.

传 zhuàn (a handed-down record) + 记 jì (to record). A written account of a person's life: 名人传记 "celebrity biographies," 人物传记 "biographies of notable figures." Note the reading shifts to zhuàn here, never chuán.

e: to infect; to be contagious; to spread (a disease)
d: 传 chuán (to transmit) + 染 rǎn (to dye, to be tainted). The spread of an illness from one person to another: 传染病 "infectious disease." Figuratively, an emotion or a mood that catches: 他的笑很有传染力 "his laugh is contagious."
传染 (chuánrǎn, to infect, to pass on) + 病: a disease that spreads from one person to another. It is the headline word during any epidemic and the category label on public-health notices.

e: legend; folklore; that which is passed down
d: 传 chuán (to transmit; to pass on) + 说 shuō (speech; to speak; theory). A legend or oral tradition , stories that have been passed down through generations without fixed written form.
传统 (traditional) + 节日 (festival, holiday). The inherited ritual calendar: 春节, 元宵节, 清明节, 端午节, 七夕节, 中元节, 中秋节, 重阳节. These are 传统节日 as opposed to 法定节假日 (statutory public holidays) like National Day.

传统 (tradition) + 文化 (culture). The received deposit of Chinese civilization: classical literature, Confucian ethics, folk festivals, traditional arts and crafts, medicine, cuisine, and everything else that is "Chinese" by inheritance rather than by innovation.

传统 (traditional) + 医学 (medicine). The formal name for the system of Chinese medicine (中医 zhōngyī) as a body of inherited knowledge: acupuncture, herbal medicine, moxibustion, massage (推拿 tuīná), and the diagnostic frameworks of qi, yin-yang, and the five phases.
船 (boat) + 票 (ticket): the fare for a passage by water, parallel to 车票 (bus/train ticket) and 机票 (plane ticket).
船 (boat) + 长 (zhǎng, chief): the head of the ship. The same 长 head-of suffix gives 校长 (principal) and 队长 (team leader).
船 (boat) + 只, here a classifier turned collective suffix. The pair names boats as a category rather than one hull, the way 车辆 names vehicles in bulk. Standard in port notices, news, and maritime law.

e: to start a business; to found a venture; to pioneer
d: 创 chuàng (to create; to initiate) + 业 yè (undertaking). To found something from the ground up, whether a company or a larger enterprise: 自主创业 "to start one's own business," 创业公司 "a startup." Carries the flavor of building where nothing stood before.
吹 (chuī, to blow) + 牛 (ox). From the full phrase 吹牛皮 (chuī niúpí, blow up an ox-hide), once said of herders inflating a hide skin-raft by lung power: big puff, little substance.

e: Spring Equinox — balance of yin and yang
d: 春 chūn (spring) + 分 fēn (to divide; to share equally). The Spring Equinox: the day of perfect balance, when day and night are equal. In traditional cosmology, the moment when yin and yang are in exact equilibrium before yang takes the lead toward summer.

春 (spring) + 风 (fēng, wind). The mild wind of spring, and by extension any warm, reviving influence, a kind teacher, good news, a stroke of fortune. The phrase 春风得意 (chūnfēng déyì) describes riding high on success.

The Lunar New Year (春节 Chūnjié) is the year's most important ritual occasion. Before the family feast on New Year's Eve, offerings of food, incense, and paper money are made to the ancestors (祭祖 jìzǔ). Firecrackers (鞭炮 biānpào) are set off to drive away evil spirits and welcome the new.

Major customs of 春节: 贴春联 paste spring couplets on the door · 放鞭炮 set off firecrackers · 发红包 give red envelopes (现在多用微信红包) · 守岁 stay awake through New Year's Eve · 拜年 pay New Year visits · 吃饺子 eat dumplings (especially in North China, shaped like gold ingots 元宝).

春 (spring) + 天 (tiān, day/season). The everyday word for the season, the one you reach for in conversation. 天 here marks a stretch of time rather than a single day, the same suffix in 夏天 (summer) and 冬天 (winter).

e: it's spring now; spring has arrived (no verb needed)
d: One of the most elegant features of sentence-final 了: it can attach directly to a noun phrase, without any verb, to announce that the situation has become that thing. This works because 了 marks change of state , and "it has become spring" is a state change even with no overt verb present.

e: the feel of spring; signs of spring
d: 春 (spring) + 意 (yì, sense/intent). The atmosphere of spring in the air, the green budding and softening light that signal the season has arrived. 春意盎然 (chūnyì àngrán) describes a scene brimming with spring.
词 cí (word; lyric; multi-character unit) + 典 diǎn (canonical reference). A dictionary organized alphabetically by pinyin or by topic that defines words and phrases rather than individual characters.

词 cí (word) + 句 jù (phrase). Words and phrases taken together, that is, the wording of a text: 推敲词句 "to weigh one's wording carefully." It frames language at the level of phrasing rather than whole sentences.

Tune pattern , the named musical template to which a 词 is written. Specifies the number of lines, the syllable count of each line, the tonal contour, and the rhyme scheme. Several hundred standard tune patterns exist in the classical repertoire.
词 cí (word) + 语 yǔ (speech; phrase). A cover term for words and set phrases together, broader than 单词. Used when talking about vocabulary as a body of expressions.

e: ancestral hall — the lineage's center of gravity
d: The 祠堂 is architecturally distinct from both domestic and religious buildings. Typically facing south, with a courtyard (天井 tiānjǐng), successive halls of increasing sanctity, and a rear hall housing the ranked spirit tablets, the building's layout enacts a cosmological and social hierarchy simultan…

e: to hold compassion in one's heart; compassionate by nature
d: 慈悲 (compassion) + 为 (to be; as) + 怀 (bosom; to hold in the heart). To carry compassion as one's fundamental orientation. Used to characterize people of consistently gentle, merciful temperament , those who reliably respond to others' suffering with care rather than indifference.

慈 (loving-kindness; tenderness) + 母 (mother). A classical compound appearing in the famous poem by Mèng Jiāo (孟郊, 751–814 CE): 慈母手中线，游子身上衣 , "In a loving mother's hands, thread; on a wandering son's body, clothing." 慈 here carries the full weight of gentle, attentive care.

慈 (loving-kindness) + 善 (goodness; virtue). The compound that carried 慈 from the religious register into modern social discourse. 慈善事业 (císhàn shìyè, charitable work), 慈善机构 (císhàn jīgòu, charitable organization), 慈善捐款 (císhàn juānkuǎn, charitable donation) are all standard modern compounds.

e: the heart of deference and yielding — sprout of 礼 ritual propriety
d: 辞让 cí ràng: declining (an honor) and yielding (precedence to another). The capacity to defer , to put another's needs or claim before one's own in appropriate situations. The sprout of 礼 lǐ (ritual propriety).
此 cǐ (this) + 外 wài (outside). A formal written connector, "outside of this," used to add a further point: 此外，还有一点需要注意 "besides, there is one more point to note."

聪 (cōng, sharp-eared; quick-witted , 耳 radical) + 明 (bright, clear-sighted , 日 sun + 月 moon). Intelligence as a compound of keen hearing and clear sight. 聪 alone originally meant "sharp of ear" in classical texts; combined with 明 (bright), it became the standard adjective for intelligence.

e: from then on; henceforth — narrative turning point
d: 从 cóng (from) + 此 cǐ (this; here). 从此 is a narrative marker that signals a permanent change of state after a critical event. Common in stories, histories, and personal narratives: 从此他再也没有回来 "from then on, he never returned." 从此以后 is the fuller form.

e: thereby; thus; and as a result
d: 从 cóng (following from) + 而 ér (and so). A written connective that draws a consequence: the second clause follows as a result of the first. Common in formal and academic prose.

e: always; never (with negation); at all times up to now
d: 从 cóng (from; since) + 来 lái (coming; up to now). "Coming from the past all the way here," from some starting point up to the present moment. Almost always paired with negation: 从来不 (never; has never) / 从来没有 (never; has never happened).

e: once upon a time; formerly; in the old days
d: 从 cóng (from; following) + 前 qián (front; before). "From the front / from the time that was in front": an even more remote and literary sense of "formerly" than 以前.

A fixed frame meaning "starting from now." 从 (from) plus 现在 plus 起 (to start). It marks a turning point or a resolution: 从现在起，我要早睡 ("from now on, I'll go to bed early"). A close variant is 从现在开始, with 开始 (to begin) in place of 起.

Texture stroke technique: the set of specialized brushwork methods used to render the surface of rocks and mountains. Different schools developed different 皴 techniques: axe-cut strokes 斧劈皴, hemp-fiber strokes 披麻皴, Mi dots 米点皴.

e: to miss (a chance, a train, a person)
d: 错 cuò (crosswise) + 过 guò (to pass). To pass by crosswise rather than meet: two things slip past each other and the moment is lost. Used for chances, trains, and people: 错过机会 "to miss a chance," 错过末班车 "to miss the last bus."

错 cuò (wrong) + 误 wù (to err, mistake). Both a noun, the mistake itself, and an adjective, mistaken or incorrect: 犯了一个错误 "made a mistake," 错误的决定 "a wrong decision." The standard, slightly formal word for an error of fact or judgment.

e: a wrongly written character; a typo
d: 错 cuò (wrong) + 字 zì (character). A character written incorrectly, whether mis-formed by hand or mistyped: 这篇作文有很多错字 "this essay has many wrong characters." A 错别字 cuòbiézì folds in 别字, the right-looking but wrong character.

e: to reach; to convey; to attain

d: The Dalai Lama , the title of the head of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism and, historically, the political leader of the Tibetan government. Understood as the successive incarnation of Avalokiteshvara. The current (Fourteenth) Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, has been in exile in India since 1959.
The semi-legendary Indian founder. His defining image: nine years of wall-gazing at Shaolin, his arms falling off from holding them up in meditation (hence the armless Daruma dolls in Japan).
答 dá (to answer) + 题 tí (question). To work through the items on an exam or quiz: 认真答题 "answer the questions carefully." Its mirror is 出题 chūtí, to set the questions.

e: to agree; to promise; to answer (a call)
d: 答 dā (to answer) + 应 yìng (to respond). To answer a request with consent: to agree or promise. Also the literal "to answer" when called: 我叫了半天他都没答应 (I called for ages and he never answered). Note the neutral tone on 应 here.

e: to conquer the realm; to win power through struggle
d: 打 dǎ (to strike; to fight; to build through effort) + 江山 (the realm). Always implies hard-won, usually military achievement , you do not inherit 江山, you take it. The character 打 carries physical force: the same verb used for punching, striking, and waging war.

e: to break with tradition; to challenge convention
d: 打破 (to break, to smash) + 传统 (tradition). The act of violating inherited norms deliberately. In modern usage, 打破传统 can be positive (innovative, forward-thinking) or negative (disrespectful, reckless) depending on context.

e: to get through (a call); to open up (a passage); to clear a blockage
d: 打 dǎ (to make; to strike; to do) + 通 (to get through). A resultative verb: to do something until it is through.
The verb for producing samples before an order. 打样费 (dǎyàngfèi) is the sampling fee, often refunded against the first order; 打样周期 is how long sampling takes.

折 counts tenths of the price you pay, not the amount taken off. 八折 means you pay eight tenths, a 20% discount. Learners hear "eight" and think "80% off." In a negotiation 点 (diǎn, a percentage point) is more common than 折 for small moves.

打 dǎ (to hit; to strike) + 字 zì. You are "striking" the characters into existence: the same 打 used in 打球 (play ball by striking it), 打电话 (make a phone call by striking a connection), 打鼓 (beat a drum).

e: the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sutra; the long form
d: The full Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, translated by Xuanzang in 600 fascicles, makes the Diamond and Heart Sutras look like fragments. The Heart Sutra is in fact a condensation of its core teaching. The long form unpacks emptiness across hundreds of contexts, dialogues, and lists.

e: great loving-kindness, great compassion — the full bodhisattva quality
d: 大 (great) + 慈 (loving-kindness) + 大 (great) + 悲 (compassion). The epithet most closely associated with Guanyin: 大慈大悲观世音菩萨. The reduplication of 大 before each component gives it the character of a liturgical formula.

e: main road; grand way; the broad path
d: 大 dà (big; main; grand) + 道 (way; path). Physically: a wide, main thoroughfare. Philosophically: the grand way of moral order or heaven's intention.

大多数 (the great majority) and 少数 (the few) partition a set by proportion: 大多数人都同意 (most people agree), with the majority phrase taking 都 like any near-universal. 少数 appears in the fixed civic vocabulary 少数民族 (minority nationalities, China's official term for its 55 recognized non-Han groups).

大 dà + 方 fāng (square; proper; generous). Having the big-square manner: poised, natural, generous, not petty. Used for both personality (generous with money) and bearing (natural and composed, not awkward). A high compliment in Chinese social contexts.

大 dà + 夫 fū, but in this sense read dàifu with a neutral tone. A common, slightly informal word for a doctor, especially in northern speech: 看大夫 to see a doctor, 张大夫 Dr. Zhang. Read 大夫 dàfū instead and the same characters name a senior official of the old imperial court, a different word entirely.
大 dà (large, rough) + 概 gài (general outline; to level off). A rough outline: approximately, probably. One of the most natural hedges in spoken Mandarin: 大概三点 "around three o'clock."
