大 (big) + 哥. Literally the eldest brother in the family. By extension it addresses the leader of a group, the boss of a gang, or any older man you want to flatter into helping you.
大哥 (big brother) + 大 again. First a nickname for the 1980s brick mobile phone, the status symbol of bosses; by extension the kingpin or undisputed number one in any field.
大 dà (big) + 海 hǎi (sea). The everyday word for the sea as a whole, the vast expanse of salt water. 大海捞针 "to fish a needle from the sea" is the Chinese "needle in a haystack."

Floor slang for the main order as opposed to samples. 大货生产 is bulk production, 大货样 a unit pulled from it. The word appears in nearly every merchandiser message: 大货已经上线了 means your order is on the line.

大 dà (big) + 家 jiā (family; home). Literally "the big family," used for "everyone present" or "all of us." Much warmer and more conversational than 人们. The go-to word for addressing or including a present group: 大家好！(Hello everyone!).

e: the Dajia Pilgrimage — one of the world's largest religious events
d: The annual Dajia Mazu Pilgrimage (大甲妈祖绕境进香) is a nine-day, eight-night procession covering approximately 340 kilometers through central and southern Taiwan, beginning from the Zhenglong Temple (镇澜宫 Zhènlán Gōng) in Dajia, Taichung.
大 (big) + 街 (street). A broad, busy thoroughfare, the high street of a town. Pairs with 小巷 (xiǎoxiàng, narrow lane) in the set phrase 大街小巷, meaning every street and alley.
大 (big) plus 姐 marks the eldest of several sisters at home. On the street it doubles as a friendly, respectful way to address a woman somewhat older than the speaker.

e: a large amount: a great quantity of
d: 大 dà (big) + 量 liàng (amount). Functions as a quantifier before mass and plural nouns: 大量资金 (a large amount of capital), 大量时间 (a great deal of time), 大量生产 (to mass-produce).
Big sound. Used adverbially before the verb: 大声说 (speak up), 大声朗读 (read aloud). Its opposite 小声 keeps the peace: 请小声一点，孩子睡了。Quiet please, the child is asleep.
大使 dàshǐ (ambassador, lit. great envoy) + 馆. The ambassador's official house abroad. A smaller mission led by a consul is a 领事馆 lǐngshìguǎn, a consulate.

e: great knight-errant; heroic wanderer; the wuxia protagonist archetype
d: 大 dà (great) + 侠 xiá (chivalrous fighter; knight-errant). The archetypal wuxia protagonist: skilled, wandering, honorable, righting wrongs without official sanction. The 大侠 has no fixed home , the entire 江湖 is their domain.

Big-small: the size scale, the template for the whole antonym-compound family. 这双鞋大小正好 means the shoes fit exactly. Its siblings 长短 (length), 轻重 (weight), and 高矮 (height) work identically, and 轻重 doubles as "relative importance," what a tactless person 不知轻重 fails to weigh.

e: university; college — and the Confucian Great Learning
d: 大 dà (great; large) + 学 xué (learning). The modern term for university. But 大学 is also the title of one of the Four Books of Confucianism (四书 Sìshū) , the 大学 (Great Learning), a short text that outlines the program of self-cultivation leading from individual virtue to social order to universal peace…

e: Great Learning · Doctrine of the Mean
d: Originally chapters of the 礼记, elevated to independent classic status by Zhu Xi. 大学 Dàxué outlines the nested self-cultivation program (修身齐家治国平天下).

e: the greater cause; moral principle; overriding righteousness
d: 大 dà (great; large) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral duty). The righteousness that supersedes personal ties, individual interest, or clan loyalty. 大义灭亲 dàyì mièqīn = to put righteousness above family (a set phrase for reporting or condemning a family member for the sake of the greater moral order).

e: to be greater than; larger than
d: 大 dà (big) + 于 yú (than). The comparison frame "greater than," standard in maths and formal description: 收入大于支出 "income exceeds expenditure." Its mirror is 小于 xiǎoyú (less than).
Greater Seal Script , the broad category encompassing the varied script forms of the Zhou dynasty bronze inscriptions, Stone Drum text, and oracle bone script.

e: to handle on behalf of; to do for another
d: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 办 bàn (to handle; to manage). To take care of a task or piece of business in someone else's stead: 代办手续 "to handle the formalities for someone," 代办签证 "to arrange a visa on another's behalf." The errand done in your name.

e: to represent; a representative; to stand for
d: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 表 biǎo (to express; outward). As a verb, to represent or stand for: 红色代表喜庆 "red stands for celebration." As a noun, the person who represents others: 班代表 "class representative," 人民代表 "people's deputy."

e: to buy on behalf of; a purchasing proxy
d: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 购 gòu (to purchase). To buy something for another person, often goods from abroad: 海外代购 "overseas purchasing proxy." A familiar modern word from the rise of cross-border shopping, where one traveler buys for many at home.

e: price paid, cost (in effort or loss)
d: 代 (to stand in for, substitute) + 价 (price). The cost something exacts, not in money but in effort, sacrifice, or loss. You pay a 代价 for a mistake, a victory, or a hard choice.

e: to act as agent; acting (in a post); agency
d: 代 dài (on behalf of) + 理 lǐ (to manage). To handle affairs in an official capacity for someone else: 代理人 "an agent," 代理商 "a distributor," 代理校长 "acting principal." As a modifier it marks a temporary or proxy holder of a post.

e: to replace; to substitute for; in place of
d: 代 dài (to stand in for) + 替 tì (to replace). The general verb for one thing or person taking another's place: 用机器代替人工 "to replace manual labor with machines." Often follows the pattern A 代替 B, "A in place of B."

e: to neglect; to slight a guest through inattention
d: 怠 dài (lazy, inattentive, slack) + 慢 màn (slow). To fail to attend to someone with the care and promptness they deserve. The standard word for hosting someone poorly or neglecting a guest's needs. Often appears in apologies: 怠慢了您, please forgive my poor hospitality.

e: the elixir field — the body's energy center
d: 丹 dān (cinnabar; red; elixir) + 田 tián (field). The "elixir field," the body's primary energy reservoir. Three locations: 下丹田 xià dāntián (lower, 3 inches below the navel, the primary center and focus of most practice) · 中丹田 zhōng dāntián (middle, the chest) · 上丹田 shàng dāntián (upper, the head).

e: a single word; a vocabulary word
d: 单 dān (single) + 词 cí (word). One word taken on its own, the unit you memorize when studying a language. Common in 背单词 bèi dāncí, to memorize vocabulary.
The price per piece; 总价 (zǒngjià) is the total, 金额 (jīn'é) the amount on a line. The usual follow-up is what the unit price includes: 包括 (bāokuò) and 不包括 are the words to listen for.
单身 dānshēn (single, unmarried) + 汉 hàn (man). An unmarried man living on his own. The 汉 here is purely the colloquial "man," with none of the heroic ring of 好汉.

e: to take on; to shoulder (responsibility); accountability
d: 担 dān (to carry) + 当 dāng (to take up a role). To take responsibility upon oneself; as a noun, the quality of being willing to do so. 有担当 yǒu dāndāng describes a person who steps up rather than dodging.

e: to worry; to be concerned about
d: 担 dān (to carry on a shoulder pole; to bear a load) + 心 xīn (heart). Lit. "to carry the weight of the heart." Worry as a physical burden: the heart becomes heavy, something you haul around all day. One of the most common emotional verbs in everyday Mandarin.

h: 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟
p: Dàn yuàn rén cháng jiǔ, qiānlǐ gòng chánjuān
e: Su Shi · 水调歌头 · Mid-Autumn 1076
d: May people live long; across a thousand li, may we share this moon's beauty together. Written in 1076, when Su Shi had not seen his brother Su Zhe for seven years. 婵娟 (chánjuān) was a classical term for the beautiful full moon.

弹 tán (to spring, to bounce) + 性 xìng (property). The quality of stretching and springing back, literal in materials and figurative in arrangements: 弹性材料 "an elastic material," 弹性工作时间 "flexible working hours." Names a built-in capacity to flex without breaking.
蛋 (egg) + 白 (bái, white): literally the white of the egg. In science it extends to protein in general, and 蛋白质 (dànbáizhì) is the standard word for dietary protein.
蛋 (egg) + 糕 (gāo, a steamed or baked flour cake): a cake gets its name from the eggs whipped into the batter. The word covers birthday cakes, sponge cakes, and the slice you buy at a café.
蛋 (egg) + 黄 (huáng, yellow): the yolk. It pairs neatly with 蛋白, the two halves of every egg named by their color. Salted yolk, 咸蛋黄 (xián dànhuáng), is a prized flavor in mooncakes and pastries.

e: local; of the place in question
d: 当 dāng (right at) + 地 dì (place). "Of the very place" you are speaking about: 当地人 dāngdì rén (locals), 当地政府 dāngdì zhèngfǔ (the local government). The spatial twin of 当时.

e: face to face; to one's face; in person
d: 当 dāng (right at) + 面 miàn (face). To do something in someone's presence rather than behind their back: 当面说清楚 (sort it out face to face). Carries a note of directness and accountability.
当 dāng (ought, fitting) + 然 rán (so). "As it should be," and so "of course." Stands alone as a full answer (当然！"of course!") or leads a clause: 当然可以 "certainly you may."

e: at that time; then; at the time in question
d: 当 dāng (right at) + 时 shí (time). Points back to a specific past moment and the state of things in it: "at the time." Often paired with a later contrast, as in "back then I did not understand, but now I do."

e: at this moment; right now; the present
d: 当 dāng (at; facing; this very) + 下 xià (this point in the downward flow of time). The present moment , the point where time has currently descended to. 当下 has a slightly elevated, philosophical register compared to 现在 (now), and appears frequently in Buddhist and reflective contexts.

e: to take seriously; to take literally
d: 当 dāng/dàng (to treat as; regard as) + 真. To treat as real. Often used in the negative: 别当真 bié dàngzhēn "don't take it seriously," "I was just kidding."

e: In public; in front of everyone (lit
d: In public; in front of everyone (lit. "at the mass"). The adverb that transforms many face-related situations. 当众批评 (dāngzhòng pīpíng, to criticize publicly) and 当众表扬 (dāngzhòng biǎoyáng, to praise publicly) are qualitatively different from the same acts done privately.

e: to treat as; to regard as; to take for
d: 当 dàng (to equate) + 作 zuò (to make, to do). To regard X as Y: 把困难当作机会 (treat difficulty as opportunity). A near-synonym is 当成 dàngchéng. Note the falling tone, which marks it apart from level-tone dāng.

e: to make trouble, to be naughty
everywhere; all over; in every place
d: 到 dào (arrive at) + 处 chù (place; location). Arriving at every place: ubiquity, pervasiveness. 到处都是 (there are ... everywhere) is one of the most common constructions. 到处找 (to look everywhere) = searching that has spread to every location.

到 dào (arrive) + 达 dá (reach; attain). Both components mean roughly the same thing, making 到达 more emphatic and formal than 到 alone. Standard in written Chinese for scheduled arrivals: planes, trains, deliveries, expeditions. Spoken Chinese usually just says 到.

e: after all; in the end; (interrogative intensifier)
d: 到 dào (arrive at) + 底 dǐ (bottom; base). Arriving at the bottom: getting to the root of the matter, reaching the real answer. In interrogative sentences, 到底 intensifies the question and demands a genuine response , it presses the interlocutor to stop evading and give a straight answer.

到 dào (arrive) + 来 lái (come). A literary and slightly elevated compound used for the arrival of things rather than people in motion: the advent of spring, the arrival of a new era, the coming of opportunity. Found in formal prose and news writing more than casual speech.

"Up to the present," used to measure a stretch reaching the present moment, often with 还 (still) or 都 to stress that something has or has not happened by now: 到现在他还没来 ("he still hasn't come, even now"). The fuller form 到现在为止 ("up to now") adds 为止 ("as the limit").

e: it would actually be better to (colloquial)
moral outlook; values framework; one's view of what is right and wrong
d: 道德 (morality) + 观 guān (view; perspective; lens through which one sees things , the same 观 in 世界观 worldview, 价值观 value system, 人生观 life philosophy).

e: the truth of the path — the Noble Eightfold Path
d: 道 dào = way, path. Sanskrit magga. The prescription: the 八正道 bā zhèng dào (Noble Eightfold Path): right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.

e: the Way models nature; the Way follows its own spontaneous pattern
d: 道 (the Way) + 法 (to model; to follow as a pattern) + 自然 (self-thus; spontaneous; natural). The culminating principle of Daodejing chapter 25. The Way does not follow anything outside itself , its law is its own spontaneous nature.

e: a Daoist temple; a Daoist monastery
d: 道 dào (the Way; Daoism) + 观 guàn (temple). The temple of a Daoist community, where 观 takes its fourth-tone reading. Set against the Buddhist 寺 sì (monastery) and the general 庙 miào (shrine).

e: Daoism — the way of naturalness and non-action
d: The Daodejing 道德经 (attributed to Laozi, c. 4th–3rd century BCE) and Zhuangzi 庄子. Central concept: 无为 wú wéi, effortless action aligned with the natural order. The sage ruler governs so lightly that the people believe they govern themselves.

e: reason; logic; principle; the way things work
d: 道 dào (way; path) + 理 lǐ (principle; pattern; grain of wood, the inherent structure of things). "The logic of the path." The way things make sense: the reason behind an argument, the principle underlying a situation, the basic logic that should govern behavior.

道 dào (way; path) + 路 lù (road; route). The most standard, neutral word for a road or path. Used freely in both spatial and metaphorical senses. 人生道路 (the road of life) is one of the most common metaphorical applications, at home in political speeches and personal memoirs alike.

e: moral duty; principle of right conduct; the Way and righteousness
d: 道 dào (the Way; the correct path; principle) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral duty). The pairing of the Way as principle and righteousness as conduct , what a person owes to the moral order. 道义上的责任 dàoyì shàng de zérèn = moral responsibility (as opposed to legal obligation).
稻 dào (rice plant) + 草 cǎo (straw). The dried stalks left after rice is harvested, used for thatch, rope, and scarecrows. 最后一根稻草 "the last straw," the final small thing that breaks a back.

e: Arrival of qi, the sensation confirming correct needling
d: Arrival of qi, the sensation confirming correct needling: heaviness, distension, or a spreading warmth at the needled point. Classical and modern acupuncturists both treat déqì as the essential marker of effective treatment.

To acquire guilt before someone: the verb of social danger. The folk warning 宁得罪君子，不得罪小人 advises that a crossed gentleman forgives and a crossed petty man files it away, which is the whole word-field in one proverb.
德 (phonetic transcription of "Deutsch") + 国 guó (country). 德 is the standard phonetic carrier for "Deutsch" in country and language names: 德国 Germany, 德语 German language, 德文 German script.

e: virtuous conduct; moral behavior; virtue as it shows in action
d: 德 dé (virtue; inner moral power) + 行 xíng (conduct; to walk; action). How virtue manifests in behavior , not the inner quality alone but the visible expression of it in how a person moves through the world. 德行 presupposes that genuine virtue is always legible: it shows.

e: Kṣitigarbha — guardian of hell and savior of the dead
d: Sanskrit Kṣitigarbha ("Earth Womb/Treasury"). The bodhisattva who specifically vowed to save beings in hell realms and not enter nirvāṇa until all hells are empty. Associated with Mount Jiuhua 九华山 in Anhui. His vow: 地狱不空，誓不成佛 (If the hells are not empty, I vow not to become a Buddha).
地 dì (ground) + 点 diǎn (point). A specific point on the ground, the precise spot where something happens: a meeting place, an event venue, the scene of an incident. More exact than 地方 dìfang.
When the focused element is a place, the construction answers "where?" — again, about a past event both speakers know happened. The place phrase typically includes 在 and appears immediately after 是.

地 dì (earth; ground) + 方 fang. The all-purpose word for "place," from a physical spot to an abstract point in an argument (这个地方我不同意 "on this point I disagree"). With full tone, 地方 dìfāng means "local" as opposed to "central": 地方政府 local government.

e: the underworld; the realm of the dead
d: 地 (earth; ground) + 府 (government office; official residence). The underground realm of the dead, governed by 阎王 Yánwáng (Yama, the king of the underworld) and his bureaucracy.

地 dì (earth; ground) + 雷 léi (thunder). Landmine , an explosive buried in the ground that detonates on contact. The compound is viscerally accurate: a mine hidden in the earth that erupts like thunder when triggered.

地 dì (earth) + 球 qiú (ball; sphere). Lit. "earth ball." The modern scientific term for the planet , a coinage that dates to the late 19th century, when Chinese translators had to name the heliocentric model.

地 dì (earth; ground) + 图 tú (diagram; picture; plan). Lit. "earth diagram." A transparent compound , the earth drawn out as a picture. 地图 is the standard word for any kind of map, from a hand-drawn sketch to a satellite navigation app.

e: underground; beneath the earth; covert; subterranean
d: 地 dì (earth; ground) + 下 xià (below; under). Literally: beneath the earth. Extended to mean "covert" or "underground" in the political sense , 地下组织 (underground organization), 地下工作 (underground/clandestine work). 地铁 dìtiě (subway; underground railway , lit. "underground iron") uses the same 地.

e: terrain; topography; the shape of the land
d: 地 dì (ground; land) + 形 xíng. The shape of the land: terrain, topography, the rise and fall of the ground. 地形复杂 = the terrain is complex; 地形图 = a topographic map. The most literal of the situation-words, where the shape being read is the physical landscape itself.

e: the hell realm; the path of extreme suffering
d: The lowest of the six realms: extreme suffering as the karmic consequence of severe negative actions , violence, cruelty, deliberate harm.
灯 (lamp) + 光 (guāng, light, glow): the light a lamp throws, the lighting of a room or stage. Where 灯 is the object, 灯光 is the glow itself.
灯 (lamp) + 火 (huǒ, fire): the massed lights of a town or harbor seen at night, often in the literary phrase 灯火通明 (dēnghuǒ tōngmíng), brilliantly lit.
灯 (lamp) + 笼 (lóng, cage, basket): a flame or bulb held inside a frame of paper or silk. The red 灯笼 hung at the New Year and the Lantern Festival is its most familiar form.

e: to climb to high ground; to ascend
d: 登 dēng (to climb; to ascend; to mount) + 高 gāo (high; tall; elevated). The defining physical act of the festival. As a compound, 登高 appears broadly in Chinese outside the festival context , it can describe any ascent, or metaphorically, advancing in rank or achievement.
等 děng (to wait) + 候 hòu (to await). A more formal, written-leaning word for waiting than plain 等. Common on signs and announcements: 请耐心等候 "please wait patiently."

e: to equal; to be equivalent to; to amount to
d: 等 děng (equal) + 于 yú. States equality, literal or figurative: 二加二等于四 "two plus two equals four," 不说话等于同意 "saying nothing amounts to agreeing."

e: low and short; squat; close to the ground
d: 低 (low) + 矮 (short, of stature or height). Used for structures rather than people: low-ceilinged rooms, squat walls, single-story buildings hugging the ground. 低矮的平房 (low-slung single-story houses) is a recurring image in descriptions of older hutong neighborhoods or rural architecture.

e: low and deep (of sound); somber; heavy; low-spirited
d: 低 (low) + 沉 (to sink, heavy, deep). The compound sits at the intersection of acoustic and emotional: a 低沉的声音 is a deep, resonant voice that seems to come from somewhere down in the chest; a 低沉的心情 is a mood that has sunk below normal , subdued, heavy, not quite depressed but nowhere near cheerful.

e: low place; lower ground; a lower spot
d: 低 (low) + 处 (place, location). A low-lying spot or lower area. Practical and descriptive in geography, architecture, and flood-risk contexts: 低处积水 (water pooling in low-lying areas) is a standard phrase in weather reports.

e: low-key; understated; keeping a low profile
d: 低 (low) + 调 (key, register, tone , musical or social). Originally the low musical key; now the social posture of deliberate understatement. 低调做人 (carry yourself with a low profile) and 低调行事 (act without fanfare) are standard phrases in professional and political discourse.

低 (low) + 级 (grade, level, rank). At the lower end of a scale , which in practice means either genuinely entry-level (低级职员, junior staff; 低级别, low rank) or, more pejoratively, crude or vulgar in taste and behavior: 低级趣味 (vulgar tastes), 低级错误 (dī jí cuòwù, a basic mistake , the kind you shouldn't mak…

e: low; down; dispirited; fallen in spirit
d: 低 (low) + 落 (to fall, to drop, to settle down). Mood or morale that has fallen and settled at a low point. 情绪低落 (qíngxù dīluò, spirits low) is the standard phrase for feeling deflated, discouraged, or quietly unhappy without necessarily being in crisis.

e: one rank below others; to consider oneself inferior
d: 低 (lower) + 人 (person, others) + 一等 (one grade, one rank). To be placed one step below others in status , or to place oneself there through shame or social conditioning.

e: in a low voice; softly; in a whisper
d: 低 (low) + 声 (sound, voice). Speaking quietly, in a lowered voice. Appears as an adverb (低声说 , to say in a low voice) or a verb complement.

e: to lower one's head; to bow; to yield
d: 低 (low, lower) + 头 (head). The single most loaded compound on this page. Physically, it is simply to look down , at a phone, at work, at the ground while walking.

低 (low) + 音 (sound, musical tone). The low end of the pitch spectrum , the bass register in music, the bottom frequencies in acoustics. 低音炮 (dīyīn pào, "bass cannon") is the colloquial term for a subwoofer. 低音提琴 (dīyīn tíqín) is the double bass. In vocal music, 低音歌手 is a bass singer.

The main ride app, also usable inside Alipay and WeChat. Industrial zones have confusing addresses, so ask the factory to send a 定位 (dìngwèi, location pin) and set that as the destination. 上车点 (shàngchēdiǎn) is the pickup point.
弟 dì (younger brother) + 子 zǐ. The pupil who studies under a teacher and carries the lineage forward, used of philosophical, martial, and religious schools alike.
第 dì (ordinal) + 二 èr (two). The ordinal "second." The same pattern extends without limit: 第三 third, 第四 fourth, 第十 tenth. The number after 第 is just the ordinary cardinal, unchanged.

e: which (in order); what number in a series
d: 第 dì (ordinal) + 几 jǐ (how many; which). The question form that asks for a position rather than a quantity. The expected answer is always another 第 form: 第三 (the third), 第七 (the seventh).

第 dì (ordinal) + 一 yī (one). The ordinal "first." Note the live tone-sandhi: 一 yī shifts to second tone before a fourth-tone syllable, so it is read dì-yí in 第一个 but stays dì-yī before a pause or another tone.
第一 dì-yī (first) + 流 liú (stream; class). Of the highest grade or quality: 第一流的大学 "a first-rate university." A close synonym of 一流 yīliú, with 第 adding a touch of formality.

e: to overturn heaven and earth; to turn everything upside down; to invert the natural order
d: 颠倒 diāndǎo (to invert; to turn upside down; to have things reversed from their proper state). When the natural or moral order is inverted , the corrupt elevated, the worthy suppressed, right made to appear as wrong. Carries strong negative charge: something fundamental has been wrongly reversed.
点 diǎn (to choose; to dot) + 菜 cài (dish). To pick dishes off a menu and order them. The host usually does the 点菜 for the table. For the many senses of 点 see the 点 entry.

e: to ignite; to light a fire

d: 点 diǎn (to touch lightly, to dip) + 头 tóu (head). To dip the head: to nod in agreement or greeting. 点头同意 "to nod in assent." Its opposite gesture is 摇头 yáotóu, to shake the head.

Dim sum: small Cantonese dishes served with tea in the teahouse tradition. The term literally means "touch the heart." Dim sum culture grew from the Cantonese tea-drinking and commercial meeting tradition of Guangdong and Hong Kong and is now the most internationally recognized format of Chinese com…
To like (a post): tap-approve. 赞 alone means to praise; 点赞之交 ("a likes-only friendship") names the acquaintance you never see but always like.
电 (diàn, electric) + 灯 (lamp): the everyday electric light or bulb. The default ceiling and desk light in a modern home, as opposed to candle or oil flame.
电 diàn (electric) + 话 huà (speech). Speech carried on electricity, the telephone, and by extension the call itself: 打电话 dǎ diànhuà "to make a phone call," 接电话 "to answer the phone."
"Electric remittance," usually just called T/T. 信用证 (xìnyòngzhèng) is a letter of credit (L/C), slower and more paperwork, with the bank standing between the parties.
Computer: electric brain. 台式电脑 is a desktop, 笔记本 a laptop. The formal 计算机 persists in degree names and government documents.

电 diàn (electric) + 影 yǐng (shadow; reflection; image). Film, movie , named for the projected shadows of early cinema. 看电影 = to watch a film. 电影院 = cinema. 电影节 = film festival (Cannes 戛纳电影节, Venice 威尼斯电影节, Berlin 柏林电影节, Hong Kong 香港电影节).

e: movie ticket: a ticket for a film screening
d: 电影 diànyǐng (film; movie) + 票 piào (ticket). A cinema ticket. The 票 here pulls double duty: it admits you to the hall and assigns you a seat. The takings a film earns at the box office are its 票房 piàofáng, literally the ticket room, the modern measure of a movie's success.

电 diàn (electric) + 子 zǐ (small particle; child). As a physics term: the electron. As a prefix: electronic, digital. 电子产品 = electronics (products). 电子书 = e-book. 电子商务 = e-commerce (also shortened to 电商 diànshāng). 电子政务 = e-government. 电子竞技 = esports (also 电竞 diànjìng).

调 diào (to direct, to send out) + 查 chá (to check, to examine). To look into a matter systematically, whether a police inquiry or a market survey. 市场调查 (market survey), 调查结果 (the findings of an investigation). Both verb and noun.

e: to transfer; to mobilize; to arouse
d: 调 diào (to transfer) + 动 dòng (to move). To move a person to a new post, or to mobilize forces and feelings. 调动工作 (transfer to a new job), 调动积极性 (arouse enthusiasm). The sense is of marshalling people or energy toward a purpose.

e: to dispatch; to schedule; a dispatcher
d: 调 diào (to move, to transfer) + 度 dù (to measure, to manage). To dispatch and coordinate trains, vehicles, crews, or tasks; also the person who does it. 列车调度 (train dispatching), 调度中心 (control center). The work of directing many moving parts.

e: to regulate; to adjust; to balance
d: 调 tiáo (to adjust) + 节 jié (to control, to moderate). To keep a level or rhythm steady: 调节温度 (regulate the temperature), 空调 (air conditioning, literally "air regulator"), 自我调节 (self-regulation). The sense is ongoing balance rather than a single change.

调 tiáo (to harmonize) + 解 jiě (to resolve, to untie). To step between two sides and settle their dispute. 调解纠纷 (mediate a dispute), 调解员 (a mediator). The social form of tiáo: bringing people, not flavors, into accord.

调 tiáo (to blend) + 味 wèi (flavor, taste). To season food, to bring its flavors into balance. The seasoning itself is 调料 tiáoliào or 调味品 tiáowèipǐn. The kitchen sense of tiáo: mixing tastes until they are right.

调 tiáo (to adjust) + 整 zhěng (to put in order). To set something right by careful change: 调整计划 (adjust the plan), 调整心态 (adjust one's attitude), 价格调整 (a price adjustment). The everyday word for fine-tuning anything.

e: tune; melody; tone (of voice or mood)
d: 调 diào (melody, pitch) + 子 zi (noun suffix). A tune or melody, and figuratively the pitch or mood of speech or writing. 唱调子 (carry a tune), 定调子 (set the tone, decide the direction). The everyday word for the shape of a sound.

e: to plummet; to tumble down sharply
d: 跌 diē (to stumble, to fall sharply) + 落 luò. A more violent or dramatic fall than 落 alone , prices plummeting, a person tumbling. Common in financial and news contexts.

e: to lose moral face; to be shamed; disgraceful
d: More severe than 丢面子. 丢脸 involves an element of moral failure , betrayal, cheating, acting in ways that contradict one's stated principles. Can affect not just the individual but their family and group. The scope is broader and the damage more lasting than simple social embarrassment.

e: to lose face; to be publicly embarrassed
d: 丢 diū (to lose; to throw away , the losing of something you once had). To lose face is not merely to feel embarrassed privately; it is to have one's standing visibly diminished in the eyes of others. The public, witnessed nature of face-loss is what makes it significant.

东 (east) + 北 (north). In Chinese geography, 东北 almost always means Northeast China , the three provinces of Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang, corresponding roughly to historical Manchuria (满洲 Mǎnzhōu).

e: host (of a banquet, event, or country)
d: 东 (east) + 道 (road; way) + 主 (master, host). From the Zuǒzhuàn (5th century BCE): the state of Zhèng, lying east of the Qin army's road, offered to supply and host the Qin troops. "East-road-master" became the word for host.

东 dōng (east) + 方 fāng (direction). The eastern direction, and by extension "the East" as a cultural sphere. Its pair is 西方 xīfāng, the West. The four directions all take 方: 南方 the south, 北方 the north.

e: Winter Solstice — the turning of yin into yang
d: Winter Solstice, the most important of the twenty-four solar terms, celebrated as a major festival throughout Chinese history. Marks the shortest day and the nadir of the yin/yang cycle, from which point yang begins its return. Dumplings are eaten in the north; tangyuan in the south.
懂 (understand) plus the resultative 得 (de). It reaches past facts toward practical wisdom: knowing how to do a thing, or appreciating its value.
懂 (understand) plus 事 (shì, affairs, the way things work). Said of a child or young person who grasps how to behave, reads a room, and considers others. High praise from a parent.
懂 (understand) plus 行 (háng, a trade or line of work). To be expert in a field, to know its ins and outs as an insider rather than an outsider.
动 dòng (move; act) + 词 cí (word). The "moving-word," a verb: a word for an action or state. 吃, 走, and 喜欢 are all 动词.

过 marks that the subject has undergone the experience at least once, at some indefinite point. 我去过中国 (I have been to China) says nothing about when; it registers the experience itself. Contrast 我去了中国, a specific completed trip. Negation keeps 过 but uses 没: 我没去过中国 (I have never been to China).

e: completed action, the closest thing to a past tense
d: 了 after the verb marks the action as completed. With a past time word it produces what English renders as simple past: 我昨天买了一本书 (I bought a book yesterday). But 了 marks completion, not pastness: 明天吃了饭再走 (leave tomorrow after finishing dinner) puts 了 in a future clause.

e: verb + 一下 — do briefly / casually
d: Placed right after the verb, 一下 makes the action quick, light, and informal: 看一下 ("have a look"), 想一下 ("think for a sec"), 试一下 ("give it a go"). It softens commands into friendly requests and lowers the stakes of an action.

e: sustained state: the door stands open
d: 着 marks a state that holds: 门开着 (the door is open), 墙上挂着一幅画 (a painting hangs on the wall), 他穿着一件红衣服 (he's wearing a red shirt). Where 在 tracks an activity unfolding, 着 freezes the result and holds it. The contrast is sharpest with verbs like 穿: 他在穿衣服 (he is putting clothes on) vs.

e: moving qigong; forms with coordinated movement and breath
d: 动 dòng (moving; active) + 功 gōng (practice). Qigong with movement, from slow and gentle forms like 八段锦 Bāduànjǐn (Eight Brocades) and 五禽戏 Wǔqínxì (Five Animals) to more vigorous practices. Movement is synchronized with breath and guided by awareness.

动 dòng (to move) + 力 lì (force). The force that drives motion. Literal in machines, where it names motive power, and figurative in people, where it names the motivation that keeps one moving toward a goal.

e: to get riled up; to let anger stir (colloquial)
d: 动 dòng (to move; to stir) + 气 qì. For qi to be "moved," to let irritation become active anger. Often used in negative advice: 别动气 "don't get worked up." The qi-as-fluid logic is explicit: something causes the qi to shift and agitate.
动 dòng (to move) + 物 wù (thing). The "moving things," the animals, set against 植物 the "planted things," the plants. 动物园 dòngwùyuán is the zoo, the "animal garden."

e: movement; action; gesture; motion (of the body)
d: 动 dòng (to move) + 作 zuò (to do; to make). A single physical movement or gesture: 这个动作很难 "this move is hard," 动作快一点 "move faster." Also "action" in film: 动作片 dòngzuòpiàn (action movie).

e: 都: every member of a group — simultaneous coverage
d: 都 applies a single predicate to all members of a group at the same time. The group is fixed; 都 says no member is excluded from the statement. Works with pronouns (我们, 他们, 大家), explicit quantifier phrases (三个人, 所有人), and fronted question words (什么, 谁, 哪儿).

Dujiangyan , the 3rd-century BCE irrigation system on the Minjiang River, still operational. 都 refers to the capital; 江 is river; 堰 (yàn) means weir or low dam. The system controls water through geometry rather than barriers, making it the oldest functioning hydraulic infrastructure in the world.

The dutar (都塔尔 dūtǎ'ěr, from Persian do-tar meaning "two strings") is the emblematic instrument of Uyghur music: a long-necked lute with two strings, pear-shaped body, and a thin, resonant tonal quality with long-sustained notes.

e: broad bean chili paste; Pixian paste
d: Pixian fermented broad-bean-and-chili paste , the foundational flavoring of Sichuan cooking. Produced in Pixian County outside Chengdu by fermenting broad beans and chilies for months to years. Almost every Sichuan dish begins by frying doubanjiang in oil until the red oil (红油 hóng yóu) releases.

e: tofu — a cross-cuisine staple appearing in nearly every regional school
tofu pudding; soft tofu in brine

d: Toxicity, one of the key properties documented for each drug in the Bencao Gangmu. Li distinguished between non-toxic (无毒), slightly toxic (小毒), moderately toxic (有毒), and highly toxic (大毒) substances, with corresponding cautions about dosage, preparation, and contraindications.

Only child (lit. "alone-born child-female" , zǐnǚ covers both sexes). The defining identity category for the urban Chinese generation born 1980–2015 under the one-child policy. 独生子 (dúshēng zǐ) is a son; 独生女 (dúshēng nǚ) is a daughter.

读 dú + 懂 dǒng (to understand). A resultative compound: read-to-the-point-of-understanding. Used both literally (read a difficult text and grasp it) and metaphorically (read a person and truly know them).

e: to read; to study; to attend school
d: 读 dú + 书 shū (book). Three overlapping senses: (1) the literal act of reading, (2) studying for school or self-improvement, (3) attending an educational institution. 他在北京大学读书 "He's a student at Peking University." Closer to "to be in school" than English "to read books" suggests.

读 dú + 音 yīn (sound). Literally "the read-sound" , the conventional pronunciation of a written character. The standard reference in dictionaries: 这个字的读音是 zhège zì de dúyīn shì… "the pronunciation of this character is…"
读 dú + 者 zhě (one-who). The standard term for the reader of a book, magazine, or newspaper. 亲爱的读者 "Dear reader" is the conventional opening for a letter from the editor.

e: to block; to stop up; congested
measures of length, capacity, and weight
d: Qin issued empire-standard weights and measures, with bronze and iron reference units distributed to local administrators. Surviving Qin weights are stamped with the imperial decree authorizing them. Tax assessment, grain storage, and commercial transactions across the empire used a single system.

Dragon Boat Festival , celebrated on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. Commemorates Qu Yuan's drowning in the Miluo River. Marked by dragon boat races and the eating of 粽子 zòngzi (sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves).

e: Duan inkstone, from Duanxi in Guangdong province
d: Duan inkstone, from Duanxi in Guangdong province. The finest inkstone in the traditional Chinese hierarchy. Prized for its fine grain (described as 嫩 nèn, tender), water retention, and the distinctive circular "eyes" 石眼 that appear in the stone and are incorporated into decorative designs.
短 (deficient) + 处 (chù, point, place): a point where one falls short, a flaw or weakness. The abstract sense of 短 made concrete as a named fault.
短 (short) + 发 (fà, hair): hair worn short. Contrasts directly with 长发 (chángfà, long hair).

e: "Short Song" — Cao Cao's most famous poem
d: A banquet poem on the shortness of life and the hunger to draw great men into one's service. Its opening, 对酒当歌，人生几何 ("facing the wine one should sing; how much is a human life?"), is a stock quotation for the fleetingness of time.
短 (short) + 裤 (kù, trousers): trousers cut short above the knee. The most literal modern use of the length sense.
短 (short) + 期 (qī, period): a short span of time. Common in finance, planning, and study, opposite of 长期 (chángqī, long term).
短 (deficient) + 缺 (quē, lacking): a shortage of supply, when something runs short of what is needed.

短 duǎn (short; brief) + 信 xìn (word; letter; communication). A short letter. The compound maps the ancient sense of 信 as written communication directly to the mobile-phone era , there was no borrowing from English, no phonetic transcription, just a classical compound structure applied to a new techn…
短 (short) + 暂 (zàn, temporary): short and passing, said of moments, lives, or encounters that do not last.

e: to break; to sever; to cut off

d: Flow interruption: the failure of the river to reach the sea due to upstream water extraction. The Yellow River experienced 断流 in 22 of the 28 years between 1972 and 1999, a crisis that triggered national water management reform.
队 (formed group) + 伍 (a file of five soldiers, the old squad). The pairing names a body of people standing or moving in order, from a literal military column to a figurative workforce or movement.
队 (formed group) + 形 (shape). The geometric pattern a group holds while moving: a wedge of soldiers, a flying V of geese, a defensive line on the pitch.
队 (team) + 员 (member, a person filling a role). Any rank-and-file member of a team: a player, a scout, a rescue worker.
队 (team) + 长 (chief, the elder/head). The one at the front of the column: a sports captain, a squad leader, the head of a work brigade.

The teacher's tag and the explainer's checkpoint, punctuating reasoning the way English "right?" does. The listener's murmured 对对对 in reply is the sound of a Chinese conversation agreeing with itself.

e: I'm sorry — lit. "I cannot face you"
d: 对 duì (to face; toward) + 不起 buqǐ (cannot rise to; cannot face). Literally "I cannot face you," an expression of guilt and apology for having let someone down. The response is 没关系 méi guānxi (it doesn't matter) or 没事 méishì (no problem).

e: the other party; the opposite side
d: 对 duì (facing; opposite) + 方 fāng (party). The other side in a conversation, negotiation, contest, or relationship. Its pairs are 双方 shuāngfāng (both parties) and 我方 wǒfāng (our side).
对 duì (facing; mutual) + 话 huà (speech). Speech exchanged face to face. Concrete dialogue in a textbook or film, and figurative dialogue between sides: 和平对话 "peace talks."

e: Oh right! — used when remembering something
d: 对 duì (correct) + 了 le (change of state). "Oh right!", used to introduce something you just remembered or to redirect a conversation. Not about correctness in this use: 对了 at the beginning of a sentence is a discourse marker meaning "Oh! I just remembered…" or "Wait, by the way…".

e: "For me" or "as far as I'm concerned
d: "For me" or "as far as I'm concerned." Frames a statement as true from your perspective without claiming it is universally true. Often paired with adjectives of preference or difficulty: 对我来说, 这个太难了 ("for me, this is too hard").

e: regarding; with regard to; as for
d: 对 duì (toward) + 于 yú (to). Introduces the thing an opinion or attitude is directed at: 对于这个问题 "regarding this question." It heads the topic of a sentence, much like English "as for."
Tonal and semantic parallelism , the requirement that paired couplet lines mirror each other grammatically, semantically, and tonally.
兑 (to cash, redeem) + 换 (swap). The formal term for currency conversion or redeeming points and vouchers. What 换钱 says casually, 兑换 says on the signboard.

e: more or less; to some extent
d: The question word reduplicated into a hedge: some amount on the scale, unspecified but nonzero. It softens claims politely, which makes it a favorite of careful speakers: everyone at the meeting 多多少少 had objections, though few voiced them.

多 (much) + 亏 (kuī, to be indebted to, to owe). "Much-owed-to" , fortunately thanks to X. Expresses relief that something good or fortunate happened because of another person or circumstance: 多亏你帮忙，要不然就麻烦了 (thanks to your help, otherwise it would have been a problem). Colloquial and warm in register.

多 (how much) + 么 (question/exclamation suffix). An exclamatory intensifier: 多么美啊 (how beautiful!); 多么幸运 (how lucky). More literary than colloquial 多 alone. Used in song lyrics, poetry, and formal speeches to express admiration or strong feeling.

The universal way to ask a price. Because cost can be any amount, you use 多少, never 几: 这件衣服多少钱？("how much is this piece of clothing?"). The answer uses money measure words: 块 kuài (yuan, colloquial), 毛 máo (ten cents), 分 fēn (cent). 一共多少钱 ("how much altogether") totals a bill.
多 (multi-) + 元 (yuan, element, source, unit). Multi-source, diverse in origin. 多元文化 (multiculturalism); 多元社会 (pluralistic society); 多元经济 (diversified economy).

e: hungry ghost — a being trapped in a realm of insatiable craving
d: 饿 è (hungry; starving) + 鬼 guǐ (ghost; spirit). One of the six realms of Buddhist cosmology (六道 liùdào): hungry ghosts have enormous bellies and throats too narrow to swallow, condemned to perpetual craving without satisfaction: the post-mortem form of greed.

e: the hungry ghost realm; the path of insatiable craving
d: 饿鬼 è guǐ (hungry ghosts): beings with enormous appetites and tiny throats , perpetually starving, unable to consume enough to be satisfied. In Buddhist iconography they are depicted as emaciated figures with swollen bellies and needle-thin necks.

e: the Oroqen — northern China's forest hunters
d: The Oroqen (鄂伦春族 Èlúnchūn zú , from Tungusic words meaning "people who use reindeer" or "people on the mountain ridge") are among the smallest ethnic groups in China, with a population of approximately 9,000, concentrated in Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang province.

e: the Evenki — reindeer herders of the forest steppe
d: The Evenki (鄂温克族 Èwēnkè zú , "people who live on mountains covered with forests") are the most widely distributed Tungusic people, with populations in China (approximately 30,000, concentrated in Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang), Russia, and Mongolia.

e: kindness received; an unrepayable debt of gratitude
d: 恩 ēn (favor; kindness; grace) + 德. Kindness so substantial it counts as virtue. Used for a debt of gratitude that runs deeper than ordinary thanks: a teacher who shaped one's life, a friend who saved one in a crisis.
儿 (child) plus 歌 (song). A children's song, the first 歌 most native speakers ever learn.
儿 ér (child, son) + 子 zi (suffix). The standard word for a son. Its pair is 女儿 nǚ'ér (daughter), which keeps 儿 but not 子.

e: thereafter; and only then; after that
d: 而 ér (and) + 后 hòu (after). Orders one event strictly after another in a literary register: do A, 而后 do B. Lives on in the maxim 三思而后行 "think thrice, then act."
而 ér (but) + 是 shì (is). The corrective half of the 不是…而是… frame: it rejects a wrong claim and supplies the right one. 不是他，而是我 "it was not him, but rather me."

e: that is all; nothing more; merely
d: 而 ér (and) + 已 yǐ (to stop; only). A sentence-final frame that caps a statement with "and nothing more," often softening or downplaying. Frequently paired with 只是 zhǐshì (merely) earlier in the clause.

耳 (ear) + 朵 (duǒ, flower; measure word for flowers, ears, and clouds). 朵 is the measure word for ear-shaped objects; 耳朵 is the unmarked everyday word for the ear as a physical body part. 一只耳朵 or 一个耳朵 are both acceptable, but 耳朵 alone typically refers to the ear without a number.

耳 (ear) + 机 (machine; device). The device for the ear. 入耳式耳机 (in-ear earphones), 头戴式耳机 (over-ear headphones). A modern compound that keeps 耳 as its anchor, illustrating how the character's body-part meaning extends naturally to technology.

耳 (ear) + 目 (eye). The two organs of alert perception together , the paired sentinels. Used figuratively for one's information network, or for spies and informants: 皇帝的耳目 (the emperor's ears and eyes). Also in 耳目一新 ěrmù yīxīn (a completely fresh impression, as if new eyes and ears).

e: to have heard of; auditory knowledge
d: 耳 (ear) + 闻 (to hear; to be known). To have heard of something, often at a distance or through others.
二 (two) + 哥. The second of the brothers, ranked after 大哥. The numbering system is literal: each older brother is addressed by his birth order, never by name within the family.

二 èr (two) + 胡 hú (a category of instruments of non-Han origin, literally "barbarian"). The erhu has exactly two strings, which defines both its name and its voice: the two strings produce the characteristic close-interval resonance that makes the instrument sound like a human throat.
二 èr (two; a second) + 话 huà (speech; words). Always appears in the negative: 没有二话 or 不说二话 means to comply without objection or complaint, without a second word.

The 28 Lunar Mansions: the primary coordinate system of Chinese astronomy, dividing the ecliptic and celestial equator into 28 unequal stations corresponding to the moon's daily progress around the sky.
二 èr (two; second) + 手 shǒu (hand). Something that has passed through a second hand. Standard term for used goods, pre-owned vehicles, and resale markets.

二 èr (two) + 元 yuán (origin; element; primary unit) + 论 lùn (theory; discourse). The philosophical position that reality is composed of two irreducible substances or principles. 二元 èryuán alone means "dual; binary; two-dimensional" and appears across technical and philosophical contexts.
二 èr (two) + 月 yuè (moon; month). Chinese months are purely positional: the first month is 一月, the second is 二月, through 十二月 (December). There are no separate month names.

e: to publish; to issue; to express (publicly)
d: 发 fā (to issue) + 表 biǎo (to express; surface). To put a piece of writing or an opinion out into the public sphere: 发表文章 "to publish an article," 发表意见 "to voice an opinion."

e: To get rich, to make money
d: To get rich, to make money: the aspiration whose first syllable 发 (fā) sounds like 八 (bā, eight) in Cantonese, giving eight its commercial prestige. 恭喜发财 (gōngxǐ fācái, "congratulations and may you prosper") is the standard Spring Festival greeting.

e: to give off; to emit; to issue (a sound, light, order)
d: 发 fā (to emit) + 出 chū (out). To let something out from a source: a sound, a smell, a light, a command. 发出声音 "to make a sound," 发出命令 "to issue an order."

e: to show mercy; to bring forth compassion (colloquial)
d: 发 fā (to bring forth; to emit) + 慈悲. The colloquial register for asking someone to be merciful, lenient, or helpful. The religious vocabulary of 慈悲 serves as the vehicle for a thoroughly everyday request. Tone determines whether the phrase is earnest, playful, or ironic.

e: to send a red envelope; to distribute lucky money
to lose one's temper; to flare up (contrast)
d: 发 fā (to emit; to break out) + 火 huǒ (fire). Not a 气 compound, but essential for contrast. Where 生气 is quiet simmering anger, 发火 is the eruption: raised voice, visible emotion, the moment qi becomes fire. Colloquial. Very common in domestic and workplace situations.

e: official receipt: an invoice; a tax receipt
d: 发 fā (to issue; to send out) + 票 piào (slip; note). The official, tax-registered receipt a seller issues for a purchase. In China the 发票 is a regulated document used for reimbursement and tax, very different from a plain shop receipt (小票 xiǎopiào).

e: to run a fever; to give off heat
d: 发 (fā, to emit) plus 热 (heat): to give off heat. Of a body it means to run a fever; of a machine it means to overheat. The clinical register on a thermometer reading or a hospital chart.
To run a fever: emit burn. 量体温 is to take a temperature; 退烧 is the fever breaking, and 退烧药 the medicine that breaks it.

e: to happen; to occur; to take place
d: 发 fā (to send forth) + 生 shēng (life; to arise). For an event to come into being: 发生事故 "an accident happens," 发生变化 "a change occurs." Used of events, not of people deliberately doing things.

e: to send; to transmit; to dispatch
d: 发 fā (to send out) + 送 sòng (to deliver). To send a message, signal, or shipment outward to a recipient: 发送邮件 "to send an email." The everyday verb for transmitting in the digital age.

e: to discover; to find; to realize
d: 发 fā (to bring forth) + 现 xiàn (to appear; manifest). To bring something previously hidden into view, whether a fact, an object, or a realization: 发现问题 "to spot a problem," 科学发现 "a scientific discovery."

发 (emit) + 音 (sound). The compliment every learner works for is 你的发音很标准 ("your pronunciation is very standard"), 标准 being the operative cultural value: the broadcast-Mandarin ideal against which accents are measured.

e: making vows — aspiring to rebirth with sincere intention
d: 发 fā (to make; to express) + 愿 yuàn (vow; aspiration; wish). The devotional expression of one's sincere desire to be reborn in the Pure Land.
发 fā (to bring forth) + 展 zhǎn (to unfold; spread). To grow and expand from a smaller or earlier state: 经济发展 "economic development," 发展中国家 "a developing country." Works as both verb and noun.

Policy and business vocabulary. 行业的发展方向 (the industry's direction of development), 国家的发展方向 (the country's direction of development). Often paired with verbs of pointing or indicating: 明确发展方向 (to clarify the direction).

e: Legalism — governance through law, reward, and punishment
d: The philosophy that conquered China. Key theorists: 商鞅 Shāng Yāng (architect of Qin's reforms), 申不害 Shēn Bùhài (on administrative technique), 慎到 Shèn Dào (on positional power), and 韩非子 Hán Fēizǐ (synthesizer of all three).
法 fǎ (law) + 律 lǜ (rule; statute). The body of law as a system, the formal rules a state enacts and enforces. 遵守法律 "to obey the law," 法律问题 "a legal question."

e: Dharma master; a learned monk or nun
d: 法 fǎ (Dharma) + 师 shī (master; teacher). A respectful title for a monk or nun versed in the teaching, qualified to expound it to others. Used before or after a religious name.
法 fǎ (law) + 院 yuàn (institution; courtyard). The court where law is applied and cases are judged. 人民法院 "the People's Court," 上法院 "to go to court."
帆 (sail) + 船 (boat): a boat driven by canvas. Covers everything from a small racing dinghy to the old treasure ships, and names the Olympic sport of sailing.

e: to turn hostile; to fall out with someone
d: 翻 (to flip, turn over) + 脸 (face). To flip the face from friendly to cold in an instant, breaking off goodwill. The vivid version is 翻脸不认人 (fānliǎn bú rèn rén), to turn cold and pretend you never knew the person.

e: to climb over (especially a mountain or wall)
d: 翻 (fān, to flip; to turn over) + 越. The physical act of climbing up and over an obstacle. Strongly associated with crossing mountain ranges; the verb of choice for descriptions of mountain expeditions, escape across hostile terrain, and the Long March.

e: the mortal realm; the ordinary world (as seen from above)
d: 凡 fán (mortal; ordinary; not immortal) + 间 (space; realm). The mortal world as defined by its contrast with the celestial.

繁 fán (complex; numerous) + 体 tǐ (form; body; style) + 字 zì. The original, more structurally complex character forms that preserve more visual information about component etymology. Used in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, and many overseas Chinese communities.

e: on the contrary; instead; the other way around
d: 反 fǎn (reverse) + 而 ér (and so). Marks an outcome that runs opposite to expectation: you would predict one thing, but the reverse happens. 不但没…反而… "not only did not... but on the contrary...".

反 fǎn (back) + 应 yìng (to respond). The response that comes back when something acts on you: a chemical reaction (化学反应), a person's reaction to news, a body's reaction to medicine. Both noun and verb.
The neutral opener. 客诉 (kèsù) is a complaint from your own customers, a useful word because it shifts the pressure to the market rather than to you.
反 fǎn (reverse) + 正 zhèng (right). Literally "reverse-or-right," whichever way it turns out: the all-purpose "anyway, the outcome is the same." 反正我不去 "anyway, I'm not going."

Fixing defective goods. Its harder cousins: 报废 (bàofèi) scrapping, 补货 (bǔhuò) replacing goods, 退货 (tuìhuò) returning them. 整改 (zhěnggǎi) is a corrective action on the process itself, so the defect stops recurring.

e: to get drowsy; to feel sleepy
d: 犯 (to come on, to have a bout of) + 困 (sleepy). A spell of drowsiness creeping over you, often at the wrong time. Colloquial and very common: the after-lunch slump, the late-night struggle to stay awake.

e: harmonic tones — the "heavenly" register of the guqin
d: 泛 fàn (to float; to overflow) + 音 yīn (sound). Produced by lightly touching the string at one of the 13 marked 徽 huī positions without pressing it to the board, then plucking. The result is a clear, bell-like overtone.
饭 fàn (cooked rice, a meal) + 馆. A modest, sit-down place to eat, the neighborhood diner rather than a banquet hall. Often said 小饭馆 for the cheap, friendly kind.

e: convenient; to make things easy for; (euphemism) to use the toilet
d: 方 fāng + 便 biàn (convenient; suitable). Easy and convenient, of a time, a place, or an arrangement. 方便面 fāngbiànmiàn is instant noodles, literally "convenient noodles." As a polite euphemism it also means to relieve oneself.
Equation. The term is two thousand years old, taken from the chapter of the Nine Chapters that solved systems of linear equations with counting rods. 解方程 (jiě fāngchéng) is to solve an equation.

e: method; means; way of doing something
d: 方 fāng (square; direction) + 法 fǎ (way). A method or procedure considered in the abstract, the systematic way to approach a task: 学习方法 "study methods," 科学方法 "the scientific method."

方 (direction; side) + 面 (face; surface). A particular "side" or "face" of a topic , one of the aspects of a multi-sided issue. Extremely common in academic, journalistic, and analytical Chinese. 在这方面 (in this regard), 各个方面 (all aspects), and 经济方面 (in terms of economics) are standard expressions.
方 fāng (way) + 式 shì (form; pattern). The manner or mode in which something is done, broader and more abstract than 方法: 生活方式 lifestyle, 付款方式 payment method.

When the focused element is a manner, means, or instrument, 是…的 answers "how?" The manner phrase sits after 是 and before the main verb. This is a natural way to specify or contrast the means of travel, communication, or action.

方 (region) + 位 (position). More technical than 方向: a fixed cardinal bearing rather than a heading. Used in geography, military, navigation, and feng shui contexts. 方位词 (fāngwèicí) is the grammatical category of "position words" , 上 above, 下 below, 前 front, 后 back, 左 left, 右 right.

e: Directional Taboos — feng shui and orientation
d: Spatial orientation is governed by 风水 fēngshuǐ (feng shui, lit. "wind-water"), the art of placing buildings, graves, and furniture to harmonize with the flow of qi 气. The main door of a house should not directly face a staircase, a toilet, or a knife-like corner of another building.

方向 + 感 (gǎn, sense; feeling). The personal faculty of knowing where you are in space , and, by extension, where your life or project is heading. Used both literally (in conversations about getting lost) and figuratively (about clarity of purpose).
方向 + 盘 (pán, plate; disc). The literal "direction-disc" of a vehicle. Used figuratively for whoever holds control: 谁掌握方向盘 ("who holds the wheel") = who is in charge of the direction.
Topolect, regional speech , the Chinese term for what English often calls "dialect." Applied to the major regional speech varieties: Cantonese, Wu, Min, Hakka, Gan, Xiang.

房 (house) plus 东 (dōng, east; by old convention the host stands on the east side). The person who owns the dwelling and rents it out. The 东 element marks the host or owner, the same 东 found in 股东 (gǔdōng, shareholder).
房 (house) plus 价 (jià, price). The purchase price of property. A constant topic in contemporary Chinese life, where 房价 in big cities is a daily-news obsession.

房 fáng (room; building-section) + 间 jiān (space between; a measure word for rooms). The standard neutral word for a room in a house, hotel, or office. 三室两厅 = three bedrooms two living rooms (standard real-estate description).
房 fáng (house) + 主 zhǔ (owner). The person who owns a dwelling. The pattern noun + 主 names the owner of a thing: 车主 chēzhǔ (car owner), 业主 yèzhǔ (property owner).
房 (building) plus the neutral-tone noun suffix 子 (zi). The default everyday word for a house or any standalone building you live in. Concrete and countable: you buy one, rent one, or build one.
房 (house) plus 租 (zū, to rent, rent money). The money paid to occupy a dwelling. Pair it with 交 (jiāo, to hand over): 交房租 means to pay the rent.

仿 fǎng (to imitate; resembling) + 佛 fú (phonetic only; here read fú, not fó, with no Buddhist meaning). A high-frequency literary and spoken adverb meaning "as if; seemingly; as though." Used to describe perceptions, memories, or states that have a dreamlike or approximate quality.

e: to visit; to call on; to interview; (computing) to access
d: 访 fǎng (to call on) + 问 wèn (to ask after). A formal visit made to a person, place, or, by modern extension, a website or file. 国事访问 "a state visit," 访问网站 "to access a website."

e: floating river lanterns — guiding wandering spirits home
d: 放 fàng (release; set free) + 河 hé (river) + 灯 dēng (lantern). Paper lanterns, typically lotus-shaped with a candle inside, set onto rivers, ponds, and coastlines on the evening of the 15th.

e: to slow down; to ease up the pace
d: 放 fàng (to release, to let go) + 慢 màn (slow). To deliberately release speed. Used for vehicles, speech, breathing, economic growth. The verb of conscious deceleration.

e: to relax; to stop worrying; to feel at ease
d: 放 fàng (to put down; to release; to set free) + 心 xīn (heart). Lit. "put the heart down." The direct antonym of 担心. If worry is carrying the heart, 放心 is setting it back on the ground: the relief of knowing that what you feared is safe or resolved. Extremely frequent in reassurances and farewells.
Flying white: a dry-brush effect where the hairs of the brush separate, leaving streaks of paper showing through the ink. A controlled accident, difficult to achieve and highly prized.
飞 (to fly) plus 机 (machine): the flying machine. This is the everyday word for any fixed-wing aircraft, from a jetliner to a small propeller plane.

e: lightning fast; at a flying pace
d: 飞 fēi (to fly) + 快 kuài (fast). Vivid intensifier: the speed of something that seems to fly. It modifies a verb as an adverb or stands alone as a predicate adjective. Also used for a blade that is razor-sharp , fast at cutting.

e: a bird in flight, flying bird
d: 飞 (flying) plus 鸟 (bird): a bird on the wing. The word keeps the character close to its pictographic root, naming the very creature the glyph was drawn from.

e: to soar, to circle in flight

d: 飞 (to fly) plus 行 (to move, to travel): movement through the air. More formal and technical than plain 飞, this is the word for piloting, air travel, and aviation as a field. 飞行员 (fēixíngyuán) is a pilot.
飞 (flying) plus 涨 (to rise, of water or prices): prices climbing as if in flight. The standard word for a steep, fast jump in cost.

非 fēi (not) + 常 cháng (ordinary). As an adverb before an adjective it means "extremely" (非常高兴 "extremely happy"); as an adjective before a noun it keeps the older sense "extraordinary, exceptional" (非常时期 "extraordinary times").
非 fēi (not) + 法 fǎ (law). Outside the law, not lawful: 非法行为 "illegal conduct," 非法移民 "illegal immigration." Its opposite is 合法 héfǎ (lawful).
Mozi distinguished between defensive warfare (permitted) and aggressive conquest (condemned as categorically unjust).
非 fēi (to fault) + 议 yì (to discuss; opinion). To talk of something as wrong, to find fault with it: 无可非议 "beyond reproach, nothing to criticize." Here 非 acts as a verb, "to deem wrong."

e: to take effort; to be laborious; to be time-consuming
d: 费 fèi (to spend; to cost; to consume) + 功夫 (effort). Where 下功夫 emphasizes voluntarily investing effort, 费功夫 emphasizes the effort a task demands of you , the cost side of the equation. A task that is 费功夫 is demanding, painstaking, time-intensive.

费 fèi (to spend; cost; waste; excessive expenditure) + 用 yòng (use). What is spent in order to use something: the cost of deployment. Covers expenses of all kinds , medical fees, travel costs, operational expenditure , across formal and everyday registers.
The compromise line. Offering it yourself, once fault is clear, buys goodwill for the next order.
分 (fēn, to divide) plus 封 (to confer land): to carve a realm into fiefs and grant them to vassals. The defining act of the early Zhōu political order.

e: to separate; to part; to divide up
d: 分 fēn (divide) + 开 kāi (open; apart). To pull two things apart or keep them distinct: 把垃圾分开 "sort the rubbish," 我们分开走 "let's go separately."

e: to classify; to sort into categories
d: 分 fēn (divide) + 类 lèi (kind; category). To divide things into kinds: 垃圾分类 "waste sorting," 图书分类 "cataloguing books."
分 (fēn, to divide) plus 离 (to part). Two reinforcing halves: things that were one are now in pieces. Used for people parting and for substances separated in a process.

e: to part ways; to break up (a couple)
d: 分 fēn (separate) + 手 shǒu (hand). To let go of one another's hand. In everyday use it most often means a romantic break-up, but it can simply mean two people parting at a crossroads.
分 fēn (point) + 数 shù (number). A test score, and in mathematics a fraction. Both senses share the idea of a number standing below or against a whole.
分 fēn (a divided unit) + 钟 zhōng (clock). A minute as a span of time: 等五分钟 "wait five minutes." To tell the time on the clock face, 分 alone is enough: 两点十五分 "two fifteen."
Molecule: divided unit. The same word, differently stressed, means "member of a group" in political vocabulary (知识分子, intellectuals), a coincidence of compounding worth knowing before it confuses.

e: measure word for copies and portions
share money — the obligatory wedding gift

d: 丰 (lush, plentiful) plus 富 (abundant). As an adjective, rich in variety or quantity. As a verb, to enrich or broaden, as in 丰富知识 (to broaden one's knowledge).

e: style; manner; character; the distinctive way something is done
d: 风 fēng (wind; manner) + 格 gé (standard; grid; manner). The characteristic way someone or something presents itself , artistic style, architectural style, speaking style, leadership style.

风 fēng (wind; atmosphere) + 景 jǐng (view; scene; spectacle). The atmospheric scene , the view that catches the eye and stirs the spirit. Not just a geographic description but an aesthetic one: 风景 implies the view is worth seeing.

e: a feng shui treasure land; an auspiciously sited place
d: 宝 bǎo (treasure; precious) + 地 dì (land; place). A site so well positioned in the landscape , with mountains, water, orientation, and dragon veins all aligning , that it is considered to bring fortune to whoever inhabits it or is buried there.

e: wind and water mutually generate — the core principle of feng shui energy management
d: The operative logic behind 风水: when wind is blocked by mountains and water is present to create a boundary, 气 accumulates rather than dispersing. Wind and water are the agents , qi is what they manage.

e: geomantic grave siting — fortune for the living through the dead
d: The location and orientation of a grave (阴宅 yīnzhái, "yin dwelling") directly affects the fortune of the descendants, a doctrine that made grave geomancy (阴宅风水 yīnzhái fēngshuǐ) one of the most important applications of feng shui.

e: wind direction; (figurative) which way the wind blows
d: 风 fēng (wind) + 向 xiàng (direction). The direction the wind comes from. Used figuratively for the drift of opinion or events: 看风向 "to see which way the wind is blowing," to read the mood before acting.

e: wind-words wind-language — whispers; rumors; idle gossip
d: Reduplication of 风 (wind) around 言 yán (words; speech) and 语 yǔ (language). Words as insubstantial as wind , whispers and rumors that circulate without clear source or foundation.
封 (to seal) plus 闭 (bì, to shut): to close something off completely. Used for sealing a road, a building, a wound, or, figuratively, a closed-off mindset.

e: feudal investiture — the Zhou territorial hierarchy
d: 封 fēng (to enfeoff; to heap earth as a boundary marker) + 建 jiàn (to establish). The Zhou system of distributing territory to vassals with corresponding titles, ritual privileges, and obligations.

Feudal superstition: the official Communist Party category used to delegitimize traditional folk religious practices, ancestor veneration, feng shui, and divination. The phrase was weaponized during the Cultural Revolution.

e: to seal an opening; to keep quiet

d: 封 (the closing layer) plus 面 (miàn, face / surface): the outer face that wraps and closes a book. By extension, the front cover of any publication.
封 (to seal) plus 锁 (suǒ, to lock): to seal and lock down, blocking passage or flow. Used for military blockades, sealed-off areas, and information blackouts.

"Seal the sample": approved units are labelled, signed by both sides, and kept by each as the binding quality standard for bulk. Also called 标准样 (biāozhǔnyàng) or 金样 (jīnyàng, golden sample). Keep at least one yourself.

e: receiving heaven's mandate and carrying forward its fortune — the opening formula of imperial edicts
d: 奉 fèng (to receive; to hold reverently) + 天 tiān (heaven) + 承 chéng (to carry on; to inherit) + 运 yùn (fortune; cycle; destiny). The four characters that opened every imperial edict from the early Ming dynasty onward.

e: to deny, to refuse to acknowledge
d: 否 fǒu (negation; to deny) + 认 rèn. The structural opposite of 承认. To formally refuse the recognition: to deny an accusation, deny an affair, deny a relationship.

e: a married couple; husband and wife (formal)
d: 夫 fū (husband) + 妇 fù (married woman). A married couple, close in meaning to 夫妻 but more formal and bookish. Often attached to a surname: 张氏夫妇 the Zhang couple, 新婚夫妇 newlyweds. Where 夫妻 feels everyday and warm, 夫妇 reads as written or ceremonious.

e: husband and wife — the household foundation
d: The marital relationship orders the household 家 jiā, which is the structural unit between the individual and the state. The husband is obligated to provide and to lead with moral example; the wife is obligated to manage the inner household and to support the family's moral life.

夫 fū (man) + 人 rén (person). A respectful term for a married woman, especially the wife of a person of standing: 总统夫人 the first lady, 王夫人 Madam Wang. It honors the woman through her husband's status, so it is formal rather than intimate; you would not call your own wife 夫人 in casual speech.

e: the Dharma; Buddhist teaching; the law of the Buddha
d: 佛 + 法 fǎ (law; method; dharma). The teachings of the Buddha as a whole, understood as both doctrine and practice. Also the specific rendering of Sanskrit dharma, which encompasses cosmic law, the teachings themselves, individual phenomena, and moral truth.

佛 (Buddha) + 教 jiào (teaching; religion; to teach). The standard modern term for Buddhism as a religion or institutional tradition. Entered China officially during the Han dynasty (around the 1st century CE), though oral transmission and merchant routes likely brought it earlier.

e: Buddhist festivals — integrated into the Chinese calendar
d: 浴佛节 Yùfó Jié (Buddha's Birthday, 4th lunar month, 8th day): ritual bathing of the infant Buddha statue with scented water, commemorating his birth.
佛 fó (Buddha) + 经 jīng (scripture). The sutras, the recorded discourses of the Buddha. Reciting and copying 佛经 is a long-standing devotional practice, as with the much-loved 心经 xīnjīng (Heart Sutra).

e: the Smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha · ~1,800 characters · Kumārajīva's 402 CE translation
d: The short Amitabha Sutra. The daily-recitation text of Pure Land practice. The Buddha describes the Pure Land's adornments to Śāriputra, names the practice (single-minded recollection of Amitābha), and is supported by the buddhas of the six directions affirming the teaching.

佛 + 系 xì (style; type; lineage, as in 日系 Japanese-style). Emerged in Chinese internet culture around 2017 to describe a mentality of deliberate non-striving: going with the flow, not competing, indifferent to outcomes.

e: to conform to; to accord with; to match
d: 符 fú (a tally; to tally) + 合 hé (to fit). To match a standard or expectation exactly, the way two halves of an ancient tally fit: 符合规定 "to conform to the rules," 符合条件 "to meet the conditions."

e: talismans and registers — written instruments of Daoist power
d: 符 fú (talisman, a written or drawn symbol charged with spiritual power) + 箓 lù (registers, lists of divine names that give priests authority over corresponding spirits).

e: blessed fortune; a life touched by luck
d: 福 fú + 气 qì (atmosphere; quality; energy). The quality of being blessed: having fortune as part of one's life-energy. 有福气 yǒu fúqi = to be blessed / to have good fortune. A compliment that goes beyond luck to a general quality of being favored by life.

e: a mansion; an official's grand residence
d: 府 fǔ (official residence; manor) + 第 dì (ranked dwelling). The stately home of a high official or noble family. Literary and historical; you meet it in novels and on heritage plaques rather than in conversation.

e: to bow the head; to submit
d: 俯 fǔ (to bend down, to lower) + 首 shǒu (head). To lower the head, and by extension to yield or submit. 俯首听命 "to bow the head and take orders" describes obedient submission. The direct opposite of 昂首.

e: tofu skin; bean curd skin; yuba

d: 父 fù (father) + 辈 bèi (generation, cohort). The fathers' generation taken as a class, everyone of the parents' age and above. Set against 子辈 zǐbèi, the children's generation, when speaking of how a family changes across the line.
父 fù (father) + 母 mǔ (mother). The standard word for parents as a pair. Father comes first by convention, the same ordering that runs through the whole kinship vocabulary.

父 fù (father) + 亲 qīn (kin, close relative). The formal, written word for father, the one used on documents, in introductions, and in respectful speech. In daily conversation people say 爸爸 bàba instead; 父亲 carries weight and distance.

e: parent and child — the root relationship; filial piety
d: The foundational relationship , described by Confucians as the root from which all other social virtues grow. The child's obligation is 孝 xiào (filial piety): obedience, care in old age, ritual mourning at death, and continuation of the family line.
Names the owner of an action. Ask it about every open item before the meeting ends. 对……负责 also means "to be accountable for" a result, which makes it the word of quality disputes.

e: nearby; in the vicinity; around here
d: 附 fù (to attach to; to be adjacent to) + 近 (near). The area attached nearby , the general term for the vicinity of a place. 附近 functions as both noun (学校附近, in the vicinity of the school) and adverb-like modifier.

e: spirit possession — the spirit descending into the shaman
d: 附体 (spirit possession , lit. "spirit attaches to body") is one of two modes of shamanic trance in Tungusic tradition. In the other mode (魂游 húnyóu , soul-flight), the shaman's own soul leaves the body and travels to the spirit world while the body remains passive.

e: to revive; to come back to life; resurrection
d: 复 fù (again, to return) + 活 huó (to live). To live again: the dead returning to life, or by extension a thing once finished springing back. 复活节 fùhuójié is Easter, the festival of resurrection.

e: to restore the old order; to revert to the past
d: 复 (fù, to return to; to restore; to repeat) + 旧 (old). To restore a previous state , often used in political contexts for attempted counter-revolution or reactionary restoration. 复旧势力 (forces seeking to restore the old order) was a standard phrase in Cultural Revolution rhetoric.

复 (again) + 习 (practice, whose traditional form 習 shows wings over the sun: a fledgling's repeated flights). The exam-season verb, echoing the Analects' opening line about the pleasure of timely review, which every Chinese student can quote and few believe during finals.

e: to be rich in; to contain abundantly
d: 富 (abundant) plus 含 (to contain). To hold something in great quantity, common in writing about food and nutrition.
富 (rich) plus 强 (strong). A wealthy and powerful state, a phrase reaching back to the warring-states ideal of 富国强兵, a rich country and a strong army.
富 (rich) plus 人 (person). A wealthy individual, and collectively the rich as a class, set against 穷人 (qióngrén), the poor.
富 (rich) plus 有 (to have). Literally "rich and possessing." Describes a person with great wealth, and figuratively something abundantly endowed with a quality, as in 富有经验 (rich in experience).
富 (rich) plus 裕 (abundant, ample). Describes a comfortable, well-off condition, often of a household, village, or society rather than a single tycoon.

Direct narration: the mode of straightforward statement and description, naming the subject and describing it without indirection. Also the name of a later Han dynasty poetic genre notable for its elaborate descriptive technique.

e: to change (something); to alter; to modify
d: 改 gǎi (to correct; to revise; to alter, itself containing 己 self + 攴 striking hand) + 变 biàn. The key difference from standalone 变: 改变 is transitive and agentive. Someone 改变s something. 变 alone can describe change that happens to a subject; 改变 requires an agent making a deliberate alteration.

e: to change into, to turn into
d: 改 (alter) + 成 (become). A result complement: to alter A so that it becomes B. Names the new state explicitly after the verb.

改 gǎi (to correct; to revise) + 革 gé (to reform; to strip away, the hide-tanning radical). The standard term for political and institutional reform. Where 变革 describes change as a phenomenon, 改革 is more often a policy objective: you implement 改革, you carry out 改革.

e: reform and opening up — the policy itself
d: The defining phrase of post-Mao China: the paired program of internal structural reform (改革) and outward engagement (开放) launched in 1978.
改 (alter) + 进 (advance). To better a method, product, or process by moving it forward. The everyday word in engineering and management for incremental improvement.

Changing the tool after a trial. The crucial question is who pays: changes caused by the factory's error are on them, changes caused by a new request from you are on you. Agree which is which in writing before work starts. 修模 (xiūmú) is repair or maintenance.
改 (alter) + 善 (good). To change toward the good: to better conditions, relations, or quality. Used for situations and systems more than for a person's skill.
改 (change) + 天 (day). To shift a plan to a different day. A soft, friendly way to postpone or to propose meeting later, very common in spoken Mandarin.
"Let's chat another time." Proposes future contact without committing to a specific time. Warm and noncommittal, like English "let's catch up soon." Common closer among friends and acquaintances.

e: to transform, to remold, to renovate
d: 改 (alter) + 造 (build, make). To rebuild something into a new form: renovating a building, retrofitting a machine, or, in older political language, reforming a person's thinking.

e: to correct; to put right; to amend
d: 改 gǎi (to change) + 正 zhèng (straight). To change something crooked back to straight: 改正错误 "to correct a mistake." The act of bringing a thing back onto the line.

The red veil worn by the bride during the wedding procession and ceremony, lifted by the groom in the bridal chamber. The lifting of the veil (揭盖头 jiē gàitóu) was the culminating moment of the traditional wedding ceremony.

e: lidded bowl — the standard gōngfu brewing vessel

d: 赶 (gǎn, to rush, to drive forward) + 紧 (tight). To move with no slack, to act before the moment slips. A spoken, everyday urging to do something now.

e: hurry up; do it right now
d: 赶 gǎn (to catch up; to rush) + 快 kuài (fast). Used when something needs to happen without delay. Always an adverb modifying a following verb; it conveys urgency rather than habitual speed, with an implicit time pressure in the context.

e: to feel; to register a state
d: 感 gǎn (feel) + 到 dào (arrive at · result marker). The 到 is a resultative complement signaling that the feeling has landed, been registered as a completed state. The most neutral, all-purpose feeling verb. Almost always takes an adjectival or clausal complement.

e: to be moved; to touch someone's heart
d: 感 gǎn + 动 dòng (to move). The heart set in motion by something beautiful, kind, or touching. One of the most emotionally central verbs in Chinese, high frequency in literature, film, and daily speech.

e: to honor all grace received; gratitude as virtue
d: 感 gǎn + 恩 ēn (grace; benevolence: the kindness of parents, teachers, heaven). A Confucian virtue, the act of recognizing and honoring all goodness received throughout one's life. The deepest gratitude word.

e: to reform through moral influence; to transform with virtue
d: 感 gǎn + 化 huà (to transform; to convert). To touch someone's heart so deeply they are morally transformed. A key Confucian concept: the ideal ruler governs by exemplary virtue; his presence alone 感化s those around him.

e: deeply grateful; moved by another's kindness
d: 感 gǎn + 激 jī (to stir; to agitate; rapids, turbulent water). The heart stirred up by a significant kindness. Implies emotional debt that moves you. Stronger than 感谢; use for meaningful help, not everyday thanks.

感 gǎn + 觉 jué (to awaken; become aware; originally: waking from sleep, the first moment of consciousness). A dual-category word that functions as both verb and noun. The most flexible word in the 感 family. Covers gut feeling, subjective impression, intuition.

When a perception verb (看 kàn, 听 tīng, 吃 chī, 闻 wén, 用 yòng, 做 zuò) is followed by 起来 and then an adjective, the meaning is: "judging by [sense] / when you [sense] it, [it is adj]." This is one of the most common patterns in spoken Mandarin for expressing impressions and evaluations.

e: bittersweet swell of emotion; to sigh with feeling
d: 感 gǎn + 慨 kǎi (to sigh; to lament; a person exhaling with grief). The bittersweet wave felt when contemplating time, change, and transience: the specific ache of things passing. Quintessentially literary. Common in memoirs, essays, and poetry.

e: cold; flu; to catch a cold
d: 感 gǎn + 冒 mào (to emit; to brave recklessly). In traditional Chinese medicine, illness = pathogenic qì 气 entering the body. 感冒 = receiving and being overcome by wind-cold 风寒.
