师 shī (teacher) + 父 fù (father). A master who trains an apprentice in a trade or martial art, addressed with the warmth and deference owed a father. The near-homophone 师傅 shīfu is the everyday term for a skilled worker or driver; 师父 keeps the closer master-disciple bond.

Master , the reliable general-purpose address for service workers and skilled tradespeople. Also the formal term for a craft or trade teacher. The safest default when addressing an unfamiliar adult male in a service or public context.

e: Classic of Poetry · Classic of Documents
d: Two of the Five Classics. 诗经 Shījīng (Classic of Poetry, c. 11th–6th century BCE) , 305 poems, folk songs and court hymns among them; Confucius allegedly edited the collection and praised it as the foundation of literary education.

e: a line of verse; lines of poetry
d: 诗 shī (poem) + 句 jù (line). A line or verse of poetry, the unit a poem is built and quoted in: 优美的诗句 "beautiful lines of verse." Often used in the plural sense, the lines of a poem taken together.
Sage Poet: honorific for Du Fu, whose verse embodied moral gravity and historical witness.
Immortal Poet: honorific for Li Bai, whose verse seemed to transcend ordinary human craft.
To carry out construction: "execute the work." The word on every fence and detour sign. 施工中 means "under construction," on streets and, borrowed, on websites.

十 shí (ten) + 二 èr (two). The separator apostrophe in pinyin marks the syllable boundary: shí·èr, not shí·ér. Twelve is culturally loaded: 十二生肖 shí'èr shēngxiào (the twelve zodiac animals) and 十二个月 shí'èr gè yuè (twelve months) both run on this number.

e: the Twelve Muqam — Uyghur classical music tradition
d: The Twelve Muqam (木卡姆 mùkǎmǔ, from Arabic maqam, meaning mode/scale) is the comprehensive musical tradition of the Uyghur people: twelve suites, each a multi-movement composition comprising song, instrumental interlude, and dance, totaling hundreds of pieces.

十 shí (ten; complete) + 分 fēn (part; portion; to divide). Ten out of ten parts: the full measure of something. The most natural intensifier in formal and written Mandarin, sitting between 很 hěn (colloquial "very") and 非常 fēicháng (extremely, emphatic).
十 shí (ten) + 干 gān (stem; heavenly stem). The cycle of ten: 甲 jiǎ, 乙 yǐ, 丙 bǐng, 丁 dīng, 戊 wù, 己 jǐ, 庚 gēng, 辛 xīn, 壬 rén, 癸 guǐ.

十 shí + 年 nián (year). A decade. In Chinese cultural memory, ten years functions as the basic unit of historical reckoning: the Cultural Revolution lasted "ten years" (1966-1976, the 十年浩劫 shínián hàojié , ten-year catastrophe); a generation is roughly one decade; the proverb 十年树木，百年树人 places educati…

e: eight or nine times out of ten; most probably
d: 十 (ten) + 有 (have) + 八九 (eight or nine). Out of every ten, eight or nine, hence almost always, in all likelihood. A common way to state strong probability: 这件事十有八九是真的, "this is most probably true." The form 十之八九 (eight or nine out of ten) is equivalent.

十 shí + 月 yuè (moon; month). The standard Mandarin name for October and for the tenth month of any lunar calendar. Chinese month names are purely numerical: 一月 through 十二月, January through December. The naming system makes 十月 the last single-digit-ten month before 十一月 (November) and 十二月 (December).

十字 shízì (cross shape) + 路 lù (road) + 口 kǒu (opening; mouth). The point where two roads cross to form the shape of 十: a four-way intersection. Widely used both literally (traffic intersections) and metaphorically (a crossroads in life, a moment of decision between multiple paths).
石 shí (stone) + 头 tou (suffix). The everyday word for a stone or rock. The bare 石 survives mostly in compounds and set terms; 石头 is the word you say out loud.

e: the spirit of the age; the zeitgeist
d: The defining outlook and values of an era, the calque that matches the German "Zeitgeist." 时代 (the age) plus 精神 (spirit). Used in cultural and political commentary to name what an age believes about itself: 把握时代精神 ("grasp the spirit of the times").

e: the right moment; timing; an opportune occasion
d: 时 shí (time) + 机 jī (machine; pivot; crucial moment; opportunity). 时机 is the Confucian classical meaning of 时 made into a compound: the moment that is ripe, when conditions align. It is strategic time, the narrowing window before it closes.

e: the plain future: tomorrow I go
d: A future time word with a bare verb is complete and idiomatic: 我明天去上海 (I'm going to Shanghai tomorrow), 下个月放假 (vacation starts next month). No marker is required at all.

When the focused element is a time expression, it appears directly after 是. This answers the implicit question "when?" about a past event both parties know occurred. The event itself is not in question , only its timing is being asserted.

e: timely centrality; acting appropriately for the moment

d: 实 shí (true) + 话 huà (words; speech). Words that match the facts, plainly told: 说实话 "to tell the truth," also a set phrase "to be honest." Its opposite is 假话 jiǎhuà (a lie).
Inviting candour removes the face cost of a no. Say early that you prefer bad news now to surprises later; engineers in particular will take you up on it.

实 shí (real) + 际 jì (juncture; situation). The actual state of things as opposed to the theoretical: 实际情况 "the actual situation," 实际上 "actually, in fact." Of a person, 很实际 means practical and realistic.
实 shí (actual) + 践 jiàn (to tread; to carry out). The doing that turns an idea into action and tests it against reality: 理论与实践 "theory and practice," 实践证明 "practice has proven."

e: to realize; to bring about; to achieve
d: 实 shí (real) + 现 xiàn (to appear; to manifest). To make something real, to turn a plan, goal, or dream into an accomplished fact: 实现目标 "to achieve a goal," 实现梦想 "to make a dream come true."

e: to put into practice; to implement (a policy, a system)
d: 实 shí (real; actual) + 行 xíng. To act on for real. Distinguished from 进行 (to be in the process of) by emphasis on real-world implementation: 实行新政策 "implement a new policy"; 实行改革 "carry out reforms."
Experiment: to test against reality. 做实验 is to run an experiment; 实验室 is the laboratory; 实验中学 is the "experimental high school" found in nearly every Chinese city.

实 shí (real) + 在 zài (to be present). As an adverb it intensifies: 实在太累了 "I'm really exhausted." As an adjective it describes someone solid and unpretentious: 这个人很实在 "this person is genuine and reliable."
食 shí (to eat; food) + 物 wù (thing). Food as a category of substance, the general written term: 健康食物 "healthy food." For "a meal" you would say 饭 fàn, and for cooked dishes 菜 cài.

e: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 94 BCE)
d: 史 (historical record) + 记 (to record; to note). The foundational work of Chinese historiography, written by Sima Qian (司马迁, c. 145–86 BCE) over decades and completed after his castration by order of Emperor Wu of Han.

史 (historical record) + 料 (materials; raw material , the same 料 as in 材料 cáiliào, material/ingredient). 史料 refers to primary source materials: documents, inscriptions, court records, archaeological finds , the raw evidence from which historical accounts are constructed.

史 (historical record) + 书 (book; written text). The classical compound for historical writings, used in literary and academic contexts. 史书记载 (shǐshū jìzǎi, "according to historical records") is a standard phrase for citing the written tradition.
使 (to make, to set going) + 坏 (bad). To deliberately make trouble for someone behind their back, to pull a malicious prank or sabotage on the sly.

使 shǐ (to send; to cause; an envoy) + 命 mìng (mandate). The mandate one is sent to fulfill, a mission or calling. 使命感 shǐmìnggǎn = sense of mission (the felt conviction that one has a purpose to fulfill).

e: to use; to employ; to make use of
d: 使 shǐ (to cause; to employ; to dispatch) + 用 yòng (to use). The formal, neutral verb for using a tool, a resource, a method, or a right. Appropriate in written and professional contexts. More deliberate in tone than plain 用: where 用 is the bare act, 使用 implies purposeful, authorized deployment.

e: generations; for generations; from age to age
d: 世 shì (generation) + 代 dài (generation, era). The succession of generations taken together: 世代相传 "handed down through the generations," 世代务农 "farming for generations." Often adverbial, meaning across the whole line of descent.

世 shì (age) + 纪 jì (a record; a span of years). A hundred-year stretch of time: 二十一世纪 "the twenty-first century," 半个世纪 "half a century," 跨世纪 "spanning the turn of the century." The standard unit for dividing modern history.

Thirty chapters on the feudal lords and hereditary houses of the Zhou and after. Notably, Sima Qian placed 孔子 Confucius among the 世家, treating an uncrowned teacher as the equal of princes because of his lasting influence, an early statement that cultural authority can outweigh political rank.

e: the world of sentient beings; this life; among the world
d: More literary than 世界, similar in range to 人间, but cooler and more doctrinally precise in Buddhist usage. Appears in classical compounds: 出世间 (transcending this world), 世间法 (the dharmas of this world, as opposed to transcendent dharma), 世间万象 (the ten thousand phenomena of this world).

世 shì (the living age) + 界 jiè (boundary; realm). The world as a whole, both the physical globe and the human sphere within it: 全世界 "the whole world," 世界和平 "world peace," 世界观 "worldview." One of the most common nouns in the language.

e: first in the world; the world's best
d: 世界 shìjiè (world) + 第一 dì-yī (first). The top of a global ranking, by extension the finest there is. Used of athletes, products, and achievements that lead the field.

世 shì (the human world) + 俗 sú (custom; common). What belongs to ordinary worldly life rather than the religious or ideal: 世俗社会 "secular society," 世俗的眼光 "a worldly point of view." Can describe the secular as a neutral domain or carry a mild note of the common and unrefined.

世 shì (generation) + 袭 xí (to inherit; to succeed to). Passed down by birth from one generation to the next: 世袭制度 "the hereditary system," 世袭爵位 "a hereditary title." Marks a right or rank inherited through bloodline rather than earned or appointed.
Market, in both senses: the physical 菜市场 (vegetable market) and the abstract 市场经济 (market economy). 市场部 is the marketing department.

e: market economy — what China was moving toward
d: 市场 (market, literally marketplace) + 经济 (economy). The conceptual opposite of 计划经济 jìhuà jīngjì (planned economy, the command economy the PRC had used since 1949).

e: to show; to indicate; to reveal

d: 事 (shì, matter, affair, event) + 故 (cause, the reason behind it). An accident or untoward incident: literally an event with a cause, usually an unwanted one. 交通事故 (jiāotōng shìgù) is a traffic accident; 安全事故 (ānquán shìgù) is a safety incident.

e: a Zhuge Liang after the fact; hindsight wisdom
matter; affair; thing (to be dealt with)
d: 事 shì + 情 qíng (situation; circumstance). The everyday noun for a matter or affair, anything happening that you talk about or handle. The most common way to say "thing" when you mean a situation rather than an object.

Wang Yangming's insistence that moral cultivation is not a retreat into contemplation but a process that occurs within engagement with actual affairs. The battlefield, the courtroom, the family, the market , all are sites where 良知 is extended or blocked.

e: fact; the actual state of affairs
d: 事 shì + 实 shí (real; solid). The matter as it really is, a fact. The phrase 事实上 shìshí shàng means "in fact, actually," used to correct an impression or introduce the truth of a case.

e: beforehand; in advance; prior to the event
d: 事 shì + 先 xiān (before; first). Before the matter happens, in advance. Its mirror is 事后 shìhòu (afterward), so the pair frames an event as before-and-after.

事 shì (matter; affair) + 业 yè (undertaking). The cause or career one commits to, larger and more aspirational than a job: 事业心 "career ambition," 教育事业 "the cause of education." To 干一番事业 is to accomplish something lasting with one's life.
Running the new tool for the first time. Rounds are numbered T1, T2, T3, said as letters plus Chinese numbers (T一, T二). Each round produces parts to measure; the goal is to stop modifying.

e: is it or isn't it? · right? (A-not-A question / tag)
d: The A-not-A question form of 是 , a canonical Chinese question-formation strategy. Verb + 不 + Verb creates a yes-no question with slightly more rhetorical directness than a rising-intonation question. 是不是 also functions as a sentence-final tag question: 你也去，是不是？ ("You're going too, right?").

e: yes; that's right; indeed (affirming something just said)
d: 是的 in its collapsed, fully reduced form is simply an affirmation: "yes, that is the case." The 是 confirms the truth of what was said; the 的 creates a sense of definitiveness or "that's just how it is." It is warmer and more emphatic than a bare 对, and more measured than an enthusiastic 当然.

e: right and wrong; the rights and wrongs; trouble; gossip
d: 是 shì (right; this; is) + 非 fēi (wrong). The pairing of right and wrong as a single notion: 明辨是非 "to clearly distinguish right from wrong." By a common slide it also means the quarrels and gossip that arise from disputes: 惹是非 "to stir up trouble."

e: the heart of right and wrong — sprout of 智 wisdom
d: 是非 shì fēi: right and wrong, approval and disapproval. The capacity to distinguish correct from incorrect actions , not just in oneself (羞恶之心) but in the world in general. The sprout of 智 zhì (moral wisdom , knowing how to act rightly in complex situations).

p: shìfēi zhī xīn, zhì zhī duān yě
e: The heart of right and wrong is the beginning of wisdom
d: Mencius, 孟子·公孙丑上. 是非 shìfēi = right and wrong (是 shì = right, correct; 非 fēi = wrong, incorrect). 之心 zhī xīn = the heart of; the feeling for. 端 duān = beginning; germ; tip of something.

是 (yes/right) + 否 fǒu (no; to negate , a classical negative particle). A formal, written-register conjunction meaning "whether or not." The colloquial equivalents are 有没有 or 是不是. 是否 appears in journalism, academic writing, formal correspondence, and polished speech.
"Is that so?" or "really?" Slightly cooler than 真的吗, often signaling polite interest without strong surprise. The neutral acknowledgment that you have heard and registered what was just said.

e: who told you? (FOCUS: which agent, unknown)
d: The agent-focus question: 是谁 + Verb + 的. Both speakers know that someone told this person something , the unknown is who. 谁 occupies the focus position between 是 and the verb phrase. This is one of the most natural everyday uses of 是…的: interrogating the agent of a known past action.

"Oh, so it's like that." A softer, gentler version of 原来如此. The 啊 particle gives it a reflective, taking-it-in quality. Useful when someone has just shared something personal or explained a situation.
适 shì (to suit) + 当 dàng (to fit). Describes a measure, amount, or action that is right for the situation: 适当的时候 (at an appropriate time), 适当休息 (rest as appropriate).

e: to suit; to be suited to; to fit
d: 适 shì (to be apt) + 合 hé (to fit). A verb taking an object: X 适合 Y means X suits Y. 这本书适合孩子 "this book is suited to children."

e: to adapt; to get used to; to suit
d: 适 shì (to suit) + 应 yìng (to respond, to meet). To adjust oneself to new circumstances: 适应环境 (adapt to the environment), 适应新工作 (get used to a new job). The response here is the slow one of fitting in over time.

e: that which passes; the departed; what flows away
d: 逝 (to pass; to depart; to flow away) + 者. A thing-nominalization rather than a person-nominalization , 者 here points to an event or process rather than a human agent. This usage shows the full range of 者: it nominalizes any predicate, not just those describing human beings.
The standard acknowledgement. 好的 (hǎo de) is "okay," 明白 (míngbai) "understood," 收到，谢谢 the polite version. Acknowledging promptly is expected; silence reads as a problem.

Two demonic generals, 千里眼 Qiānlǐyǎn (Eyes That See a Thousand Li, a green-faced demon) and 顺风耳 Shùnfēng'ěr (Ears That Hear Downwind, a red-faced demon), terrorized the coastal people. Lin Mo defeated them in combat through her superior spiritual power, converting them to her service.

e: wristwatch: a watch worn on the wrist (錶 in traditional script)
d: 手 shǒu (hand; wrist) + 表 biǎo (here the instrument sense, written 錶 in traditional script). A wristwatch. This is the sense that traditional writing marks with the metal radical (錶), since a watch is a metal device whose face displays a reading. Simplified Chinese writes it 表.

手 shǒu (hand) + 机 jī (machine). China's most common word for mobile phone , the machine held in the hand. Completely replaced the earlier 手提电话 and the formal 移动电话 in everyday usage. 玩手机 wán shǒujī = "to play on one's phone" (ubiquitous activity).

e: A small gift brought back from travel
d: A small gift brought back from travel: a souvenir or local specialty given to family, friends, or colleagues on return from a trip. The term is particularly common in Cantonese-speaking areas and in Hong Kong. The expectation of bringing 手信 from any notable journey is near-universal.

手 (hand) + 足 (foot). The literal limbs of the body, used figuratively for brothers or close companions. Classical Chinese: 手足之情 (shǒuzú zhī qíng, the feeling between hands and feet) means brotherly affection , your siblings are as necessary to you as your own hands and feet.

e: to defend the realm; to hold and preserve what was won
d: 守 shǒu (to guard; to protect; to hold steady , the character shows a hand over a roof, the posture of protection) + 江山. The harder and longer task: not the dramatic moment of conquest but the slow, unglamorous work of governing, maintaining order, and preventing the realm from unraveling.

e: conservative; set in old ways; resistant to change
d: 守 (shǒu, to guard, to hold onto , a hand over a roof) + 旧 (old). To guard the old order against change. In Chinese political and social discourse since the late Qing dynasty, 守旧 has been the standard term of criticism for those who resist modernization or reform.

e: the first time; for the first time
d: 首 shǒu (first) + 次 cì (time, occurrence). The first occasion on which something happens, common in news and formal writing. 首次访问 "a first visit," 首次公开 "made public for the first time." More formal than the spoken 第一次 dì-yī cì.

首 shǒu (head, chief) + 都 dū (metropolis, city). The head-city of a country, its seat of government. 中国的首都是北京 "China's capital is Beijing." Note the reading: here 都 takes its first tone dū (city), not the toneless dōu (all).

首 shǒu (head, chief) + 领 lǐng (to lead; the neck, the collar). The leader of a tribe, band, or organization. Carries a slightly traditional or martial flavor: the chief of a clan, the head of an outfit. 部落首领 "a tribal chieftain."

e: first of all; firstly; in the first place
d: 首 shǒu (first) + 先 xiān (before, prior). The standard opener for an ordered list of points, often paired later with 其次 qícì (next) and 最后 zuìhòu (finally). Marks the very first item in a sequence of reasons, steps, or arguments.

e: prime minister (of a modern foreign government)
d: 首 shǒu (head; chief) + 相 xiàng (minister). The modern title for the head of government in countries such as Britain and Japan: 英国首相 "the British Prime Minister."

首 shǒu (first) + 要 yào (important). Marking the single most important matter, ranking above all others. 首要任务 "the primary task," 首要问题 "the chief problem." Stronger and more formal than 重要 zhòngyào (important), since it claims the top spot, not just high rank.

e: life-span; lifetime; (of a thing) durability, service life
d: 寿 shòu (longevity; long life) plus 命. The measured length of a life. Used both for living beings (人均寿命 "average human life-span") and, by extension, for objects (机器的寿命 "the service life of a machine").

e: can't stand it; unbearable; past one's limit
d: 受 shòu (to endure; to receive) + 不了 liǎo (cannot complete the action of enduring). The potential complement with 不了 means the action cannot reach completion , endurance hits its limit. One of the most frequently used expressions in daily speech for frustration, exhaustion, or overwhelm.

书 shū + 本 běn (root; copy; the original volume). The physical book as an object. Often used in the contrast 书本知识 (book knowledge) vs. 实践 (practice) , a tension that runs through Chinese educational discourse.

书法 shūfǎ + 家 jiā (specialist; master of a domain). A practitioner of calligraphy at the level of mastery. 王羲之 Wáng Xīzhī (4th c.) is the canonical master; his 兰亭序 Lántíng Xù (Preface to the Orchid Pavilion) is the most celebrated piece of Chinese calligraphy.
书 (shū, books) plus 房. The room set aside for reading and writing. In the scholar's house it was the heart of the home, lined with 书 and the four treasures of the study (brush, ink, paper, inkstone).

p: shū ràng tā ná zǒu le
e: the book was taken away by him (colloquial 让 passive)
d: 让 ràng as passive marker: Subject + 让 + Agent + Verb + Result. Equivalent to 书被他拿走了, but more colloquial. 让 feels more spoken, lighter in register. Common across Mandarin dialects and in casual conversation. Note that 让 can also mean "let/allow" , context disambiguates.
Sage of Calligraphy: the title given to Wang Xizhi.

e: the book was borrowed by him (FOCUS: by him, not by someone else)
d: Agent focus: who performed the known action. The agent (他) is placed between 是 and the verb + 的. Both speakers know the book was borrowed , the question or point of emphasis is who borrowed it. This is also how 是…的 can function like a passive: the book (subject) + 是 + agent + verb + 的.

The seven warring states had developed their own variant scripts. Qin imposed the small seal script (小篆 xiǎozhuàn) as the official form throughout the empire, with prime minister Li Si (李斯) overseeing the standardization.

e: study; book room; a small library or bookshop
d: 书 shū + 屋 wū (room; small dwelling). A room given over to books , intimate, personal, unlarge. The word appears in study names of scholars and poets: 鲁迅的百草园 is a garden; his workroom was a 书屋. It is also the second half of this site's name: 角落書屋.

e: to grow distant from; to drift apart; estranged
d: 疏 shū (loose; scattered; infrequent; originally: a channel that has grown shallow) + 远 yuǎn (far). The channel of a relationship silting up, the contact thinning until the other person feels far away. Can be transitive (to push someone away deliberately) or intransitive (to drift apart gradually).
蔬 shū (vegetables) + 菜 cài (greens). The formal, category word for vegetables as a food group, the term you see on nutrition labels and in recipes: 多吃蔬菜 "eat more vegetables."
熟 (cooked, ripe, familiar) + 练 (drilled). The same 熟 used for cooked food: a skill drilled until it is done, no longer raw. Describes a practiced, effortless command of a task.
To belong to a zodiac sign , 你属什么？(nǐ shǔ shénme?) "What sign are you?" The verb for stating your zodiac animal.
Zodiac sign, literally "belonging-image." The colloquial word for your zodiac animal, used in everyday speech.

e: to belong to; to be part of; to fall under
d: 属 shǔ (to be subordinate to) + 于 yú (to). States membership or ownership: 这本书属于我 "this book belongs to me," 鲸鱼属于哺乳动物 "whales belong to the mammals."

e: Shu Han — the southwest, the legitimist cause
d: Founded in 221 by 刘备 Liu Bei, a distant relative of the Han imperial house who claimed to be restoring, not replacing, the dynasty (hence Shu Han, 蜀汉).

e: quantity: the amount or number of something
d: 数 shù (number) + 量 liàng (amount). The neutral, countable "how many / how much" of a thing. 数量 answers questions of scale and stock: how many units, how large a supply.
Mathematics: number-study. 数学家 (shùxuéjiā) is a mathematician; 数学课 (shùxué kè) is math class, the collocation every student uses daily.
Number, numeral, digit. The everyday word for a figure, whether spoken, written, or on a screen. 数字化 (shùzìhuà) extends it to "digitization," the same move English made with "digit."
4 (四 sì) , inauspicious; sounds like 死 sǐ (death). Buildings skip floor 4, hospitals avoid room 4. 8 (八 bā) , extremely auspicious; sounds like 发 fā (prosper). License plates with 8s sell at premium.
帅 (handsome) + 哥. A good-looking young man, and also a friendly way to flag down any young man whose name you don't know, the male counterpart of 美女 (měinǚ).

e: to swish (meat through hot liquid); to shabu

d: 双 shuāng (pair; double) + 重 chóng (layer). Two layers of the same thing: 双重标准 "double standard," 双重身份 "dual identity." Here 重 is the layer-counting chóng.

The bank's proof that you sent the money, also 汇款水单. The factory will ask for it the moment you say you have paid, and production often waits for it. Send it promptly; it is the fastest way to start the lead-time clock.

Water-ground tone , the smooth, polished vocal style developed by Wei Liangfu that defines 昆曲 singing. The metaphor refers to the way stone is ground by water to a perfect smoothness. Characterized by slow tempos, elaborate ornamentation, and seamless melodic flow.

e: ink wash; water-and-ink; the classical Chinese painting medium
d: 水 shuǐ (water) + 墨 mò (ink , a slab of compressed carbon pigment, dissolved in water to create the medium). The classical Chinese painting medium: ink dissolved in varying concentrations of water, applied with a brush to paper or silk to create images through gradations of tone from dark to light.

e: level; standard; horizontal; one's degree of proficiency
d: 水 shuǐ (water) + 平 píng (level; flat; equal). A water surface is perfectly level , the universal measure of flatness and standards. From this physical fact, 水平 became the word for any standard of quality or proficiency.

e: water benefits all things; the Daoist image of yielding

d: Water sleeves: the long white silk extensions attached to the costume sleeves of major 昆曲 characters.
Sleep + not + take-hold, with 着 in its zháo reading. The 3 a.m. word, and the proof that the complement is about achieving a result: you can 睡 (lie down to sleep) all night and never 睡着.

"By the way." Marks an aside or a piece of side information that occurs to you mid-conversation. 顺便 literally means "in passing." The English equivalent fits cleanly. Often shortened in casual speech to just 顺便.
"While I'm at it, let me ask…" Lets you slide an unrelated question into the conversation without it feeling like an interruption. Pairs naturally with 顺便说一下 (the side-remark version).

e: an instant; the blink of an eye
d: 瞬 shùn (a blink) + 间 jiān (interval). The smallest interval of time, the moment it takes to blink: 一瞬间 "in a flash." The interval shrunk almost to nothing.

说 shuō + 不定 (cannot be fixed/determined). Means "cannot be stated with certainty," i.e., maybe, possibly. One of the most natural hedges in spoken Mandarin. More casual and spoken than 也许 yěxǔ or 可能 kěnéng.

e: to say out; to speak out; to voice (what was held inside)
d: 说 shuō (speak; say) + 出 (emergence complement). To bring words out from an interior state into speech: what was private, unspoken, or held back becomes expressed.

e: to mention; to come to (a topic); speaking of
d: 说 shuō (to speak) + 到 dào (arrive at). Speech that arrives at its topic: to come around to mentioning something, to bring something up. 说到这里 (at this point, speaking of this) is a common transitional phrase in both speech and writing.

e: "Speaking of which" or "since you mention it
d: "Speaking of which" or "since you mention it." Pivots to a related topic that the previous remark suggested. Cleaner than 对了 when the connection is more thematic than associative.

说 shuō (to say; to speak) + 道 dào (way; to say). A literary verb used in fiction and formal narrative to introduce direct speech. Written as X说道，"……" (X said, "……"). Seldom appears in casual spoken Chinese; it marks elevated or written register.
"Well said" or "you're right." Compliments the rightness of what was just said. Slightly more formal than 没错; acknowledges the other person's reasoning, not just the conclusion.
说 shuō + 服 fú (to submit; to be convinced; to be at someone's service). To speak until someone submits, to persuade successfully. The complement 服 marks the result: the persuasion worked.

e: to speak; to talk; to say something
d: 说 shuō (to say) + 话 huà (words). The everyday verb for speaking, formed as verb-plus-object: literally "to say words." Because 话 is already the object, you do not say 说话一件事; to speak about something you use 说 alone: 说一件事.
说 shuō (to say) + 几 jǐ (a few) + 句 jù (measure word). To make a few brief remarks, the polite formula a speaker uses before a short toast or comment: 我想说几句 "I would like to say a few words."

p: shuō le bàn tiān cái míngbai
e: finally understood after talking for ages
d: After a long period of effort, explanation, or struggle , 才 finally. The effort is encoded in the first clause (说了半天 = talked for half a day, idiom for "a long time"); the 才 marks that only after all that effort did the result occur. This is 才 at its most expressive: hard-won achievement.
Lead with 不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi, "excuse me") to soften it. Most people slow down for one sentence and then speed back up; asking twice is fine.

e: to explain; to illustrate; explanation; instructions
d: 说 shuō + 明 míng (clear, bright). To make something clear through speech. As a noun: 说明书 shuōmíngshū = instruction manual. As a verb: 这说明了… = "this demonstrates/shows that…"

"To tell the truth" or "honestly." Signals that what follows is candid, sometimes uncomfortably so. Often used before a confession, an admission, or a frank criticism. The English "honestly" works as a direct translation.

e: Explaining Simple and Analyzing Compound Characters

p: shuō zhe shuō zhe tā kū le
e: as she kept talking, she started to cry
d: The model sentence for this pattern. The action (talking) repeated in the V + 着 frame signals continuation; the main clause introduces the unplanned outcome (crying). Used whenever a shift happened gradually, through sustained activity, not at a discrete moment.

e: to think carefully; to reflect; to consider
d: 思 sī (to think; thought) + 考 kǎo (to examine; to investigate; to test). Deliberate, directed thinking. 思考 is the most common everyday word for careful, intentional mental activity , the kind of thinking you do when you have a problem in front of you and are genuinely working through it.

e: train of thought; line of reasoning; thinking process
d: 思 sī (thought) + 路 lù (road; path; route). Lit. "the road of thought." The direction and movement of how thinking unfolds , not the conclusion but the path that leads there. 思路清晰 (a clear line of reasoning) is high praise in Chinese academic and professional contexts.

e: to miss; to think of with longing; to yearn for
d: 思 sī (to think; to miss) + 念 niàn (to think of; to read aloud; to remember , itself containing 心 in its lower half). The compound that doubles the weight. 思念 is used specifically for people , loved ones who are far away, people who have died, a home one has left.

e: Confucius's single-phrase summary of the entire 诗经
d: Confucius's single-phrase summary of the entire 诗经: "thoughts without depravity" or "sincere in thought." The phrase became the canonical statement of the anthology's moral purpose.

思 sī (to miss; to long for) + 乡 xiāng (hometown; native place; countryside). Lit. "to miss the home place." Homesickness as a deliberate, named condition , not vague discomfort but a specific directional longing, pointing back to the place of origin.

思 sī (to think; thought) + 想 xiǎng (to think; to want; idea). Thought as a formed body , both personal and systematic. 思想 operates on two levels. At the personal level it describes someone's habitual way of thinking, their mental orientation or values: 思想开放 (open-minded , lit. "open thought").

e: to give up; to let hope die
the Sichuan Basin — the geography that produced this cuisine's ingredients and intensity
d: The Sichuan Basin , the large inland depression enclosed by mountains on all sides. 盆 means "basin" or "bowl"; 地 means "land" or "ground." The shape of a basin (四面环山 sì miàn huán shān, "mountains on all four sides") is the defining geographic fact of the region.

e: the Four Beauties of ancient China

d: 四 sì + 大 dà (great) + 名著 míngzhù (famous work). The four canonical novels of Chinese literature: Romance of the Three Kingdoms (三国演义), Water Margin (水浒传), Journey to the West (西游记), and Dream of the Red Chamber (红楼梦).

e: the four directions; all around; everywhere
d: 四 sì + 方 fāng (direction; side; square). Literally the four cardinal directions, and by extension every direction, all around. 四面八方 sìmiàn bāfāng ("four faces, eight directions") intensifies it to mean from every conceivable side. A 四方形 sìfāngxíng is a square or quadrilateral, the four-sided shape.

e: the four seas; the whole country; the entire world
d: 四 sì + 海 hǎi (sea). The four seas thought to bound the inhabited world, hence the whole realm, everywhere under heaven. 四海之内皆兄弟 ("within the four seas all men are brothers"), from the Analects, is one of the most quoted lines on universal kinship.

四 sì + 季 jì (season). Spring (春 chūn), summer (夏 xià), autumn (秋 qiū), winter (冬 dōng). 四季如春 sìjì rú chūn ("four seasons like spring") describes a mild climate where it feels like spring all year, a stock phrase of praise for places such as Kunming.
The "four-nine city": a colloquial name for old Beijing, referring to its four inner city gates and nine outer city gates. A marker of old Beijing nostalgia and native identity.

e: the Four Olds (ideas, culture, customs, habits)

d: Four Gentlemen: the four emblematic plants of the literati painting tradition: prunus plum 梅 (perseverance), orchid 兰 (secluded virtue), bamboo 竹 (resilience), chrysanthemum 菊 (dignified retirement). Together they map the principal Confucian virtues onto natural forms.

Four temperatures and five flavors: the two-axis system for classifying drug properties. The four temperatures: cold (寒), cool (凉), warm (温), hot (热). The five flavors: sour (酸), bitter (苦), sweet (甘), pungent (辛), salty (咸). Each flavor has specific organ affinities and physiological effects.
四 sì (four) + 声 shēng (tone). The four-way tone system of standard Mandarin: high-level, rising, dipping, and falling. The neutral tone 轻声 is counted separately.

四 sì + 书 shū (book). The Great Learning (大学), the Doctrine of the Mean (中庸), the Analects (论语), and the Mencius (孟子). Selected and grouped by the Song scholar Zhu Xi as the core Confucian curriculum, the Four Books became the basis of the imperial examination system for centuries.

The Four Symbols: the four mythological animal guardians of the cardinal directions: Azure Dragon (east, spring), Vermilion Bird (south, summer), White Tiger (west, autumn), Black Tortoise (north, winter).

e: Buddhist temple architecture — the visual language of Chinese Buddhism
d: The Chinese Buddhist temple complex (寺 sì or 寺庙 sìmiào) follows a distinctive axial layout: the main gate (山门 shānmén, "mountain gate," the formal Buddhist term for the entrance), then the Hall of Heavenly Kings 天王殿 (with the four directional guardians), then the main hall 大雄宝殿 (the Great Hero's Hal…

e: released; unbound — the key quality sought in practice
Song lyric poetry; the classical 词 of the Song
d: 宋 Sòng (the Song) + 词 cí (lyric). The lyric-poem form at its height, written to set tune-patterns and meant to be sung. Paired with 唐诗 Táng shī, Tang regulated verse, as one of the high points of classical poetry.
The clerk turned outlaw chief, nicknamed 及时雨 ("Timely Rain") for his open-handed generosity, who becomes the band's leader.
送 (see off) plus 别 (to part). A literary, emotionally weighted word for the moment of parting, the subject of countless Tang poems written at the roadside or the river crossing.
送 (send) plus 达 (reach, arrive). A formal verb stressing successful arrival, used for delivered mail and, in law, for serving legal documents.
送 (give) plus 给 (to, for the benefit of). The recipient-marking pattern: 送给 + person + thing. The thing crosses over and stays with the receiver.

e: soul guiding — escorting the dead to the afterlife
d: 送魂 (guiding the soul , lit. "sending the soul") is the funerary function of the shaman: after death, the soul of the deceased may be disoriented, confused about its condition, or unable to find the path to the spirit world.
送 (send) plus 货 (goods). Door-to-door delivery: the courier who 送货 to your home, the staple verb of online shopping and takeout.
送 (give) plus 礼 (gift, ritual courtesy). A separable verb-object pair for the social act of presenting a present, with all the etiquette that surrounds it in Chinese life.

e: to see someone off (on a journey)
d: 送 (see off) plus 行 (to travel, set out). To go to the station, dock, or airport to bid a traveler farewell as they begin a journey.

e: child-giving Guanyin — the form prayed to for fertility and safe birth
d: 送 sòng (to send, to give) + 子 zǐ (child) + 观音. The most commonly petitioned form of Guanyin outside formal temple Buddhism. Depicted holding a child, or seated with children around her, this iconographic type is the primary focus of domestic devotion in households hoping for a child.
Acid; sour. One word covers the chemical class and the taste, plus muscle soreness (腿酸, sore legs) and the sting of envy (心里酸酸的). Chemistry students never forget which taste an acid has.

Counting rods: the predecessor to the suanpan. Small bamboo, bone, or ivory sticks arranged in patterns on a flat surface to represent numbers in a base-10 positional system. Used in China from at least the Warring States period (475–221 BCE) through the Tang dynasty.

e: to tell fortunes; to calculate one's fate
d: 算 suàn (to calculate) plus 命. The phrase reveals the cultural assumption: a 命 is something that can be computed. Given the year, month, day, and hour of birth (生辰八字 shēngchén bāzì, "the eight characters of birth"), a fortune-teller can read out the trajectory.
The abacus, literally "calculating tray." The standard Chinese bead-frame instrument with 2 upper beads and 5 lower beads per rod, in use in its canonical form since at least the 16th century.
虽 suī (although) + 然 rán (so). Opens a concession and almost always pairs with 但是 dànshì or 可是 kěshì in the second clause: 虽然 ... 但是 ... "although ..., yet ...".

e: casual essay; jottings as you go

d: As you like, freely, casually , the softer alternative to 干杯 that allows the recipient to drink as much or as little as they wish. Using 随意 rather than 干杯 is a show of consideration, often offered to guests who are known to drink little or who have already flagged a limitation.

e: Sun Wukong — the Monkey King, the protector
d: The brilliant, fearless, impatient monkey whose magic and loyalty carry the party through every peril. He sees through every demon's disguise (with his 火眼金睛, fiery golden eyes) and fights when the monk cannot.

e: Sun Yat-sen, father of the republic
The Art of War — the foundational Chinese military text
d: Attributed to 孙武 Sūn Wǔ of the state of Wu (late Spring and Autumn / early Warring States). Thirteen chapters on strategy, deception, terrain, and the nature of victory.

e: that which is loved; the one one loves
that which is seen; what one sees
the words spoken; what was said
so-called; what is called; what people call

d: 所 (that which) + 以 (the means/reason by which). The most common consequential conjunction in modern Chinese. Follows a cause clause (often introduced by 因为) and introduces the result: 因为下雨，所以我没去 (because it rained, so I did not go).

所 suǒ (that which; a place; nominalizing particle) + 有 (have/exist). 所有 as a determiner: 所有的学生 (all the students). As a noun: 他失去了所有 (He lost everything he had). As a formal possession compound in legal/written Chinese: 所有权 suǒyǒuquán = ownership rights, title.

e: all of, the entirety of a set
d: 所有(的) + noun names the complete set up front: 所有的学生都来了 (all the students came). 所有 began as "that which is possessed" (所 + 有, what one has), and the possessive flavor survives in 我所有的钱 (all the money I have).

e: where something is; the location of; what something lies in
d: 所 suǒ (that which; nominalizing particle) + 在 (to be located). A formal noun meaning "the place/point where something is located; the essence of what something consists in." Commonly appears in 问题所在 (the crux of the problem; where the problem lies) and 关键所在 (the key point; where the key lies).

e: that which is known; what one knows
the things done; what was done
he leaves as soon as he comes back (no pause between)
d: When 就 connects two verbs or clauses, it signals immediate, seamless sequence , the second action follows the first without pause. This is the "as soon as" function: the first event triggers the second instantly. No 一 is needed here , just the bare sequence: Clause 1 + 就 + Clause 2.

e: he got married; he is now a married man
d: Major life transitions , marriage, graduation, birth, death, career changes , are natural territory for sentence-final 了. The 了 frames the event as a change that affects the current situation: the relevant new fact is that he is now married. It answers an implicit question about the present.

p: tāmen shì zài Shànghǎi jiànmiàn de
e: they met in Shanghai (FOCUS: in Shanghai, not elsewhere)
d: Both speakers know they met , the question is where. The 在上海 sits between 是 and 见面的, specifying the location of the known meeting. Common in stories, biographical accounts, and conversations about how relationships began.

e: They are in a meeting right now
d: One of the most useful office and workplace phrases. 开会 kāihuì = to hold/attend a meeting. The progressive here signals that interrupting is not appropriate. Variant: 他们在开会，请稍后再来 (They are in a meeting , please come back later). 正在 gives it a slight formality appropriate to professional contexts.

他 tā (he; other) + 人 rén. The formal and written equivalent of 别人. Appears in legal texts, philosophical writing, ethical discussions, and formal prose. In classical Chinese, 他 itself meant "other" before it was narrowed to the third-person pronoun, making 他人 doubly "other."

e: he didn't marry until thirty (late, in the speaker's view)
d: From the speaker's perspective, thirty is late to marry , perhaps later than expected or social norms dictate.

e: he went by car (FOCUS: by car, not by train, not walking)
d: Manner focus: the verb of transportation or method of doing something sits between 是 and 去的 (or the main verb + 的). The presupposition is that he went somewhere , the new information is how. 开车 (drive a car) is the manner. Other manners: 坐飞机 by plane, 骑车 by bike, 走路 on foot, 打电话 by phone.

e: he came last year (FOCUS: last year, not any other year)
d: Both speakers know he came; the question is when. 是去年 places "last year" in the focus position, bracketed by 是 and …来的. The construction answers a question or corrects a misunderstanding about the timing: "No, it wasn't three years ago, it was last year."

e: he speaks clearly — verb + 得 + degree complement
d: 得 here follows a verb and introduces a complement describing the degree, manner, or result of that action. Think of it as "to the extent that…" or "in a way that…" The complement can be an adjective, another verb, or a clause. This is the most analytically complex use of 得.

p: tā wǔ suì jiù huì dúshū le
e: he was already reading at age five! (impressively early)
d: Age five is the timeline; 就 signals it is earlier than the expected baseline for reading ability. The sentence-final 了 reinforces the new-situation quality , at that point, as early as five, he had already achieved this. The combination 就…了 is extremely common for describing precocious achievements.

e: a strange land; a place away from home

p: tā lái le liǎng gè xīngqī le
e: she has been here for two weeks (and is still here)
d: The double-了 construction with a duration complement is one of its most important uses. The first 了 marks the initial arrival (completed action of coming); the second 了 marks the current relevance , she is still here now. Without the second 了, the sentence implies the visit is concluded.

她 + 们 (men, plural marker). Used only when every member of the group is known to be female. If the group is mixed-gender or the gender is unknown, the default is 他们 (tāmen) , the male-radical form is the unmarked plural.

p: tā shì jīntiān zǎoshang zǒu de
e: she left this morning (FOCUS: this morning, not yesterday)
d: More precise time focus , this morning, as opposed to last night or yesterday. The presupposition is clear: she has already left (both speakers know this). The new information is the precise time of departure. Commonly used in conversations about arrivals, departures, and events.

e: "the 她 character" — shorthand for the gendered-pronoun debate
d: A meta-term in linguistic and feminist writing. 她字之争 ("the dispute over 她") refers to the recurring debate over whether to use 她, abolish it, or replace it with a non-marked alternative.

礻 (the spirit/altar radical, a variant of 示) + 也. Coined later than 她, by Chinese Christian translators of the Bible, to render English "He" (capitalized of God) without committing to the human-male radical 亻. 祂 carries no gender; it carries divinity.

e: spring outing; walking in green countryside
an actor lines; stage dialogue; script lines
d: 台 tái (stage) + 词 cí (words). The lines a performer speaks in a play, film, or show. 背台词 bèi táicí is to learn one lines by heart.
台 (tái, platform, stand) + 灯 (lamp): a lamp that sits on a desk or table, the small pool of light you read and study by.
Typhoon. The Chinese word and the English one echo each other, and scholars still argue over which direction the borrowing ran. Coastal summer news vocabulary.

The Taiwan Strait: the body of water between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland. Used as shorthand for the cross-strait political situation: 台海关系 (cross-strait relations), 台海局势 (Taiwan Strait situation).

e: A step, a staircase , and in face contexts, a way out
d: A step, a staircase , and in face contexts, a way out. 给他一个台阶下 ("give him a step to descend") means to provide a face-saving exit from an awkward position. One of the most useful face-vocabulary phrases in practice.

e: to raise the head; to look up
d: 抬 tái (to lift) + 头 tóu (head). To lift the head and look up, literally or in the sense of holding one's head high after hardship. Its opposite is 低头 dītóu, to lower the head.
太 tài (grand; senior; beyond; supreme) + 后 (empress). The emperor's mother or grandmother who has survived her husband's reign.

e: the Supreme Ultimate; Taiji (the source of yin and yang)
d: 太 tài (supreme) + 极 jí (the pole; the ultimate). In the Yijing tradition, the Supreme Ultimate from which 阴 yīn and 阳 yáng divide. The familiar swirl symbol is the 太极图. The slow martial art is 太极拳 tàijíquán.

e: Tai Chi Chuan — the soft internal martial art based on yin-yang principles
d: 太极 tàijí (the Supreme Ultimate , the cosmological concept) + 拳 quán (fist; boxing style). The soft, circular martial art based on the principles of 阴阳: yielding overcomes force, softness overcomes hardness, stillness overcomes motion. A paradigm of 内功 (internal cultivation).
太 tài (grand) + 空 kōng (void; empty). The "grand void," outer space. 太空人 tàikōngrén and 宇航员 yǔhángyuán both mean astronaut.

e: great peace — the classical political ideal
taking it too seriously; too earnest about it

d: The doubled 太, the senior lady of the house. Used as a title after a surname (王太太 "Mrs. Wang") and as a polite word for one's own or another's wife. The 太 marks seniority and respect.

太 tài (supreme; ultimate; the greatest) + 阳 yáng (yang force; light). The Supreme Yang , the ultimate source of yang energy in the cosmos. In the 五行 framework, the sun is the source of Fire phase energy. 太阳能 (solar energy) uses exactly this logic.
To negotiate; negotiation. Formal register, used for deals and diplomacy alike. Everyday haggling is 讨价还价; you 谈判 a joint venture, you 讨价还价 over a jacket.
Decocted herbal medicine: herbs simmered in water to produce a strong tea. The traditional and most common form of herbal administration, now competing with granules and capsules for convenience.

Thangka: a Tibetan painted or embroidered hanging scroll, used as a devotional object and teaching tool. Thangkas depict deities, mandalas, and scenes from Buddhist narratives. The production of thangkas is a living art form maintained by trained artisans in both Tibet and the exile community.

e: Tang Sanzang — the holy, helpless monk
d: The pilgrim monk, also called 唐三藏, modelled on the historical 玄奘 Xuanzang. He is pure in heart, devout, and utterly committed to his sacred mission, but physically weak and often foolishly compassionate, forever being captured by demons who wish to eat his flesh to gain immortality.

e: to flee; to escape; to run away
d: 逃 (táo, to flee) + 跑. The standard verb for running away from a threat, a captor, or an obligation. Used for fugitives, escaped animals, soldiers fleeing a battlefield, and (figuratively) people who avoid responsibility.

讨 tǎo (to seek out, to ask for) + 论. The everyday word for discussing a matter: a group talking something through to reach understanding or a decision. Cooperative by default, two or more people pooling views rather than fighting over them.

e: form; sequence; a fixed pattern (also: routine, formula)
d: A choreographed sequence of martial techniques practiced solo, encoding combat principles. Also used colloquially for any formulaic routine or pattern: 走套路 "going through the motions" · 那只是套路 "that's just standard formula."
"Especially" or "particularly." Singles out the most important case within a broader claim. 我喜欢中国菜, 特别是川菜 ("I like Chinese food, especially Sichuan food"). Direct, useful, common.

特 tè (special; particular) + 长 cháng (strength; advantage, the area where one "goes long"). 你有什么特长？ "What are your special skills?" is the standard job interview form. 特长生 = a student admitted on the basis of a special talent (music, sports, art) rather than exam scores alone.

e: to raise; to improve; to enhance
d: 提 tí (to lift, to raise; to bring up) + 高 (high). To raise the level of something: 提高效率 (improve efficiency); 提高水平 (raise the standard); 提高工资 (increase wages). The standard verb for improvement in formal and professional contexts.

e: to move up in time; to do in advance; ahead of schedule
d: 提 tí (to lift; to bring forward; to raise up) + 前 qián (front; before). Literally "to lift forward": to move a scheduled event earlier than planned, to do something in advance. The opposite is 推迟 tuīchí (to postpone, to push back).

e: to ask a question; to raise a question
d: 提 tí (to raise; to bring up) + 问 wèn (to ask). To put a question forward, typically in a class or meeting. 老师提问 "the teacher asks a question," often of a student called on to answer.

e: exam question; title; subject (of an essay)
d: 题 tí (heading) + 目 mù (item; entry). The item set at the head of a test, or the title given to a composition: 考试题目 "exam questions," 作文题目 "the essay prompt." It points at the specific thing to be answered or written about.

e: to inscribe a poem (on a painting, wall, or scroll)
d: 题 tí (to inscribe) + 诗 shī (poem). To write a poem directly onto a surface, a classic gesture in Chinese painting where verse and image share one scroll.
题 tí (to inscribe) + 字 zì (characters). To brush words onto a painting, plaque, or wall, or the inscription itself. Often done by a respected figure as a mark of honor.

e: to grasp through experience; the understanding so gained
d: 体 tǐ (body) + 会 huì (to understand). To come to understand a thing by living it, and the insight that results. 深刻的体会 "a deep understanding (won from experience)."
体 tǐ (body) + 力 lì (strength). The body's stamina, the strength that sustains physical effort over time. Often paired against 脑力 nǎolì (mental effort): 体力劳动 "physical labor."

e: considerate; thoughtful; attentive to others' needs
d: 体 tǐ (to feel in the body) + 贴 tiē (to stick close). To feel another's situation closely and act with care: 体贴的丈夫 "a considerate husband." It is warmth shown through attention to small needs.

e: framework; structured system (of ideas or institutions)
d: 体 tǐ (body; structure) + 系 xì (connection). An organized framework, usually of something abstract: 理论体系 "a theoretical framework," 教育体系 "the education system." More architectural and conceptual than the everyday 系统.

e: to experience; to live through; an experience
d: 体 tǐ (body) + 验 yàn (to test, to verify). To know something by passing through it in person: 体验生活 "to experience real life." As a noun, the experience itself: 难忘的体验 "an unforgettable experience."

e: substance and function; essence and manifestation
d: 体 tǐ (body; substance; the underlying essence) + 用 yòng (function; use; the outward expression). A compound used in philosophy, aesthetics, Buddhist thought, and political theory to describe the relationship between a thing's nature and its operation in the world.
体 tǐ (body) + 育 yù (to nurture, to educate). The cultivation of the body: school PE, and sport in general. 体育馆 tǐyùguǎn is a gymnasium; 体育课 is a PE class.
体育 tǐyù (physical education, sport) + 馆. The roofed sports hall, as opposed to the open-air 体育场 (chǎng, a field/stadium). The 馆 marks the covered, indoor venue.

Constitution: one's inherent physical and energetic type, which determines predispositions to certain diseases and guides appropriate diet, lifestyle, and treatment choices. Nine constitutional types are defined in modern TCM standardization.
体 tǐ (body) + 重 zhòng (weight). How much a person weighs: 量体重 "to weigh oneself." The weight that the body itself carries.
替 (in place of) + 换 (swap). To take one thing out and put a stand-in where it was: a worn part, a player, a placeholder word. The replacement fills the same slot the original left.

天 tiān (heaven) + 才 cái (talent; ability). Heaven-bestowed ability , the kind of capacity that seems to have come from beyond ordinary human effort. The etymology encodes a theory of talent: genius is a gift, not a product.

e: the way of heaven; the natural moral order
d: 天 tiān (heaven; sky; the natural cosmic order) + 道 dào (way; path). The principle by which the cosmos operates: rewarding virtue, punishing tyranny, maintaining the balance of nature. An impersonal moral force, not a personal god.

e: between heaven and earth; in this world
d: 间 jiān (between; the space between two things). 天地间 names the space of human existence. A frequent location phrase in classical and literary prose.

e: Heaven, Earth, Humanity — the Three Powers (三才 sāncái)
d: The three constitutive powers of the cosmos in classical Chinese thought. Heaven (天) provides the patterns and conditions from above; Earth (地) provides the material ground and resources from below; Humanity (人) stands between them, participating in both and responsible for the mediation.

Land of Abundance , literally "storehouse of heaven's kingdom." The epithet for the Chengdu Plain and by extension Sichuan, reflecting the agricultural richness produced by the Dujiangyan irrigation system.

e: natural gift; innate ability; heaven's endowment
d: 天 tiān (heaven) + 赋 fù (to endow; to bestow; to compose, originally the government's levy on subjects, then poetic composition). Heaven's formal bestowal. 天赋 is slightly more formal and literary than 天才, referring to specific aptitudes rather than a person of exceptional overall genius.

e: heavenly stems and earthly branches; the traditional Chinese calendrical system
d: The 60-year calendrical cycle built on the same yang/yin cosmology that underlies 乾坤. 天干 tiāngān (heavenly stems): ten yang elements cycling through the years (甲 jiǎ, 乙 yǐ, 丙 bǐng, 丁 dīng, etc.).
天 tiān (heaven) + 国 guó (kingdom; nation). The standard Chinese translation of "Kingdom of Heaven" in Christian scripture.

e: Tianhou Palace — her temples across the diaspora
d: After her elevation to 天后 (Heavenly Empress) by the Qing Emperor in 1683, Mazu's temples were formally renamed 天后宫 Tiānhòu Gōng (Tianhou Palace).

e: the celestial realm; heaven; the realm of gods and immortals
d: 天 (heaven; sky) + 界 (boundary; realm; world). The realm above 人间, populated by gods (神 shén), immortals (仙 xiān), and celestial officials. In folk-religion cosmology it mirrors the imperial bureaucracy below, with the Jade Emperor (玉皇大帝 Yù Huáng Dàdì) at its head.

e: the sky; the heavens as a physical expanse
d: 天 tiān (sky) + 空 kōng (empty; hollow; space). More poetic and specific than 天气: refers to the physical dome of sky above, not weather conditions. Used in literary contexts, poetry, and vivid description. 空 kōng also means "empty" , the sky is the great emptiness above.

天 tiān (sky) + 气 qì (breath; air; vital force). Literally: the sky's breath. In traditional Chinese cosmology, qì 气 is the invisible force that animates all phenomena; weather is the sky breathing. HSK 1, but it carries this depth beneath the surface.

e: color of the sky; time of day as read from the light
d: 天 tiān (sky) + 色 sè (color; hue; appearance). The quality of sky-light as a way of telling the time or mood of the day: dawn's pale gray, midday's high white, dusk's orange bleed. A literary and slightly classical usage, common in classical fiction and poetry.

The Heavenly Mountains: the mountain range dividing northern and southern Xinjiang, with peaks reaching 7,443 m. A UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site, the Tianshan is the water source for the oasis cities of the Tarim Basin and one of the great mountain ranges of Central Asia.

天 tiān (heaven) + 生 shēng (to be born; to live). "Born of heaven" = innate, not acquired. The counterpart to 后天 hòutiān (acquired; postnatal). In classical philosophy, the 先天/后天 dichotomy maps roughly onto nature/nurture, one of the most enduring debates in Chinese intellectual life.

Founded by Zhiyi 智顗 (538–597 CE) on Mount Tiantai 天台山 in Zhejiang. Tiantai's great achievement was doctrinal classification 判教 pānjìao: organizing all Buddhist scriptures into a hierarchical scheme of "five periods and eight teachings," with the Lotus Sutra 法华经 at the apex.

e: paradise; heaven as a place of bliss
d: 天 tiān (heaven) + 堂 táng (hall; grand hall; a place of gathering). The "heavenly hall," used in Chinese Buddhism for the Pure Land, and in general usage for any paradise-like place. Also commonly used hyperbolically: 美食天堂 (food paradise), 购物天堂 (shopping paradise), 自行车天堂 (cycling paradise).
Astronomy: heaven's patterns. 天文数字 ("an astronomical figure") is the standard idiom for an unthinkably large sum, same metaphor as English.

e: number one under heaven; the best in the world; the supreme superlative
d: The hyperbolic superlative: beyond which there is nothing greater. 天下 replaces "in the world," and 第一 means "first/number one." Used for scenic spots (桂林山水甲天下 , Guilin's scenery is finest under heaven), for self-proclaimed champions (自称天下第一 , to call oneself the best in the world), and in historical…

e: the vastness of the world; how great the world is

h: 天行健，君子以自强不息
p: tiān xíng jiàn, jūnzǐ yǐ zì qiáng bù xī
e: Heaven moves with vigor; the noble person strengthens himself without cease
d: From the commentary on the first hexagram 乾 qián , the Judgment commentary (大象传 Dà Xiàng Zhuàn). 天行健 tiān xíng jiàn: heaven (the sky, the cosmos) moves with consistent vigor , it does not pause, does not rest, does not slacken.

e: Heaven's movements are constant — the cosmos operates by regular, impersonal laws
d: 天 tiān (Heaven/Nature) + 行 xíng (movements, operations) + 有常 yǒu cháng (have regularity, are constant). The foundational statement of Xunzi's naturalism. Heaven's processes are reliable precisely because they are not subject to human will or divine whim.

e: the will of Heaven; what fate decrees

d: 天 tiān (heaven) + 真 zhēn (genuine; true; real). "Heaven-true" , the quality of someone whose genuine nature has not been shaped or distorted by social calculation. In children, this is charming: 天真烂漫 (innocent and carefree , the enchanting naivety of childhood).

e: the will of Heaven — Mohist moral authority
d: Unlike Confucian ethics, which grounds moral authority in tradition, the sage-kings, and the cultivation of 仁 rén (humaneness), Mozi appealed to 天 tiān (Heaven) as a purposive moral agent that actively wills universal love and punishes those who violate it.

天 tiān (heaven) + 子 zǐ (son; child). The Chinese emperor's formal title: he is heaven's son, the intermediary between the cosmic order and humanity, not a god himself but heaven's appointed representative on earth. The title dates to the Zhou dynasty and was used through the Qing (ended 1912).

e: measure word for long thin items

d: 第五条 (dì-wǔ tiáo) is Article 5. 补充协议 (bǔchōng xiéyì) is a supplementary agreement, the usual way to add terms later. 附件 (fùjiàn) is an annex, where specifications and drawings belong.

e: to gaze into the distance; to look out over
d: 眺 tiào (to look afar) + 望 wàng (to gaze). To stand at a height and let the eye travel over a wide, distant view: 登高眺望 "to climb high and gaze out." More elevated and literary than ordinary 看, it implies an open vista and a lifted vantage point.

铁 tiě (iron; steel) + 道 (way; path). The iron way: railway tracks as a path made of iron. Common in institutional and geographic contexts. Also 铁路 tiělù (the more common modern term for railway system). 铁道 tends to refer to the track itself; 铁路 to the railway as a transport network.

e: to comply with; to follow (advice, instructions)
d: 听 (to listen, to heed) + 从 cóng (to follow; to comply). To hear and act accordingly , to accept and follow guidance, instructions, or authority. Used for following medical advice (听从医嘱 tīngcóng yīzhǔ), following a superior's direction, or complying with a decision.

听 tīng (to listen) + 到 dào (arrive). Listening that arrived: the sound reached the ear and registered. 听到 is not an attempt to hear but a confirmed result. Compare 听 alone (the action of listening) with 听到 (the listening that succeeded).

e: to understand what one hears; to follow spoken language
d: 听 (to listen) + 懂 dǒng (to understand). The resultative complement 懂 marks successful comprehension , listening that reached understanding. Constant in language learning contexts: 你听懂了吗？ (Did you understand what you heard?) contrasts with 你听到了吗？ (Did you hear it? — did the sound reach you?).

e: obedient; to do as one is told
d: 听 (to listen) + 话 huà (words; speech). Obedient in the sense of listening to what is said and acting accordingly. The standard word for a well-behaved child: 这孩子很听话 (this child is very obedient).

e: to obey orders; to receive commands
d: 听 (to receive; to comply) + 命 mìng (command; order; fate). Used in military, official, and formal institutional contexts for strict compliance with authoritative commands. 听命于 (to obey the commands of; to be under the orders of).

e: to have heard (that); reportedly; I've heard that
d: 听 (to hear) + 说 shuō (to say; to speak). A hedging marker for secondhand information: "I've heard it said that…" Placed at the start of a clause to flag that the speaker did not witness the information directly. 听说他去北京了 (I heard he went to Beijing).
听 (to listen) + 音乐 yīnyuè (music , 音 sound/tone + 乐 joy/music). The most common collocation for 听 in daily life. 听歌 tīng gē (to listen to songs) is the slightly more casual form.

The sustained-attention imperative with 着. 听 alone is a simple command to listen; 听着 adds the sense of "maintain that listening state." Common before announcements, reprimands, or instructions that require focused, continuous attention.

e: usually; ordinarily; generally; as a rule
d: 通 (general; holding throughout) + 常 cháng (constant; usual; frequent). The case that holds across most instances: usually, as the general rule. 通常 sets up the ordinary expectation against which exceptions are measured: 我通常七点起床 (I usually get up at seven).

e: to be open to traffic; to begin service (of a road or line)
d: 通 (to open; to be through) + 车 chē (vehicle). To be through to vehicles: the moment a new road, bridge, railway, or subway line opens and traffic can run along it. A staple of infrastructure news, where the opening of a line is itself an event: 正式通车 (officially opened to traffic).

e: to pass through; to get past; by means of; via
d: 通 (to go through) + 过 guò (to cross; to pass). The everyday verb for getting through something: passing through a gate, passing an exam, a motion passing a vote.
通 (to connect; to convey) + 信 xìn (a letter; a message; trust). To get messages through to one another. Historically it meant to exchange letters: 我们通了多年信 (we corresponded for many years).

通 (general; running throughout) + 用 yòng (to use). Usable throughout, across cases: not specialized to one situation but serving generally. 通用 describes something accepted everywhere or applicable across the board: 全国通用 (valid nationwide), 通用规则 (a general rule that applies in all cases).

e: to notify; to inform; a notice; a notification
d: 通 (to get through; to convey) + 知 zhī (to know; to make known). To make something known by getting word through: the standard word for an official notification and the act of giving it. Works as a verb (请通知大家, please notify everyone) and a noun (一份通知, a notice).

e: at the same time; meanwhile; moreover
d: 同 tóng (same) + 时 shí (time). The same moment: 同时进行 "to proceed simultaneously." As a connector it also means "at the same time, moreover," adding a further point.
同 tóng (same) + 事 shì (work; affair). One who shares the same work, a colleague. Built on the same pattern as 同学: the shared station named by what is held in common.

e: tóngháng: a peer in the same trade · tóngxíng: to travel together
d: 同 tóng (same; together) + 行. The two readings split cleanly: tóngháng = "same trade" → a colleague, a competitor in the same line of work. tóngxíng = "to walk together" → to travel as companions. Same characters, two unrelated meanings , distinguished entirely by reading.
同 tóng (same) + 学 xué (study). One who studies alongside you. A teacher also uses 同学 to address a pupil: 这位同学 "this student here." 老同学 means an old schoolmate.
同 tóng (same) + 样 yàng (kind). Of the same kind, used before a noun (同样的方法 "the same method") or as a sentence adverb meaning "in the same way, likewise."

e: to agree; to consent; to approve
d: 同 tóng (same) + 意 yì (idea; intention). To hold the same idea, to give one's assent: 我同意你的看法 "I agree with your view." The opposite is 反对 fǎnduì, to oppose.
同 tóng (same) + 志 zhì (aspiration; will). One of the same aspiration. The standard revolutionary address for "comrade," and in contemporary informal use a self-chosen word for gay people.

Bronze man: the life-sized bronze figure commissioned in 1026 CE with channel lines and point locations engraved on the surface and a hollow interior. Filled with water and wax for examination purposes, it was the world's first standardized anatomical teaching model for acupuncture instruction.
童 tóng (child) + 话 huà (story). A tale told for children. Its kin 神话 shénhuà (god-story) means a myth, and 神话 and 童话 together cover the world of fabulous stories.

统 tǒng (to govern; to bind together) + 一. The political constant of Chinese civilization: 天下统一 (unification of all under heaven). As verb: 统一思想 (unify thinking), 统一标准 (standardize). As adjective: 统一规格 (uniform specifications).
痛 (tòng), to ache, joins 苦 (kǔ), bitter, to name suffering felt in body or mind. The most direct word for anguish, it covers physical pain and emotional torment alike.

痛 tòng (pain; with full intensity) + 快 kuài (free-flowing; pleasurable). Two distinct but related uses. As a personality or speech descriptor: so direct and honest it cuts , blunt, refreshingly frank. As an experience descriptor: so wholly satisfying that nothing was held back.

头 tóu (head) + 发 fà (hair). The hair on a person's head, as a mass. Note that 发 here is the fà / 髮 reading; in casual speech the syllable often softens toward neutral tone. Distinct from 毛 máo, the word for body hair and fur.

e: the first seven-day memorial after death
d: 头 tóu (head; first) + 七 qī (seven). Traditional Chinese mourning involves rituals at seven-day intervals for 49 days , the period the soul is believed to linger. 头七 (day 7) is the most important: the family burns paper offerings and sets a place for the deceased at the table.

e: headache, can't go — circumstance prevents ability
d: 能 covers physical capacity (your body can or cannot do something) and circumstantial ability (the situation allows or does not allow).

e: to throw; to cast; to drop in
to vote: to cast a ballot
d: 投 tóu (to throw; to cast; to drop in) + 票 piào (slip; ballot). To vote, literally to throw a slip into the box. The image is exact: a ballot is a slip of paper, and casting it is dropping it into the urn.
突 tū (to dash out, abrupt) + 然 rán (-ly). Unlike 忽然, 突然 can also be a full adjective: 很突然 "very sudden," 突然的变化 "an abrupt change." So it covers both "suddenly" and "abrupt."
图 tú (chart; image) + 画 huà (painting). A general word for a picture or illustration, the kind in a children's book or on a wall. Broader and plainer than 国画 or 油画, which name specific traditions.

图 tú (drawing; map; illustration) + 书 shū (book) + 馆 guǎn (hall; building for a function). A building for maps and books. The word 图书 túshū , "illustrated books" , is now the formal term for library holdings in general.

图 tú (drawing; diagram) + 形 xíng. A drawn figure or graphic: shapes on a page, icons on a screen, the figures of geometry. 几何图形 = geometric figures; 图形界面 = a graphical interface. Where 形状 is a thing's shape, 图形 is a shape that has been drawn as such.

2D drawings with dimensions; 3D文件 or 3D图 (sān-D tú) for the model file, usually STEP. 以图纸为准 ("the drawing governs") is the sentence that settles arguments, so make sure the drawing is the latest version.

土 tǔ (earth) + 地 dì (ground). In everyday speech, land or soil: 土地肥沃 "fertile land." In folk religion it also names the 土地神 or 土地公, the humble local earth-god of a village or plot, the small-scale heir to the old 社 cult, honoured at modest roadside shrines.

e: the Earth God — most local, most beloved deity
d: 土地公 (also 土地神 Tǔdìshén, formally 福德正神 Fúdé Zhèngshén) is the deity of a specific patch of ground: a village, a neighborhood, a field, a shop. He is the lowest-ranking god in the celestial hierarchy and the most ubiquitous.
团 (a tight cluster, a ball of people) + 队 (organized group). The modern office and startup word for a project team bound by a shared task.
团 tuán (round; group) + 结 jié (to bind). To draw a group tightly together into one body: 团结一致 "united as one." Used of teams, communities, and nations holding together against difficulty.

e: reunion; to be reunited (as a family)
pushing hands — the partner practice of Tai Chi

d: 退 (tuì, to recede) plus 热 (heat, fever): to make the fever fall. The word on a fever-reducing medicine box and what a worried parent waits for through the night.

e: to break free of a bind
to break away from, to detach from
d: 脱 (tuō, to shed, to slip off) plus 离 (to part). To break free of a tie, a danger, or a group. Stronger than 离开: it implies cutting a connection, not just walking out.

e: outward appearance: the way someone or something looks from outside
d: 外 wài (outer; outside) + 表 biǎo (surface). The outward appearance of a person or thing, especially how they look to others. Where 表面 leans toward physical surfaces and abstract superficiality, 外表 is most natural for the looks of people and objects, the impression they give at first sight.

外 wài (outer) + 丹 dān (cinnabar). The earlier tradition: physically preparing elixirs in a laboratory by heating and transforming minerals (especially cinnabar, lead, gold, and sulfur) to produce an immortality drug.
The question the tour exists to answer. A factory that sends out a step is not necessarily hiding anything, but you need to know, because quality on that step is out of its direct control.
外 wài (outside) + 国 guó (country). A country other than one''s own. A person from one is 外国人 wàiguórén (foreigner); the things of one are 外国 X, as in 外国文化 "foreign culture."
外 wài (out) + 卖 mài (to sell). Food sold to be taken away rather than eaten in. In modern usage it means app-based delivery: 点外卖 "to order takeout," 外卖员 "a delivery rider."
外 wài (outside) + 面 miàn (side; surface). The everyday word for the area beyond an enclosed space, or the outer surface of a thing. Its pair is 里面 lǐmiàn (inside).

外 wài (outside the surname) + 婆 pó (old woman). One''s mother''s mother, marked 外 because she belongs to the maternal line. Its pair is 外公 wàigōng (maternal grandfather); the father''s parents are 奶奶 and 爷爷.

The Bund , the waterfront promenade along the Huangpu River, lined with the banking and trading buildings of the concession era. The name means literally "outer mudflat." Now a heritage district and one of the most photographed urban frontages in China.
外 wài (foreign) + 语 yǔ (language). A language other than one''s own. 学外语 "to study a foreign language," 外语学院 "a foreign-languages institute."

e: to complete; to accomplish; to finish
d: 完 wán (whole; to finish) + 成 chéng (to bring to completion). To carry a task all the way to done: 完成任务 "to complete a task," 完成作业 "to finish the homework." The everyday word for getting something fully finished.

完 wán (finished; whole) + 全 quán (complete). The standard adverb for "completely," to the full degree with nothing left over: 完全同意 "completely agree," 完全没问题 "no problem at all." Negated, it gives "not at all": 完全不对.

"Completely agree." Strong endorsement. Used when you want to back the speaker without reservation. The 完全 ("completely") makes it emphatic; reserve for moments when full agreement is what you actually mean.

玩 wán (to play) + 笑 xiào (laugh). Play-laughter: a joke made between people who are at ease together. 开玩笑 kāi wánxiào (to crack a joke, to be kidding) is one of the highest-frequency phrases in spoken Mandarin.
挽 (wǎn, to pull back) + 救 (rescue). To salvage something already sliding toward loss: a failing marriage, a patient's life, a tottering situation. The emphasis is on reversing a decline.

Graceful and restrained , the dominant stylistic tradition of the 词, characterized by delicate emotion, intimate scale, and subjects of love, beauty, and seasonal melancholy. Li Yu, Liu Yong, and Li Qingzhao are its central figures.

e: ten thousand li; immense distance; vast
d: 万 (ten thousand) + 里 lǐ (Chinese unit of distance, roughly 500m). Ten thousand li is nominally 5,000 km, but the compound functions as a hyperbole for any vast, daunting distance. 万里长城 (Wànlǐ Chángchéng, "the ten-thousand-li Great Wall") is the most famous usage.

e: may all ten thousand things go as you wish; all the best
d: 万 (myriad) + 事 shì (matters, things) + 如意 rúyì (as one wishes). The standard all-occasion blessing, appearing on red envelopes, greeting cards, New Year couplets, and toasts.

万 (ten thousand) + 岁 suì (years of age; year). The imperial acclamation: 皇帝万岁 (huángdì wàn suì), "long live the Emperor." Reserved exclusively for the emperor in traditional usage; to use it for anyone else was a capital offense.

e: all things; the myriad phenomena; everything that exists
d: 万 (myriad) + 物 wù (thing, object, phenomenon). The standard classical and literary expression for "all of existence." In Daoist thought, the ten-thousand things emerge from the interplay of yin and yang, and the Dao underlies them all.

e: all phenomena; the ten thousand forms
just in case; in the unlikely event that; one in ten thousand
d: 万 (ten thousand) + 一 (one). Literally, one part in ten thousand , the probability so small it barely registers. In usage: a concession to contingency.

e: dynasty; royal house: the line of a ruling family
d: 王 wáng (king) + 朝 cháo (reign). A dynasty seen as a ruling family or royal house, often used of a single line of monarchs and, by extension, of any long-dominant power: 商业王朝 "a business empire," a sports 王朝.

e: the kingly way; governance by virtue rather than force
d: 王 wáng (king; ruler) + 道 dào (way; path). The Confucian ideal of legitimate rule: the virtuous ruler transforms those around him through moral example, not coercion. His virtue radiates outward, bringing peace and order spontaneously. Contrasted sharply with 霸道, the way of force.

王 wáng (king; ruler of a principality) + 后 (consort). The consort of a 王 (king or prince). In historical Chinese usage, 王 ranked below 皇帝 (emperor), so 王后 was below 皇后. In modern usage, 王后 translates "queen consort" in Western contexts.

A friend made online, from 网 wǎng (net) + 友 yǒu (friend). A thoroughly modern coinage and an extremely common one. Note that 友 contracts here from 朋友, a regular pattern: 友 alone serves as the bound "friend" element in compounds (校友 alumnus, 战友 comrade-in-arms, 笔友 pen pal).
网 (wǎng, net) + 站 (station): a website, a fixed point on the internet. The everyday word for any site you visit, from a shop to a search engine.

e: going toward rebirth — the Pure Land term for death as aspiration
d: 往 wǎng (to go toward) + 生 shēng (life; rebirth). The Pure Land term for a practitioner's death, framed not as loss but as aspiration fulfilled.

The four examinations , looking (observation of complexion, tongue, posture), listening/smelling (voice, breath), asking (history, symptoms), and touching (pulse diagnosis). The complete TCM diagnostic protocol compressed into four characters.

望 wàng (to look far) + 远 yuǎn (far) + 镜 jìng (lens, mirror). Literally "a lens for looking far": the instrument that brings the distant near. 天文望远镜 is an astronomical telescope; 双筒望远镜 is a pair of binoculars. A neat transparent compound that reads itself.
危 (endanger) plus 害 (harm). The danger turned active: to damage or jeopardize something, and the resulting harm itself. Common with health, society, environment.
危 (danger) plus 机 (critical juncture). A crisis: the decisive, threatening turn in an economy, a relationship, an illness, a career.
危 (danger) plus 急 (urgent). Danger compressed by time: a situation that is both perilous and pressing, where a hospital patient or a battlefield hangs by a thread.

e: a dangerous building; a lofty tower
d: 危 (here in both senses) plus 楼 (multi-storey building). In modern use, a condemned structure unsafe to enter. In classical poetry the same word means a tall tower rising into the air, the older lofty reading of 危.
危 (danger) plus 险 (steep, perilous), a doubling of two height-and-hazard words into the standard everyday term for danger. Works as both adjective (this is dangerous) and noun (a danger).

威 wēi (authority, awe) + 望 wàng (esteem). The prestige that commands respect and deference, the standing of someone in a position of leadership: 树立威望 "to establish one's prestige." Stronger than plain reputation, it carries a sense of earned authority.

威 wēi (awe, authority) + 武 wǔ (martial). Powerful and commanding in bearing, mighty in a dignified way: 威武的将军 "an imposing general," 威武雄壮 "majestic and powerful." Describes the impressive, formidable presence of soldiers, guards, or anything built on a grand and strong scale.

微 wēi (minute; subtle; trace) + 小 xiǎo (small). Doubles the smallness: 微 already indicates near-invisibility (as in 微生物 microorganism, 微波 microwave), and 小 compounds that. Used for things at the scale of cells, particles, or imperceptible contributions. A higher register than 很小.
微 wēi (faint; slight; minute) + 笑 xiào (laugh/smile). A small, soundless laugh: the smile. The word that names the warm, closed-lipped expression, distinct from the open-mouthed 大笑.

e: a besieged city; to lay siege to a city
d: 围 wéi (to surround; to encircle) + 城 chéng (city). Literally an encircled city, both the act of besieging one and the besieged city itself.
