d: 一把年纪 literally "a handful of years" , used to describe someone who is getting on in age. Often carries a mildly reproachful or surprised tone: someone that age should know better, or it's surprising they're doing something. Common in colloquial speech and semi-formal contexts.

e: a chair (one handle-shaped piece of furniture)
d: 把 as a measure word applies to objects that have a handle or can be grasped, or that you can take in hand , chairs (by the back), tools, weapons, fans, keys, locks, umbrellas, guitars. The connection to the core meaning of 把 (to grip) is transparent.

e: a cup / glass of water — 杯 bēi
d: 杯 bēi (cup, glass) counts liquids held in cups or glasses. The container becomes the classifier. This is the most transparent type: the classifier is the vessel. A large class of classifiers work this way , 碗, 盘, 瓶, 桶, 壶 , each named for the physical container holding the substance.
一 yī (one) + 笔 bǐ (measure word) + 钱 qián (money). A definite, lump amount of money, the kind written down as a single entry: 一大笔钱 "a large sum," 这笔钱 "this sum of money."
一 yī (one) + 笔 bǐ (measure word) + 生意 shēngyì (business). One transaction or deal, counted as a single recorded piece of business: 做一笔生意 "to do a deal," 一笔大生意 "a big deal."
一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 电影 diànyǐng (film). The standard way to count a film, treating it as a single complete work. The same 部 counts a 小说 (novel) or a 电视剧 (TV series).
一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 手机 shǒujī (phone). 部 counts a phone as a self-contained device. You will also hear 一个手机 in casual speech, but 一部手机 is the proper classifier.

e: a novel; one work of fiction
d: 一 yī (one) + 部 bù (measure word) + 小说 xiǎoshuō (novel). 部 counts a full-length novel as one finished work. For a short story you would more likely use 篇 piān, the classifier for shorter writings.
Disposable chopsticks: the individually wrapped bamboo or wood pairs given at most restaurants. Billions are used annually; their environmental cost is a topic of ongoing public debate.
Productive frame for arrival-triggered actions. 他一到就开始工作 (He started working as soon as he arrived). Pairs naturally with 回来 huí lái (return) and 到家 dào jiā (get home): 一回来就 / 一到家就.

e: a little; a bit (post-verbal, neutral or positive)
d: 一 yī (one) + 点 diǎn (dot; bit). Appears after adjectives and verbs, typically in commands, requests, or comparisons. Neutral to positive in coloring. 便宜一点 (a little cheaper , as a request), 快一点 (a little faster), 多吃一点 (eat a little more). In comparisons: 比昨天冷一点 (a little colder than yesterday).

e: a little; a bit (neutral, often comparative)
d: After an adjective, 一点儿 makes a neutral comparison, "a little more X": 大一点儿 (a bit bigger), 快一点儿 (a bit faster), 便宜一点儿 (a little cheaper). After a verb, it means "a little / some": 喝一点儿水 (drink a little water), 说一点儿 (say a bit).

e: a little (mass) · a part (of a whole)
d: 一点儿 measures out a small amount of an uncountable substance: 一点儿水 (a little water), 会一点儿中文 (speaks a little Chinese). It pairs with mass nouns where 几 pairs with countables. 部分 bùfen slices a defined whole: 一部分学生 (a portion of the students), 大部分时间 (most of the time). The trap of 一点儿 vs.

e: must; be sure to; definitely will
d: The emphatic resolve-and-urging frame. For yourself it is determination: 我一定要赢 ("I'm determined to win"). For others it is earnest pressing: 你一定要照顾好自己 ("you really must take good care of yourself").
队 as a measure word counts people or animals moving in a formed line: a column of soldiers, a string of camels, a file of schoolchildren.

When 工作 means a discrete job or position, it is counted with the measure word 份 fèn, the same word used for a portion or a document. 一份工作 ("one job"), 两份工作 ("two jobs," as in working two jobs). When 工作 means work as an activity or workload, it takes no measure word: 工作很多 ("there's a lot of work").
封 also works as the measure word for letters and other sealed correspondence: each sealed packet counts as one 封. 一封信 is one letter; 一封电子邮件 (yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn), one email.

一 + 个 (general measure word). 一 before tone 4 (个 gè) → yí. The most frequent combination of 一 in everyday speech: 一个人 yí gè rén (one person), 一个问题 yí gè wèntí (one question), 一个地方 yí gè dìfang (one place). 个 gè is the default measure word when no specific one applies.

"One country, two systems" , the constitutional principle under which Hong Kong was reunified with China in 1997. Proposed by Deng Xiaoping, it promised Hong Kong fifty years of maintaining its existing legal, economic, and social systems under Chinese sovereignty. The principle expires in 2047.

一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 礼物 lǐwù (gift; present). A present counts as a discrete object, so it takes 件. The same classifier extends to other countable belongings and pieces of luggage: 一件行李 (one piece of luggage), 一件作品 (one work of art).

e: a matter: one affair; one thing to deal with
d: 一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 事 shì (matter; affair). 件 is the standard classifier for an affair, an errand, or a piece of business, anything that can be treated as a single, separable concern. You do not say 一个事 in careful speech; the matter takes 件.

e: an item of clothing: one garment
d: 一 yī (one) + 件 jiàn (measure word) + 衣服 yīfu (clothing). 件 counts upper-body and one-piece garments: shirts, coats, dresses, sweaters. Lower-body garments take 条 tiáo instead (一条裤子 a pair of trousers, 一条裙子 a skirt), so the measure word itself signals which part of the body is meant.
一 yī (one) + 节 jié (measure word) + 课 kè (class). 节 here is the counter for class periods, each a fixed segment of the school day. 上一节课 "to attend a class period," 两节课 "two periods."

e: one remark; a single sentence; in a word
d: 一 yī (one) + 句 jù (measure word) + 话 huà (speech). A single spoken remark, counted with 句. Used adverbially, 一句话 means "in a word, to put it briefly."

The prototype 一…就 sentence. Used to describe something immediately clear, a design that needs no instructions, or a person who grasps something with no effort. 这个图表一看就懂 (This chart is self-explanatory).

e: "safe journey": the standard farewell to a traveler
d: 一 yī (one, whole) + 路 lù (road) + 平安 píng'ān (peace, safety). "May the whole road be peaceful." The phrase you say at the airport, the train station, or as the car pulls away. Slightly more formal than 一路顺风 yílù shùnfēng ("may the wind be with you").

e: one side; one surface; (measure) one flat object
d: 一 yī (one) + 面 miàn (measure word). 面 counts flat, surface-like objects: 一面镜子 (a mirror), 一面墙 (a wall), 一面旗 (a flag). As a noun 一面 also means "one side" of an argument or "one aspect."

e: all one's life; a whole lifetime; forever
d: 一生 yìshēng (one life) + 一世 yíshì (one lifetime). A doubled phrase for the entirety of a person's days, common in vows of love and loyalty: 我会爱你一生一世 "I will love you for the rest of my life." Warmer and more lyrical than the plain 一辈子.

一 yī (one) + 首 shǒu (measure word) + 歌 gē (song). 首 is the classifier for songs and poems: 一首歌 a song, 一首诗 a poem, 一首词 a lyric. Each piece is counted as one self-contained "head." 唱一首歌 "to sing a song."

一 yī (one) + 首 shǒu (measure word) + 诗 shī (poem). The same classifier counts poems. 写一首诗 "to write a poem," 背一首诗 "to recite a poem from memory." A classical anthology is described as so many 首 of verse.

e: one cow; a head of cattle
d: 一 yī (one) + 头 tóu (measure word) + 牛 niú (cow). Here 头 keeps its full tone as the classifier for large livestock: cattle, pigs, sheep, elephants. You count beasts by the head.

A related but distinct adverb: 一下子 means "all at once, in one go, suddenly," describing rapid or abrupt change rather than softening a verb: 天一下子黑了 ("the sky went dark all at once"). Do not confuse it with the verb-softening 一下: 看一下 ("have a look") versus 一下子看完了 ("finished reading it in one go").

e: all along; consistently; up to now
d: 一 yī (one; throughout) + 向 xiàng (facing back along). A habit or state held unbroken up to the present: 他一向如此 "he has always been like this." Marks long-standing consistency, not a one-off.

h: 一些 · 有的 · 有些
d: 一些 introduces an indefinite amount: 我买了一些水果 (I bought some fruit). 有的 and 有些 pick out a subset of a known or generic whole, and they live at the front of the sentence: 有的人喜欢，有的人不喜欢 (some people like it, some don't). The classic restriction: 有的 phrases resist the object position.

Marks two things as the same. The frame is A 跟 B 一样 (跟 gēn or 和 hé link the two). Add an adjective to compare a specific quality as equal: A 跟 B 一样 + Adj. Negate as A 跟 B 不一样 ("different") or A 跟 B 不一样 + Adj. 一样 alone can also modify a noun: 一样的衣服 ("the same clothes").

一 + 致 zhì (to reach; to arrive at). All arriving at one point. 意见一致 (unanimous opinion), 行动一致 (acting in concert), 保持一致 (maintain consistency). Higher register than 一样 yīyàng , used in formal and official contexts. 众口一致 (everyone speaking with one mouth = unanimous) is a near-chengyu variant.

e: to simply leave; to walk away from a problem
d: 一 + 走了之 , "just walk off and be done with it." A set phrase for leaving without dealing with the situation. Pejorative: the person who 一走了之 is abandoning responsibility. Used critically: 你不能就这样一走了之 (you can't just walk away like that).

The classical and Wu-dialect "she." In the 1917 debate, some intellectuals advocated reviving 伊 instead of coining 她, since 伊 already had a feminine reading in some classical poetry and avoided the male-default asymmetry.

e: Islam — practiced by the 色目人 administrators and merchants of the Yuan

d: 医 yī (medicine; to heal) + 生 shēng (practitioner). The standard word for doctor in mainland China. Note the 生 suffix , it originally meant "one who practices/studies" (compare 学生, 先生). 看医生 = "to see a doctor."

遗 yí (to leave behind) + 传 chuán (to hand down). The biological passing of traits from parent to offspring: 遗传病 "hereditary disease," 遗传基因 "the genes one inherits." The body's own version of handing something down across generations.
疑 yí (to doubt) + 问 wèn (to ask). A question that arises from uncertainty: 毫无疑问 háo wú yíwèn "without the slightest doubt." Also the grammatical term, as in 疑问句 yíwènjù "interrogative sentence."

e: in order to facilitate; so as to make convenient; so that
d: 以 (in order to) + 便 (convenient; to facilitate). Introduces a purpose clause describing how the preceding action creates favorable conditions for what follows. Register: formal written Chinese.
Substitute tea for spirits: the accepted formula for toasting without drinking alcohol. The phrase is spoken while raising a cup of tea, acknowledging the substitution explicitly.

e: as a precaution against; in order to guard against
d: 以 (in order to) + 防 (to guard against; to defend). Often extended to 以防万一 yǐfáng wànyī , "in order to guard against the one-in-ten-thousand chance," i.e., as a just-in-case precaution. One of the most common 以 compounds in everyday written Chinese.

e: after; afterward; in the future; from now on
d: 以 (positional marker) + 后 (behind; after). The paired counterpart to 以前. Stands alone for "in the future" or follows a time reference for "after X." Compare: 之后 zhīhòu (slightly more classical feel; often interchangeable) and 后来 hòulái (what happened next in a narrative , retrospective only).

e: in order to avoid; so as to prevent; lest
d: 以 (in order to) + 免 (to avoid; to exempt from). Introduces a clause describing what the preceding action is intended to prevent. Appears in instructions, warnings, and formal recommendations.

e: before; previously; in the past; formerly
d: 以 yǐ (by means of; from; at) + 前 qián (front; before). "From the front / from before": the time that stands in front of the present moment. The most versatile and common temporal use of 前. Used after a specific time phrase (三年以前, three years ago) or alone (以前, in the past, formerly).

h: 以前 · 现在 · 以后
e: before · now · after: the relative frame
d: 以前 and 以后 attach to any reference point: 三年以前 (three years ago), 吃饭以后 (after eating), or stand alone to mean "formerly" and "from now on". 的时候 de shíhou (when …) frames simultaneity: 我小的时候 (when I was little).

e: above (a number); the above-mentioned; and more
d: 以 yǐ (from; by means of; at) + 上 shàng (above; higher). Used after a number or category to mean "and above" or "the following." Three uses: quantitative (三十以上 = thirty or more), sequential (如以上所述 = as stated above), and categorical (十八岁以上 = eighteen and older).

e: above / the above-mentioned · below / the following · more than / less than
d: 以上 yǐshàng (以 + 上 above): covers both spatial above and "more than a quantity" (十八岁以上 , 18 and above) and "what has been stated above" in written discourse (以上是本次报告的主要内容 , the above is the main content of this report). 以下 yǐxià mirrors it exactly in the opposite direction.

以 (taking) + 为 (to be; to regard as). In classical Chinese the construction meant "to regard X as Y." In modern speech, 以为 has narrowed to almost always imply that the assumption turned out to be wrong , making it a useful signal of correction or disappointment.

e: self-centered; to place oneself at the center

d: 以 yǐ (from; from this point) + 下 xià (below; the following). Three uses mirror exactly those of its counterpart 以上: quantitative (十八岁以下 = under eighteen), sequential (以下是通知 = the following is an announcement), and organizational. The pair 以上/以下 frames all formal Chinese enumeration.

A bilingual contract needs a clause saying which version prevails if they conflict (如有冲突 rú yǒu chōngtū). Chinese courts and arbitrators work in Chinese, so the Chinese text is the one that will be read. Have it translated back to you independently rather than trusting that the two versions match.

e: a righteous act; a just cause; a deed done for principle
d: 义 (righteous) + 举 (act; move; deed; to raise up). A deed that rises to the level of a principled act , something done not for personal gain but for a cause recognized as right. Often used of charitable acts, acts of solidarity, or historical deeds that defended the weak or resisted injustice.

e: loyalty among friends; the code of doing right by your people
d: 义 (righteousness; what is right) + 气 (spirit; energy; disposition). The disposition to do right by the people bound to you , friends, brothers, colleagues, sworn companions. 义气 operates in a different register from 正义: where 正义 is institutional and universal, 义气 is personal and relational.

e: a righteous person; a man of principle; one who sacrifices for a just cause
d: 义 (righteousness) + 士 (a person of standing; an educated or principled person). Someone whose defining quality is acting on principle rather than self-interest, particularly at personal cost. 义士 is a term of high historical admiration.

义 (what is right) + 务 (affair; task; work). The affair of doing what is right , the tasks that fall to you not because you chose them but because they are the right ones for someone in your position. 义务 spans the full range from formal legal obligation to moral duty.

e: One hundred million, the great unit above 万
d: One hundred million, the great unit above 万. China's population is 十四亿 (shísì yì, 1.4 billion), a figure every learner should be able to parse and produce.

e: to comment on; to talk about (often behind the scenes)
d: 议 yì (to deliberate, to propose) + 论. To comment on or talk about something, frequently with an undertone of gossip or unsolicited opinion. 议论纷纷 yìlùn fēnfēn describes a crowd buzzing with opinions. Also the name of a school essay genre: 议论文 yìlùnwén, the argumentative essay.

e: change; easy; the name of the text itself
d: The single character at the heart of the entire system. The commentary tradition insists it holds three meanings at once: 变易 biànyì (the fact of change, everything transforms), 不易 bùyì (the unchanging principle behind change, the laws of transformation are constant), and 简易 jiǎnyì (the simplicity be…

The "Yi-an style": the distinctive lyric mode of Li Qingzhao (whose courtesy name was Yi-an 易安). Characterized by colloquial precision, physical specificity, and a technically innovative use of reduplicated binomes to convey emotional states.
意 yì (notion) + 见 jiàn (to see; view). What the mind sees on a matter, that is, a considered opinion: 提意见 "to offer a view." It can lean negative, where 有意见 means to have a complaint or grievance.

e: the poetic realm — atmosphere, mood, and implied space
d: 意 yì (meaning; intention; feeling) + 境 jìng (realm; situation; space). The characteristic Chinese aesthetic concept of the space created beyond the words themselves: what the poem evokes rather than describes. Good poetry has 意境; pedestrian verse merely reports facts.

e: "the intention has arrived" — the gesture is enough; the thought counts
d: Used to accept a gift graciously without demanding more, or to reassure a giver that their token gesture was sufficient and appreciated. Conveys: "I see your heart in this; the object is secondary." Also used reflexively by givers: 意思到了就好 , "as long as the intention is communicated, that's enough."

e: a token gesture; to make a symbolic offering; "just a little something"
d: Reduplication softens and miniaturizes the meaning , a universal Chinese pattern. 意思意思 as a verb phrase means "to make a token gesture, to acknowledge the relationship symbolically." It signals effort without demanding reciprocal debt.

意 yì (notion; expectation) + 外 wài (outside). Outside what the heart anticipated, hence unexpected: 意外的消息 "surprising news." As a noun it names an accident or mishap that fell beyond anyone's reckoning.
Image, imagistic motif. Tang criticism valued the evocative image (意象) over explicit statement , show, don't tell, carried to its highest refinement.

意 (intention) + 义 (righteousness; principle). More serious and weighty than 意思. 意义 refers to significance in the deeper sense , the kind that requires reflection. Used for historical significance, life meaning, moral weight. 人生的意义 (the meaning of life) uses 意义, never 意思.

The intention precedes the brush: the principle that a painter must have fully conceived the work before beginning to paint, because ink on xuan paper cannot be corrected. Applies equally to calligraphy.

"Therefore" or "for this reason." More formal than 所以, common in written and considered spoken contexts. Often used to introduce a conclusion drawn from preceding points: 因此, 我们决定… ("therefore, we decided…").
因 yīn (because of) + 而 ér (and so). A written connective that draws a result from a stated cause, close to 因此 but smoother in flowing prose: 准备充分，因而很顺利 "well prepared, and so it went smoothly."
因 yīn (cause) + 果 guǒ (fruit; result). The cause-and-effect pair as a single concept, from the everyday 因果关系 "causal relationship" to the Buddhist law of karma, where every act ripens into its fruit.
因 yīn (cause) + 素 sù (element). One of the contributing causes that feed into an outcome, used of the many partial causes behind a complex result: 经济因素 "economic factors," 不安全因素 "safety hazards."

因 yīn (cause; reason; because of) + 为 wèi (for; on account of). The most important conjunction in the language for expressing cause. Pairs with 所以 suǒyǐ (therefore) to form the standard causal construction: 因为 X，所以 Y (because X, therefore Y).

e: the underworld; the realm of the dead
the lunar calendar; the traditional Chinese calendar
d: 阴 yīn (moon; lunar) + 历 lì (calendar). The traditional calendar reckoned by the phases of the moon, as opposed to the 阳历 (yánglì, the sun-based Gregorian calendar). Strictly the Chinese traditional calendar is 阴阳合历 (a combined lunisolar calendar), but in everyday speech 阴历 is what people call it.

e: shady and cool; a shaded cool spot
d: 阴 yīn (shade) + 凉 liáng (cool). Shaded and pleasantly cool, the welcome shade of a tree on a hot day. Here the shadow is entirely positive, the relief the shaded slope offers in summer.

e: conspiracy; sinister plot; scheme operating in darkness
d: 阴 yīn (dark; covert; hidden) + 谋 móu (to plot; to scheme). A plan that operates in shadow, unseen , the hidden face that 阴 takes when it manifests as human deception. The contrast with open, legitimate action (which would be 阳) is built into the word.

阴 yīn (shaded; clouded) + 天 tiān (sky; day; weather). A day when clouds cover the sun, the most concrete everyday use of 阴. This is the original geographic shade made meteorological: the whole sky becomes the shaded slope.

e: yin deficiency — the yin coolant is insufficient; yang heat dominates
d: 虚 xū = deficient; empty; insufficient. Classic 阴虚 symptoms: heat sensations in the palms and soles of feet (五心烦热), night sweats (盗汗 dào hàn), dry mouth and throat, redness of the cheeks in the afternoon, irritability, insomnia.

e: harmony of yin and yang; the ideal state of health and well-being
d: 调 tiáo (to tune; to harmonize; to adjust) + 和 hé (harmony; peace). The goal of all Chinese medical practice: not the maximization of either force, but their active, dynamic harmony. 调和 is active , it is a verb about process, not a noun describing a state.

e: balance of yin and yang; the state of dynamic equilibrium
d: The core goal in 阴阳 thinking is not the elimination of one force or the dominance of the other , it is 平衡 pínghéng: dynamic balance between them. This is not static equilibrium (like a scale perfectly level) but living balance (like a tightrope walker, constantly adjusting).

e: yin-yang and the Five Phases — the paired cosmological framework
d: The two systems developed in parallel during the Warring States period and were synthesized into a unified framework by the Han dynasty, particularly in the 黄帝内经 (Yellow Emperor's Classic, compiled ca. 200 BCE–200 CE).

e: shadow; a shadow over the heart; a lingering trauma
d: 阴 yīn (shade) + 影 yǐng (shadow; image). A literal shadow, the dark shape cast where light is blocked, and also a medical shadow on an X-ray (肺部阴影, a shadow on the lung).

Music + 会 (gathering), usually implying the classical hall; a pop star's arena show is a 演唱会 (yǎnchànghuì, "performed-singing gathering"). Tickets for either are 票, and 抢票 ("snatching tickets") describes the purchase experience accurately.

音乐 yīnyuè (music) + 家 jiā. Implies serious, dedicated musical mastery: a composer, a concert performer, a conductor rather than a casual musician. Distinguished from 歌手 gēshǒu (singer/pop artist) by the 家 suffix, which implies depth, discipline, and classical standing.
音 yīn (sound; word) + 信 xìn (message; letter). News or word of someone far away. Most common in the negative: 没有音信 "no word at all," and the idiom 杳无音信, vanished without a trace.
银 (yín, silver) + 河 (river). A silver river across the night sky. Chinese named the galaxy as a river of stars long before it was a galaxy, and the metaphor stuck.

银 yín (silver) + 行 háng. The silver-row , originally a row of money-changers along a market street, then by extension the modern banking institution. The single most-tested 行-háng word: students who default to xíng on every 行 will read this wrong forever.

e: to introduce; to bring in (technology, talent, methods)
d: 引 yǐn (to draw; to lead) + 进 jìn (to take in). To bring something in from outside, typically from abroad: 引进技术 "introduce technology," 引进人才 "bring in talent."

e: yum cha; going for dim sum; drinking tea

d: 饮食 yǐnshí (food and drink, diet) + 文化 (culture). Chinese food culture is one of the most discussed topics in 文化 discourse , not just cuisine but the entire social system of eating: banquet etiquette, regional identity, seasonal eating, the pairing of food with medicine and philosophy.
Seal paste: the vermilion medium used to ink seals. Made from cinnabar 朱砂 (mercuric sulfide), sesame oil, and mugwort fiber. The highest-quality seal paste is made in Zhangzhou, Fujian.

e: scenting — the process of infusing tea with flower fragrance
ought to; should; be obliged to
d: 应 yīng (should) + 当 dāng (be fitting). A modal of obligation, near-identical in meaning to 应该 yīnggāi but slightly more formal, so it shows up often in rules, contracts, and writing.

e: to cope with; to handle; to deal with
d: 应 yìng (to meet) + 付 fù (to hand over, to deal out). To handle a task or person, often a difficult one. Can carry a tinge of just getting through it: 应付考试 (manage to get through the exam), 应付了事 (do something perfunctorily just to be done with it).
英 yīng (outstanding; heroic; talent that flowers) + 明 míng (luminous). The compound used to praise rulers, commanders, and decision-makers of exceptional vision. 英明的领导 "an enlightened leader."

e: valiant and impressive; heroic in bearing
d: 英 yīng (heroic, outstanding) + 武 wǔ (martial). Of a person, valiant and impressive in look and manner, the brave, spirited bearing of a hero or a fine soldier: 英武不凡 "valiant and out of the ordinary." A literary, admiring word, often used of a young officer or commander.

e: to welcome, to go out to meet
d: 迎 (yíng, to go toward) + 接 (to receive). You walk out to meet an arrival and bring them in. Often warm or ceremonial: greeting guests, soldiers, the new year.

e: to own; to cherish; to hold close
d: 拥 yōng (to embrace; to hold close; to crowd together) + 有. More emotionally warm than 所有 or 具有. Suggests not just legal or abstract possession but holding something dear. Used for things of personal value: relationships, opportunities, qualities of character, cherished experiences.

e: third Ming emperor, builder of Beijing
Yongming Yanshou (904–975 CE) — Song dynasty Chan-Pure Land synthesis
d: The sixth patriarch of Pure Land and a major Chan master simultaneously, Yanshou embodied the Chinese Buddhist principle that the two traditions are not opposed but complementary.
用 yòng (to use) + 法 fǎ (way). The way a thing is properly used, especially a word or a tool: 这个词的用法 "the usage of this word." Built on the same "way of doing" sense as 方法.

e: to study hard; to work diligently; to apply oneself
d: 用 yòng (to use; to deploy) + 功 gōng (effort; merit; achievement). To deploy effort , the literal meaning maps exactly onto the English "to apply oneself." Used particularly of students and academic work, but extends to any disciplined sustained effort.

e: to exert force; to use one's strength; hard (of physical effort)
d: 用 yòng (to use) + 力 lì (force). To put physical force into an action: 用力推 "push hard," 用力拉 "pull with all your strength." Describes how an action is done, with muscle behind it.

用 yòng (use; function) + 途 tú (route; destination; intended course). The destination of deployment: what something is for, where its use is headed. 用途 answers the question "what is this for?" and tends to describe a range of applications rather than a single act of using.
优 yōu (excellent) + 点 diǎn (point). A good point, a strength. Its exact opposite is 缺点 quēdiǎn, a shortcoming. Together they are the standard pair for weighing a person, plan, or product.

优质 yōuzhì (excellent quality , 优 excellent + 质 substance/quality) is the premium tier modifier. 打造优质产品 (to build premium products) is a common mission statement. Contrasts with 劣质产品 (lièzhì chǎnpǐn, inferior-quality products) , counterfeit or substandard goods.

尤 yóu (outstanding; especially) + 其 qí (that; those). "Especially that" , used to single out one item from a broader set as particularly true or notable. Appears before verbs, adjectives, or noun phrases. Roughly equivalent to "particularly" or "above all."

e: due to; owing to; because of
d: 由 yóu (from) + 于 yú (at; in). A formal, written near-synonym of 因为, marking the cause at the front of a sentence: 由于天气原因，航班取消了 "owing to the weather, the flight was cancelled." It pairs with 因此 rather than 所以.

邮 yóu (post; mail) + 件 jiàn (a piece). Originally any item sent through the post. In everyday modern use it most often means email: 电子邮件 diànzǐ yóujiàn (electronic mail) is regularly shortened to 邮件. To send one is 发邮件 fā yóujiàn.

e: postage stamp: a stamp for mailing letters
d: 邮 yóu (post; mail) + 票 piào (slip). A postage stamp: a tiny printed slip stuck to an envelope that stands for prepaid postage. It is 票 in miniature, a small piece of paper carrying a fixed value, and a favorite object of collectors (集邮 jíyóu, stamp collecting).
油 yóu (oil) + 画 huà (painting). The Western art of painting in oils, named for its medium. Its native counterpart is 国画 guóhuà, named for its nation rather than its material.
友 yǒu (friend) + 情 qíng (feeling). The bond of friendship. Close to 友谊 yǒuyì in meaning, but 友情 leans on the felt warmth, while 友谊 leans on the formal relationship.

e: to make sense; to be reasonable; that's a fair point
d: 有 yǒu (to have; there is) + 道理 dàolǐ (reason; logic). "To have reason," to possess the quality of making sense. One of the most common spoken responses to an argument you find convincing, used the way "fair point," "that makes sense," and "good point" function in English.

有 + 的 (nominalizing particle). Functions as an indefinite partitive , "some of [a set already mentioned or implied]." The pattern 有的…有的… (some…others…) distributes a set into contrasting subgroups and is one of the most natural ways to express "some people…some people…" in Chinese.

e: a bit; slightly (pre-verbal, negative or complaint coloring)
d: 有 + 点 diǎn (a dot; a small amount). Always appears before verbs and adjectives as a pre-modifier. The key nuance: 有点 carries a slightly negative or complaint-inflected tone. You use it for problems, inconveniences, or things that fall short.

Placed before an adjective (or a feeling-verb) to say something is "a bit / somewhat" that way, usually with a tinge of complaint or an unwanted state. 有点儿 + 累 / 冷 / 贵 / 难 = a bit tired / cold / expensive / hard. It describes a current condition the speaker finds slightly undesirable.

e: to be related; to matter; to have a bearing on
d: 有关系 means there is a connection, relevance, or effect between two things. 这跟我有关系吗？= "Does this concern me / affect me?" Used to establish relevance, causation, or connection. Contrast with 有关 yǒuguān (related to; concerning , slightly more formal, often in 有关部门, "relevant departments").
有 (to have) + 害 (harm): possessing the capacity to wound. Its antonym 无害 (wúhài) marks a thing as harmless. Frequent on labels and in science writing.

e: "Keep in touch when you have time
d: "Keep in touch when you have time." Slightly more open-ended than 改天再聊. Suggests that contact will resume when both schedules permit. Polite and standard.

有 yǒu (to have) + 礼貌. The default form of approval for someone's social bearing. Applied across the age range , to children, colleagues, strangers, foreigners , and across formality levels. 这个孩子很有礼貌 ("this child is very polite") is a high compliment to the parents as much as to the child.

e: do you have? / is there? (A-not-A question)
d: The A-not-A question form of 有. Used both for possession ("do you have X?") and for existence ("is there X?"). In rapid speech, 有没有 is often compressed or the object follows immediately: 有没有时间？ Also used as a sentence-final tag: 你来过北京，有没有？ — "You've been to Beijing, haven't you?"

e: to have face; to be prestigious; to feel honored
d: To possess and display face , to be in a position of recognized prestige or to feel that your standing has been acknowledged or elevated. Certain possessions, positions, and associations give face: luxury goods, titles, famous friends, prestigious education.

有 yǒu (to have; to possess) + 名 míng (name; fame). To have a name that people know , the most common adjective for "famous" in spoken Mandarin. Neutral in register, works for people, places, dishes, and brands alike.

e: there is someone; someone (existential + indefinite reference)
d: 有 in the existential construction introduces a person into the discourse. 有人 can function as the subject of a following verb: 有人说… (Someone said…; There are people who say…). This is a common way to introduce an indefinite agent , "some people say," "someone thinks," "there are those who believe."

有 + 时 shí (time). One of the most basic time adverbs: "at some times; sometimes." Often appears in the paired pattern 有时…有时… (sometimes…sometimes…) to describe alternating or variable states. 有时候 yǒu shíhou is the slightly more colloquial form (literally "at some time-instances").
"Sometimes," literally "there are times." Often shortened to 有时. The paired form 有时候…有时候… means "sometimes… and other times…," a neat way to describe alternating situations.

e: to be busy; to have something come up; to have a matter to attend to
d: 有 yǒu (have) + 事 shì. "Have a matter." Used to beg off (something has come up) or to flag that you need something from someone: 我有事找你 "I have something to discuss with you."

e: somewhat; to some extent; there is some degree of
capable; purposeful; with ambition and scope to act; achieving
d: 有 yǒu (to have; to possess) + 为 wéi (action; doing; purposeful agency). The counterpart to 无为 , intentional, directed, deliberate action.

e: there's a problem; there's a question
d: The genuinely ambiguous phrase: it can mean "I have a question" or "there's a problem / something's wrong," and only context disambiguates. 有问题吗？after an explanation means "any questions?"; 这里有问题 about a machine means "there's a problem here."

e: to have hope; to be promising
d: "There is hope," used of a situation that may yet turn out well: 病人还有希望 ("the patient still has hope"). It can also mean "promising" of a person or prospect: 这孩子很有希望 ("this child is very promising"). The negative 没有希望 ("there's no hope") and the verb 失望 ("to be let down") sit on the other side.
How long a quote holds. Factories tie it to material prices, especially steel, and to the exchange rate (汇率 huìlǜ). A quote with no date can be reopened at any time.
Lit. "has meaning/appeal." The go-to word for "interesting" in casual spoken Chinese. Used for books, films, people, topics, situations , anything with engaging appeal.

e: nirvana with remainder; liberation while still embodied
d: 有余 (with a remainder) + 涅槃. The state of an awakened person, an arhat or a buddha, who has extinguished the three fires but still carries a body whose karmic momentum continues. The Buddha after his awakening at Bodh Gayā lived for forty more years; that life was 有余涅槃.

e: to have a karmic connection; fated to meet
d: 有缘 means that a karmic connection exists between people , that the conditions for their meeting were in place.

e: both red and expert; politically loyal and professionally capable
d: 又 yòu...又 yòu (both...and) framing 红 (red, politically reliable) and 专 zhuān (expert, specialized). A defining slogan of the Mao era: the ideal cadre or worker was supposed to be ideologically loyal and technically skilled at once.

Deployed at the first bars of a familiar tune: the uncle's stock speech, the app's renewal popup, the roommate's diet announcement. 你又来了 aims it at a person, affection and exasperation mixed to taste.

e: the right side; on the right
d: 右 (right) + 边 (side; edge). The neutral everyday word for "the right side." 在右边 (on the right), 右边的窗户 (the window on the right). The paired form 左边 zuǒbiān (the left side) appears constantly alongside it.

右 (right) + 派 (faction, school, stream). Modern political term adopted from Western usage. In PRC political history, 右派 took on specific weight during the Anti-Rightist Campaign (反右运动 Fǎn Yòu Yùndòng, 1957–1959) launched after the Hundred Flowers Campaign.

右 (right) + 手 (hand). The right hand , the dominant hand in the original character, the hand raised to the mouth. In Chinese calligraphy instruction, 右手执笔 (hold the brush with the right hand) was the standard prescription.

e: thereupon; as a result; and so
d: 于 yú (at; in; given) + 是 (this; the situation). Classical origin: "at this point; given this situation." A narrative conjunction that advances a story , signaling consequence or the next development in a sequence. Slightly formal register.

e: Ullambana vessel; the Buddhist festival name
Ghost Festival — the great Buddhist-folk religion synthesis
d: Held on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month, the midpoint of the "Ghost Month" 鬼月 during which the spirits of the dead are believed to return to the world of the living. Families set out food offerings, burn paper goods, and float river lanterns to guide the spirits.
娱 yú (to amuse) + 乐 lè (joy). Entertainment or recreation, both the activities and the having of fun: 娱乐活动 "recreational activities," 娱乐圈 "the entertainment world."
渔 (to fish) + 船 (boat): a boat worked for the catch. 渔 carries the water radical 氵, marking the act of fishing, distinct from 鱼 the fish itself.

渔 yú (to fish) + 夫 fū (man). A man who makes his living by fishing. Like 农夫 it has a timeless, story-book ring, and it features in the famous proverb about the fisherman who profits while the snipe and the clam are locked in struggle.

愉 yú (pleased; at ease; the heart-radical with a sound component suggesting relaxed breathing) + 快 kuài (unobstructed joy). More refined and slightly more formal than 快乐. The word you reach for when describing an experience, a meeting, or an atmosphere as genuinely pleasant.

舆 yú (the common people; literally a carriage, by extension the public) + 论. The collective voice of the public on an issue: public opinion as a force. 舆论压力 yúlùn yālì "pressure of public opinion," 引导舆论 yǐndǎo yúlùn "to guide public opinion."

与 yǔ (with; and; compare) + 其 qí (that). "Compared with that" , introduces the rejected alternative in a preference structure. Almost always paired with 不如 bùrú (not as good as; better to) or 宁可 nìngkě (would rather). The full construction: 与其 A, 不如 B , "rather than A, better to B."

e: rather than waiting, it's better to act
d: The simplest pattern: verb phrases on both sides. 与其 + action to reject, 不如 + action to recommend. The rhetorical punch: waiting is rejected as the inferior choice; action is endorsed.
The universe: 宇 all space, 宙 all time, per the Huainanzi's definition. 元宇宙 (yuán yǔzhòu) is the metaverse, the newest tenant in a very old word.

e: ascension to Heaven — her death and deification
d: In 987 CE, at age twenty-seven or twenty-eight, Lin Mo climbed Meizhou Island's highest point. Witnesses reported hearing celestial music (仙乐 xiānyuè) and seeing her surrounded by colored clouds as she ascended into the sky.
语 yǔ (language; speech) + 法 fǎ (rule; law). The "law of language," the system of rules by which a language is built. The same 法 of fixed standard, here governing how words combine.

e: tone of voice; grammatical mood; modal register
d: 语 yǔ (language; speech) + 气 qì. The qi of language, how something is said rather than what. In grammatical analysis, 语气 = mood (indicative, imperative, interrogative).

e: language arts; Chinese (as a school subject)
d: 语 yǔ (language; speech) + 文 wén (writing; culture; literature). The Chinese school subject covering reading, writing, classical texts, and composition , the equivalent of "English" class in an English-speaking curriculum, but broader in scope because it encompasses classical Chinese literature along…

语 yǔ (language; speech; to tell) + 言 yán (speech; words). The word for language as a structured system , grammar, vocabulary, and everything that makes communication possible across a community. 语言 is used in academic, formal, and everyday contexts alike. 语言学 yǔyánxué = linguistics.

Factory staff often send long voice messages. 转文字 (zhuǎn wénzì) converts a voice message to text inside WeChat (press and hold the message), and the result is easy to paste into a translator. Asking for text is acceptable when phrased as your limitation.

e: the Jade Emperor — supreme deity of the folk pantheon
d: The Jade Emperor is the supreme ruler of Heaven in Chinese folk religion, governing both the divine and human realms from his celestial palace. His court mirrors a full imperial bureaucracy: he has ministers, generals, and a vast apparatus of supernatural governance.

e: to book in advance; to reserve; to schedule
d: 预 yù (beforehand) + 定 dìng (to settle). To settle something ahead of time: a table, a room, a plan. Often written 预订 when the matter booked is goods or tickets. The 预 fixes the settling in the future.

e: primordial qi; vitality; the reserves of life force
d: 元 yuán (origin; primary; first) + 气 qì. In cosmology: the undifferentiated qi before heaven and earth separated, the primordial substrate of existence. In medicine: the constitutional qi inherited from one's parents, stored in the kidneys, spent by illness and restored by rest.
Element: "original plain-stuff." Beyond the lab it means element in the design sense too: 中国元素 (Chinese elements) is the stock phrase for Chinese motifs in fashion or film.

e: originally; as it turns out; so that's how it is
d: 原 yuán (original; the root; where something came from) + 来 lái (came from; arrived from). "From the original state," used in two senses. Temporal: originally, at first (他原来住在北京 = He originally lived in Beijing). Revelatory: "so that's how it is / now I understand" (原来如此！= So that's the reason!).

e: "Oh, so that's how it is!" or "I see now
d: "Oh, so that's how it is!" or "I see now." The classic "aha" of comprehension. The pieces have just clicked together. Slightly literary in feel but used constantly in everyday speech. The looser 原来是这样 (yuánlái shì zhèyàng) is the more colloquial version.

e: original form; true shape (often the one revealed)
d: 原 yuán (original) + 形 xíng. The original form a thing had before it was disguised or altered. The vivid idiom 原形毕露 yuánxíng bìlù means "the true shape is fully exposed," said when a deception finally collapses and someone is seen for what they really are.
原 yuán (origin; source) + 因 yīn (cause). The standard noun for the cause or reason behind something: 失败的原因 "the reason for the failure." Its pair is 结果 jiéguǒ, the result.
The first thing to ask for. 根本原因 (gēnběn yuányīn) is the root cause; an answer like 工人操作不当 (worker error) usually is not one. Ask why the process allowed the error.
Signals agreement on direction while keeping the details open. Useful when the boss pushes for a handshake before the numbers are settled.

e: perfect stillness; the death of a monk

d: Pi: "circle-circumference ratio," usually written π and read pài in class. Zu Chongzhi's 355/113 approximation is taught to every Chinese student as a point of scientific heritage.

Round table , the standard configuration for Chinese group dining. 圆 means "round" or "complete"; 桌 means "table." The round form eliminates a linear head seat and places all diners in a radial relationship to the shared dishes at the center.

e: military strongman who hijacked the republic
the karmic connection is not yet exhausted; there is still fate between us
d: 未 wèi = not yet; 尽 jìn = exhausted, used up. The karmic thread still has length to run , the connection between two people has not reached its natural conclusion.

e: the karmic connection is exhausted; the fate between us has run its course
d: 已 yǐ = already; the connection has used up its allotted length. A peaceful, fatalistic way to accept a relationship ending , romantic, platonic, or professional.

e: fate vs. destiny — predestined connection vs. decreed outcome
d: 缘分 yuánfèn (predestined affinity; see the dedicated entry) and 命运 mìngyùn (fate) are related but distinct. 缘分 is about connections between people, encounters that were meant to be. 命运 is about one's overall life trajectory, the arc of what happens.

e: reason; cause; the why behind something
d: 缘 (yuán, cause, affinity, the edge along which things connect) + 故 (cause, reason). A two-character word for the reason behind an event, slightly more formal and reflective than the everyday 原因 (yuányīn).

e: dependent origination; origin; the arising through causes and conditions
d: The Buddhist technical term for pratītyasamutpāda , the arising of phenomena through causes and conditions. In everyday use, 缘起 also means simply "the origin" or "how something came about." Both usages share the underlying idea that nothing simply begins from nothing; everything has prior causes.

Source, literally "source head." The Yangtze's source was definitively surveyed only in the 1970s–80s, deep in the Tanggula Mountains on the Tibetan Plateau. The identification of a river's 源头 carries cosmological weight; knowing where a river begins is knowing something fundamental about the world.

e: in the distance; a distant place
d: 远 yuǎn (far) + 处 chù (place; location). The place that is far away, viewed from where you stand. A positional noun used as a subject or object, always indicating a vague far-off point rather than a named destination.

e: ambitious; far-reaching; grand (of goals or ideals)
d: 远 yuǎn (far) + 大 dà (great; large). Applied to goals, plans, and ideals that extend far into the future or require enormous scope to realize.

e: a distant place; far-off land; the faraway
d: 远 yuǎn (far) + 方 fāng (direction; region; place). More evocative than 远处: 远方 carries a tone of longing or aspiration. Where 远处 names a physical spot in view, 远方 names a horizon you are drawn toward. Common in poetry, lyrics, and travel writing.

e: remote antiquity; the distant ancient past
d: 远 yuǎn (far, remote) + 古 gǔ (ancient). The very distant past, the dim and often legendary beginnings before clear historical record: 远古时代 "remote antiquity," 远古传说 "ancient myths and legends." Reaches further back than 古代, toward the edge of memory.

e: to keep far from; to stay away from; to leave behind
d: 远 yuǎn (far) + 离 lí (to leave; to separate from). A deliberate act of putting distance between yourself and something: a place, a person, a habit. Carries volition. Used in health campaigns (远离烟酒, stay away from tobacco and alcohol), personal advice, and literature.
远 yuǎn (distant) + 亲 qīn (kin; close; intimate). A relative at the outer edge of the family network.

e: to be willing; to want to
d: 愿 yuàn (to wish) + 意 yì (intent). The willingness of the heart to do something: 我愿意帮你 "I'm willing to help you." It expresses consent and readiness, not mere ability.

月 yuè + 饼 bǐng (flat cake; pastry). The round cake eaten during Mid-Autumn Festival, shaped to mirror the full moon. Traditional fillings include lotus seed paste and salted egg yolk (representing the moon).

月 yuè + 光 guāng (light; beam; glory). Moonlight. One of the most evocative words in Chinese poetry , from Du Fu to Xu Zhimo, moonlight is the quintessential image of homesickness, longing, and beauty.

e: the Old Man Under the Moon; deity of marriage and romantic fate
d: 月 yuè (moon) + 老 lǎo (old; elderly; venerable). Yuèlǎo appears at night under the moon, checking his celestial book of destined marriages, and tying the red threads that will unite couples across any distance. 拜月老 (to pray to Yuèlǎo) is a common practice among those seeking romantic fate.

月 yuè + 亮 liàng (bright; to shine). The bright moon , the standard colloquial word for "the moon." More grounded and everyday than the poetic 明月 míngyuè. 看月亮 "to look at the moon" · 月亮出来了 "the moon has come out."

e: City God of Hangzhou — the martyr general
d: 岳飞 (1103–1142), the Song dynasty general celebrated for his campaigns against the Jurchen Jin invaders, was executed on fabricated charges at the order of the chancellor Qin Hui.

e: to read (with comprehension); reading (as a skill)
d: 阅 yuè (to inspect; to review) + 读. The formal, written-register word for reading-with-understanding. The standard term in education: 阅读理解 yuèdú lǐjiě "reading comprehension," 阅读量 yuèdú liàng "amount one has read." More deliberate than 看 (to look-at) and more comprehension-focused than 读 alone.

e: life experience; seasoned knowledge of the world
d: 阅 yuè (to read; to review; to inspect) + 历 lì (what one has gone through). The accumulated worldly experience a person builds up over the years: the breadth of life seen and understood, not just events lived but their lessons absorbed.

粤 yuè (Guangdong; Canton) + 菜 cài (cuisine). The cooking of Guangdong, prized for lightness, freshness, and steaming that keeps each ingredient tasting of itself. Dim sum (点心) belongs to this tradition.

e: to cross over; to get past
d: 越 + 过 (guò, to pass). The most basic verb of crossing: a fence, a stream, a hurdle, a difficulty. Highly productive in both literal and figurative senses.

e: to cross a boundary; to overstep

d: 越 + 权 (quán, authority; power). Acting beyond what your position permits , a serious accusation in any organization, especially in the bureaucratic hierarchies that have shaped Chinese institutional life since imperial times.

e: sport; exercise; to work out; a (social or political) movement
d: 运 yùn (to move; to transport) + 动 dòng (to move). Bodily exercise and sport: 做运动 "to exercise," 运动员 yùndòngyuán (athlete). The same word names an organized social or political movement, a mass of people set in motion.
海运 (hǎiyùn) is sea freight, 空运 (kōngyùn) air freight, 快递 (kuàidì) express courier for samples. 货代 (huòdài) is the freight forwarder. 整柜 (zhěngguì) is a full container load, 拼柜 (pīnguì) a shared one.
运 (yùn, to transport / haul) + 河 (river). A dug waterway built to carry boats and freight, a river made by labor rather than rain. The Grand Canal is 大运河 (dà yùnhé).

运 yùn (fortune in motion) + 气 qì (vital energy; breath; atmosphere). Fortune as a flow of qi: luck circulates rather than sitting still. 好运气 = good luck; 坏运气 = bad luck. 运气好 = to be lucky; 靠运气 = to rely on luck.
运 (move, transport) plus 送 (send). To carry goods or people over a distance, the language of logistics, supply lines, and freight.

e: to apply; to put into practice; to exercise (a skill)
d: 运 yùn (to move; to carry; to transport; to operate) + 用 yòng (to use). To bring knowledge or skill into active operation: using what one knows in a real context. Where 使用 is about deploying a tool, 运用 is about skillfully exercising something more abstract , a theory, a method, a body of knowledge.
杂 zá (mixed; miscellaneous) + 草 cǎo (grass). The unwanted, untended grass that crowds a garden or field, the plants you pull out rather than plant. 拔杂草 "to pull weeds."

e: prime minister (of imperial times); chief minister
d: 宰 zǎi (to govern; to manage) + 相 xiàng (minister). The highest official under the emperor, charged with overseeing the government. A staple figure of historical drama and idiom.
The forward-looking again fused to the meet verb. Internet speech numbers it 88 (bābā, "bye-bye"), and the dramatic register upgrades to 永别 for farewells meant to be final.

e: again and again; repeatedly; over and over
d: 再 zài (again; once more) + 三 sān (three). Three times and then some: the most natural adverb of repeated action in Mandarin. Appears before a verb to signal that someone did something multiple times, often with increasing emphasis or urgency.

e: we'll talk about it later; let's deal with it when the time comes; moreover (discourse marker)
d: 再 (later; further) + 说 (to speak; to deal with). Multiple uses: (1) Deferral: 这件事以后再说 (We'll deal with this later , let's not now). Very common for postponing a conversation or decision. (2) Discourse marker meaning "moreover; besides": 再说，我也没空 (Besides, I'm not free either).

再 (again; further; additionally) + 者. A discourse connector used in formal writing and spoken argument to introduce an additional point: "and there is also this." More formal than 另外 lìngwài (besides) and slightly more deliberate in pacing than 而且 érqiě (moreover).

e: to care about; to mind; to take to heart
d: 在 (to be present) + 乎 hū (classical particle meaning "in; within; at"). Literally "to be located within [something]": one's attention or concern is present inside something. 我不在乎 (I don't care / I don't mind) is one of the most frequent phrases in spoken Chinese.

"In my view." Slightly more formal than 我觉得, and more deliberately frames what follows as a personal perspective. Useful when you want to signal that you have actually considered the question, not just reacting.

e: together (in one place); as a couple
d: With 在, 一起 marks being gathered in one place: 我们住在一起 ("we live together"), 把书放在一起 ("put the books together"). It also carries the romantic sense of being a couple: 他们在一起了 ("they're together now / they're dating").

e: to lie in; to rest with; to consist in
d: 在 zài (to be at) + 于 yú (at). Points to where the heart of a matter resides: 问题在于 "the problem lies in," 关键在于 "the key rests with." A staple of explanatory and argumentative prose.
葬 zàng (to bury; burial , the character shows plants 艹 and 死 death: vegetation covering the dead, returning them to the earth) + 礼 lǐ (rite; ceremony).

e: to suffer; to be subjected to
the Kitchen God — divine household reporter
d: The Kitchen God (also 灶王 Zàowáng or 灶君 Zàojūn) resides in the kitchen and observes the family's behavior throughout the year. On the 23rd of the 12th lunar month (one week before the new year) he ascends to Heaven to make his annual report to the Jade Emperor.

The Kitchen God , the divine household official who observes the family year-round and reports to the Jade Emperor before the Spring Festival. Propitiated with sweet foods before his image is burned and he ascends to make his report. A new image is installed when he returns on New Year's Eve.

e: to make a sentence; to compose a sentence
d: 造 zào (to make; to build) + 句 jù (sentence). The classroom exercise of building a sentence to practice a new word, a verb-object compound: 用 "因为" 造句 "make a sentence with 'because'."

噪 (clamor, wearing three mouths) + 音. The urban complaint word: construction 噪音, traffic 噪音, and the neighbor's renovation drill. 噪音污染 (noise pollution) is a recognized legal complaint category in Chinese cities.

e: how (to do something); in what way
d: The core use: placed before a verb, 怎么 asks about the method or manner of an action. 怎么走 ("how to get there"), 怎么说 ("how to say it"), 怎么用 ("how to use it").

e: no matter how; by any means; however you try
d: 怎么 (how, in what way) fronted before 都 universalizes over all methods or manners. Often used in negative or frustrated contexts: no matter what approach is tried, the result is the same. The construction can also express total permissiveness: "any way is fine."

Two fixed expressions every learner needs. 怎么了 asks "what's wrong / what happened", reacting to a change you notice, the 了 marking the new state: 你脸色怎么了？("what's up with your face / you look unwell").

"How should I put it…" Buys a moment while signaling that you are searching for the right phrasing. Implies you have a thought but are weighing how to express it, which sounds thoughtful rather than blank. Useful before delivering a nuanced opinion.

e: how is it; how about it
d: The evaluating cousin of 怎么. It asks about a state or opinion rather than a method: 这家餐厅怎么样？("how's this restaurant?"), 你最近怎么样？("how have you been?"). It also floats a suggestion: 我们去看电影，怎么样？("let's see a movie, how about it?"). Negated, 不怎么样 means "nothing special, so-so".

e: How do I get there? / Which way? — asking for directions
d: 怎么 zěnme (how; what way) + 走 zǒu (to go). The standard question for asking directions , "How do I get to X?" Response patterns: 一直走 yīzhí zǒu (go straight), 左转 zuǒzhuǎn (turn left), 右转 yòuzhuǎn (turn right), 过了红绿灯 guò le hónglǜdēng (past the traffic light). 往哪边走？= which direction to go?

e: how; in what way; what about
d: 怎 zěn (how) + 样 yàng (manner). Asks after the manner or outcome of something: 这件事你打算怎样处理 "how do you plan to handle this?" Close to 怎么 zěnme, slightly more formal.

e: to present, give as a gift
d: 赠 (bestow, present) plus 送 (give). A formal compound for presenting something gratis, common in commerce and ceremony: free gifts with purchase, donated copies, complimentary tickets.
炸 (zhá, to deep-fry) + 鸡 (chicken). The crisp street-food and fast-food staple, often eaten with 啤酒 (píjiǔ, beer) in the Korean-style 炸鸡啤酒 pairing.

e: ritual fasting and offerings — communal Daoist ceremony
d: 斋 zhāi (fasting; purification) + 醮 jiào (offering ritual). The public ritual ceremonies performed by 道士 Daoist priests on behalf of communities: for healing, protection, the release of souls from purgatory, or celebration of cosmic events.
展览 zhǎnlǎn (to exhibit) + 馆. The hall where exhibitions are mounted, cousin to the 博物馆 but temporary in what it shows.

e: divination — reading the signs between worlds
d: Divination (占卜 zhānbǔ) is a core shamanic function: reading the state of the spirit world through material signs , the cracks in a burnt shoulder blade (肩胛骨占卜 jiānjǐgǔ zhānbǔ, scapulimancy , also the origin of Shang dynasty oracle bones), the flight of birds, the behavior of flames, the patterns in…

e: Stratagems of the Warring States — the source text
pre-battle ritual — the shaman as military consultant
d: Before major military campaigns, Tungusic and Mongolian rulers consulted their shamans , divining the auspiciousness of the timing, the direction of attack, and the likely outcome.
站 (station) + 点 (diǎn, point): a designated point or node, whether a physical service point or a website. Broad and slightly technical, common in logistics, networks, and field operations.
站 (to stand) + 岗 (gǎng, a post or sentry position): to take up a guard post. A verb-object phrase, literally "to stand a post," used of soldiers, guards, and watchmen holding their station.
站 (stand) + 立 (stand): two near-synonyms stacked for emphasis, a written-register word for standing upright. More formal than plain 站, common in instructions, ceremonies, and description.
站 + 起来 (the directional complement "up"): to rise from sitting to standing. The 起来 makes the verb a completed upward motion rather than a static posture.

站 (station) + 台 (tái, raised platform): the boarding platform at a station, the raised edge alongside the track. By extension, 站台 also means to publicly back someone, to "stand on the platform" for them.
站 (station) + 长 (zhǎng, head, chief): the person in charge of a station. Originally a stationmaster; now also the administrator of a 网站, a webmaster.

e: To dip, as in dipping a dumpling into sauce (蘸酱 zhàn jiàng)
d: To dip, as in dipping a dumpling into sauce (蘸酱 zhàn jiàng). The correct word for the motion; 沾 (zhān) is a common error for this usage.

e: Han diplomat who opened the routes
to look around; to peer about
d: 张 zhāng (to open, to spread) + 望 wàng (to look). To look around searchingly, the eyes opened wide and turning in every direction: 四处张望 "to look all around." It carries a note of uncertainty or expectation, as of someone scanning a crowd for a face.

Director/CEO Zhang , the surname + 总 form is among the most useful professional address terms. 总 is short for 总经理 (general manager) or 总裁 (president/CEO). It can safely be used for any senior executive and errs on the side of flattery. Variants: 总监 zǒngjiān (director), 副总 fùzǒng (deputy director).
章 zhāng (chapter) + 节 jié (section). The structural divisions of a written work taken together. A book's text is segmented into 章 and 节 the way a stalk is segmented by its knots.

e: inside and outside the Great Wall; the agricultural vs. steppe world
d: A geographic and cultural formula that names the two worlds the wall divided: the settled, grain-farming Han civilization inside, and the pastoral, nomadic cultures of the steppe outside. 内外 encodes not just geography but an entire worldview about civilization and its boundaries.

e: length; the long and short of it
d: 长 (cháng, long) bound to 短 (duǎn, short): a paired opposite naming the dimension of length itself. Figuratively it means the rights and wrongs, or any unforeseen mishap.

e: the Yangtze River — lit. "the long river"
d: 长 cháng (long) + 江 jiāng (large river; river south of Huai River). The Yangtze, Asia's longest river at 6,300 km, is simply "the Long River." Compare: 黄河 Huáng Hé (Yellow River) is named for its color; 长江 is named for its length.

e: Battle of Changping (260 BCE) — the decisive blow against Zhao
d: The largest and most catastrophic battle of the Warring States period. Qin and Zhao forces fought for three years in the Shangdang region (modern Shanxi) before Zhao replaced its cautious commander 廉颇 Lián Pō with the aggressive 赵括 Zhào Kuò, a general who knew military theory but had never commanded…

The phrase that justifies concessions on both sides: the factory gives on price for the sake of future orders, you give on terms for the sake of a stable partner. Invoke it when asking for something; hear it as a request when the other side uses it.

丈 zhàng (an honorific for an adult man) + 夫 fū (man). The ordinary, neutral word for one's husband, the man one is married to. In older usage 大丈夫 dà zhàngfu also means a true man, a man of character, but on its own 丈夫 simply names the spouse.
收款账户 (shōukuǎn zhànghù) is the receiving account. Fraudsters impersonate suppliers by email and announce new bank details.
The thank-you at the end names the hospitality: 谢谢款待 or 谢谢您的热情招待.

找 zhǎo (to search for; to look for) + 到 dào (arrive). Searching that arrived at its target: the thing was found. 找 alone is the act of searching; 找到 is the confirmed discovery. 找不到 (can't find it) and 找到了 (found it!) are extremely high-frequency in daily speech.

e: to look for a job; to job-hunt
d: The set phrase for job-hunting. 找 (to look for) plus 工作. Common in life and conversation, especially among graduates and people changing roles: 毕业以后我要找工作 ("after I graduate I'll look for a job"). The result of a successful search is 找到工作 ("found a job"), with 到 marking the achieved result.

e: Zhaozhou's dog — the gateway kōan of Chinese Chan
d: Master Zhaozhou Congshen 赵州从谂 (778–897 CE) was asked: "Does a dog have Buddha nature?" He replied: 无 wú. Since Buddhist doctrine holds that all sentient beings have Buddha nature, "no" is doctrinally wrong , but so is "yes" if it's merely conceptual.
照 zhào (to shine upon; to illuminate) + 明 míng (bright). Used for artificial lighting systems, stage lighting, and the act of shining a light on something. 照明设备 = lighting equipment.
照 zhào (to shine; to reflect) + 相 xiàng (appearance). To fix a likeness in a picture: 给我照相 "take a photo of me." A separable verb: 照了一张相 "took one photo."

Individual scenes: excerpts from longer 昆曲 dramas performed as self-contained pieces. As the full-length drama tradition declined, individual scenes that are particularly beautiful or dramatically concentrated became the standard performance unit.

e: isn't this exactly it / this is clearly the case

d: "That's not necessarily so." A more literary pushback, often used in discussions or debates. 倒 marks the contrary tone; 未必 means "not necessarily." Slightly considered, signals careful disagreement.
这 zhè (this) + 个 ge. The demonstrative "this one," with 个 supplying the classifier slot. Its pair is 那个 nàge (that one). Often heard as a filler too, like an English "um."

"Well, this…" or "as for this…" The 嘛 particle gives the phrase a casual, considering tone. Often used to introduce a response to a question that does not have a simple answer. Roughly: "well, about that…"
这 zhè (this) + 回 huí (time). The colloquial "this time," interchangeable with 这次 zhè cì but a touch more casual: 这回我一定赢 "this time I'll win for sure."
"That's why." Used after explaining a cause to land the consequence with emphasis. 这就是为什么我不喜欢他 ("that's why I don't like him"). Slightly emphatic; signals you have just arrived at the punchline.
这 (zhè, this) + 里 (interior space) = 这里 (this place, here). 那 (nà, that) + 里 = 那里 (that place, there).

"Let me put it this way." A colloquial reframing marker, used when you are about to take another run at explaining something. The 吧 particle softens it and invites the listener to follow you into the next attempt.

e: like this; this way; so; in this manner
d: 这 zhè (this) + 样 yàng (manner). Points at a way of being or doing close at hand: 这样做 "do it like this," 就这样吧 "let it be this way, then."

着 (zháo, to be caught by) + 急 (urgency). To be seized by anxiety. This is the inward state of 急: a fretting heart, not a fast body. It is the most common everyday word for feeling worried over something time-sensitive.

e: a place to land; a resolution

d: 针 zhēn (needle) + 灸 jiǔ (moxibustion, burning dried mugwort at acupoints to warm qi). The compound covers both therapies, which are always taught together. Acupuncture inserts fine needles at specific points (穴位 xuéwèi, acupoints) along the meridians to regulate the flow of qi.

e: the eye of a needle; (medical) sty
d: 针 zhēn (needle) + 眼. The hole in a sewing needle , the same metaphor English uses. Also a colloquial term for a sty on the eyelid (the small swelling looking like a tiny eye).

e: that's really not easy; well done
d: Standard expression of admiration or sympathy for someone who has overcome difficulty: a graduation, a long project, raising children. The 真 makes it heartfelt rather than perfunctory.

e: sincere, in earnest (in attitude or expression)
d: 真 zhēn + 诚 chéng (sincerity; the Confucian virtue of inner-outer alignment). Sincere in attitude: an apology, a wish, a smile, a thank-you that is not just formal courtesy but actually meant. The diplomatic and written register.

"Seriously?" Literally "true or fake," used as an emphatic version of 真的吗 when something sounds surprising or hard to believe. Common among younger speakers and friends; slightly informal for use with elders or in professional settings.

The most common follow-up question in casual conversation, expressing surprise. 真的 on its own answers it: "Yes, really." Often softened to 真假 (zhēn jiǎ, "real or fake?") in playful or informal speech.

e: really nice; truly good; that's lovely
d: The all-purpose appreciation. 真好! works as a stand-alone exclamation: "wonderful!" 真好的人 "a really good person." 这里真好 "this place is really nice."
Double-wall insulation: the air between liner and shell is pumped out, 抽真空 (chōu zhēnkōng). 保温 is keeping warm, 保冷 keeping cold; 保温测试 is the thermal retention test, and 保温效果 the result.

真 zhēn + 理 lǐ (principle; pattern; reason). The truth in the philosophical, abstract sense , the deep principle that governs, the ultimate reality. The word used in religious, scientific, and political discourse for capital-T Truth.
真 zhēn + 实 shí (solid; real; substance). The factual register: actually-the-case, in contrast to fabricated, fictional, or virtual. Used for stories, events, identities, statistics.
Light complaint, often spoken with a sigh. The 真 marks the speaker's genuine irritation rather than a measured judgment.

e: the truth; the real state of affairs
d: 真 zhēn (true) + 相 xiàng (appearance; face). The true face of a matter once the surface is stripped away: 事情的真相 "the truth of the matter," 揭露真相 "to expose the truth."

e: a sincere heart; from the heart (adv.)
d: 真 zhēn + 心 xīn (heart). Sincerity located at the heart-level: not just attitude (真诚) but the felt inner orientation. As a noun: 一片真心 "a heart full of sincerity." As an adverb: 真心爱你 "I love you from the heart."

e: genuine, true (the real thing, not the imitation)
d: 真 zhēn + 正 zhèng (correct; proper; orthodox). The genuine-article register: this is the real one, the one that lives up to the name, not the imitation. Common attributively before nouns.

e: battle-line foundation; one's footing in a contest
d: 阵 zhèn (battle formation) + 脚. The foot of the battle line , the structural integrity of a position. The common idiom 乱了阵脚 luàn le zhènjiǎo "to lose one's footing" describes the moment a debater, athlete, or general is rattled and the formation collapses.

e: composed; calm; to keep one's cool
d: 镇 zhèn (to press down; to keep calm) + 定 dìng (settled). The steadiness of a person under pressure, a cool head when others panic: 保持镇定 "to stay composed," 镇定自若 "perfectly calm and self-possessed."

e: the Arousing — Yijing trigram for thunder

d: 拯 (zhěng, to lift up out of) + 救 (rescue). A weightier, more literary "save," used for deliverance on a grand or moral scale: saving a soul, a people, a planet.
整 zhěng (whole) + 个 gè. "The whole of" something taken as one piece: 整个城市 "the whole city," 整个晚上 "the entire evening." Here 个 keeps its sense of a single complete unit.

e: to tidy up; to sort; to put in order
d: 整 zhěng (whole; to straighten) + 理 lǐ (to put in order). To arrange scattered things back into order: 整理房间 "to tidy the room," 整理笔记 "to organize one's notes."

e: the whole; the entirety; as a whole
d: 整 zhěng (whole, complete) + 体 tǐ (body). A thing taken as one integrated body rather than as separate parts. Its standing contrast is 部分 bùfen, a part: 整体利益 "the interests of the whole."
正 zhèng (proper; upright) + 常 cháng (ordinary). On the standard track, as things should be: 一切正常 "everything is normal." Its opposite is 反常 fǎncháng or 不正常.

e: just right; exactly; as it happens
d: 正 zhèng (exactly) + 好 hǎo (good). Landing exactly on the mark of fit or timing: 大小正好 "exactly the right size," 你来得正好 "you've come at just the right moment."

e: rectification of names; calling things by their correct names
d: A key political-philosophical doctrine of Confucius. When a disciple asks what he would do first if given control of a state, Confucius says: rectify names 必也正名乎.

e: upright qi; righteous energy; moral integrity
d: 正 zhèng (upright; correct; proper) + 气 qì. In TCM: the body's defensive qi that resists pathogenic invasion. In moral discourse: the upright character and courage that resists corruption and injustice.
正 zhèng (straight; right) + 确 què (sure; firm). Correct in the sense of matching the truth or the standard: 正确答案 "the correct answer," 正确的方法 "the right method." Its opposite is 错误 cuòwù.

Traditional characters: the term used in Taiwan for the traditional character system that Taiwan retained when the PRC introduced simplified characters in the 1950s. Taiwan uses 正體字 (traditional/correct form characters); PRC uses 简体字 (simplified characters).

正 zhèng (correct; upright; proper , the character shows a foot 止 walking toward a target 一, straight on) + 义 yì (righteousness; moral rightness). Together: righteousness that is properly aligned , justice as it should be, not merely as claimed. 正义感 zhèngyìgǎn = a sense of justice.

A more formal and written version of the progressive, combining 正在 with 进行 jìnxíng (to carry out, to proceed) and 中 zhōng (amid, in the middle of). Common in announcements, project status updates, and written notices. 活动正在进行中 = the event is currently underway.

政治 zhèngzhì (politics) + 家 jiā. More elevated than 政客 zhèngkè (politician, often pejorative, implying opportunism and maneuvering). 政治家 implies vision, skill, and genuine mastery of governance: a statesman rather than a mere political operator. The 家 suffix confers dignity.
之 zhī (classical possessive) + 间 jiān (space between). The bookish, frequent way to say "between": 朋友之间 "between friends," 国与国之间 "between nations." It frames the space within a relationship or a set.

e: the reason why; the cause for which

d: The everyday acknowledgement that you have received and registered information or an instruction. Extremely common as a one-word reply. Beware the tone: a flat or clipped 知道了 can read as impatient, like "yeah, I know already." 好的 (okay) or 明白了 (understood) are gentler alternatives.

e: a bosom friend; one who truly knows you
d: 知 zhī (to know) + 己 jǐ (self). One who knows your self, the rare friend who understands you completely. The famous line 人生得一知己足矣 holds that to gain a single true friend in life is enough.

知 zhī (to know; to be known) + 名 míng (name; fame; renown). Literally: one whose name is known. 知名 sits in the formal-written register; everyday speech prefers 有名 yǒumíng (has fame) or 出名 chūmíng (name has come out). 知名度 zhīmíngdù = degree of fame, public profile.

知 zhī (to know; to understand) + 识 shí (to recognize; to discern; knowledge gained through recognition). Factual, storable, transmissible knowledge , what fills textbooks, databases, and examinations. 知识分子 zhīshi fènzǐ (intellectual; educated person , lit.

e: soulmate; the one who truly understands
d: From Boya and Ziqi: one who knows your tone. Weightier than 朋友 (friend); to call someone 知音 claims they understand what you mean beneath what you say. The lament 知音难觅 ("a zhiyin is hard to find") is the cultured way to say good friends are rare.

e: the one who knows; the wise person

d: 知 zhī (to know) + 足 zú (sufficient; foot; fullness). One of the Daodejing's most politically charged concepts: knowing when one has enough, and stopping there. The opposite of insatiable accumulation.

e: to execute; to enforce; to carry out (an order, a plan, a sentence)
d: 执 zhí (to grasp; to hold) + 行 xíng. To grasp-and-act. The formal verb for executing , orders, contracts, court rulings, software programs. 执行命令 "carry out an order"; 执行任务 "carry out a mission"; 执行总裁 (CEO) , literally "executing chief manager."
直 (zhí, straight) + 接 (join). The two ends meet with nothing in between, a straight join. As an adverb it means doing a thing with no go-between, no detour.

职 zhí (post; duty) + 业 yè (work). The line of work a person practices for a living: 职业选择 "choice of profession." As a modifier it means professional or vocational: 职业运动员 "professional athlete," 职业学校 "vocational school."

e: professional ethics; occupational morality; the moral standards specific to a role
d: 职业 zhíyè (occupation; profession; vocation) + 道德. The morality that attaches specifically to a role , what it means to be a good doctor, journalist, teacher, or official, as distinct from merely following the general rules of society.

e: spirit money — currency for the afterlife
d: 纸钱 (also 冥纸 míngzhǐ, 金纸 jīnzhǐ in Taiwan, or 冥币 míngbì) are paper facsimiles of money and goods burnt as offerings; the smoke carries them to the dead.

e: to point out the direction; to provide guidance
d: 指 (zhǐ, to point) + 明 (míng, clear) + 方向. The fixed phrase for guidance from a teacher, leader, or authority. Common in educational and political registers , a teacher 为学生指明方向, a leader 为国家指明方向. Carries a slightly elevated, often exhortatory tone.
指 (to point) + 南 (south) + 针 (needle). A south-pointing needle: the Chinese compass was designed to point south rather than north, in keeping with the cosmological primacy of the south.

至 zhì (to reach; at the extreme of) + 少 (few, little). At the minimum: "reaching the least amount." 至少要三天 (it'll take at least three days); 至少有一百人 (at least a hundred people). The counterpart is 至多 zhìduō (at most). 至少 sets a floor; 至多 sets a ceiling.

e: aspiration; ambition; the goal one is set on
d: 志 zhì (will; resolve) + 向 xiàng (direction). The direction of one's will, what one aspires to: 远大的志向 "lofty aspirations." The facing of ambition, where a person has set their life.

The most common reason a community calls a shaman is illness. In shamanic cosmology, sickness typically results from one of three spirit-world causes: soul loss (魂魄丢失 húnpò diūshī , the soul has been captured by a spirit or wandered away in fright), spirit intrusion (邪灵侵入 xiélíng qīnrù , a harmful s…
How long the factory stands behind the goods. Pair it with 验收标准 (yànshōu biāozhǔn), the acceptance standard, normally the sealed sample and an AQL level.
Short for 质量检验. 品管 (pǐnguǎn) or 品质部 is the quality department. Ask to see the inspection records (检验记录 jiǎnyàn jìlù) for a recent batch, not only the procedure.

e: quality: how good something is (also physical mass)
d: 质 zhì (substance, nature) + 量 liàng (measure). In everyday speech 质量 is quality, the standard or grade of a product or piece of work: 质量好 (good quality), 提高质量 (to raise quality). In physics the same word is the technical term for mass. Context separates the two cleanly.

e: to get rich; to make a fortune
d: 致 (to bring about, to arrive at) plus 富 (wealth). To become wealthy, especially through one's own effort. 勤劳致富 (qínláo zhìfù), getting rich through diligence, is a stock phrase.

智 zhì (wisdom; intellect) + 力 lì (power; force; strength). Intelligence framed as a measurable force: the mental capacity that can be applied, trained, and compared. 智力测试 zhìlì cèshì = intelligence test. 智力开发 zhìlì kāifā = intellectual development (especially of children).
智 zhì (intelligence) + 商 shāng (quotient , in mathematics, the result of division; also: commerce, suggesting calculation).

e: the wise person; one who possesses wisdom

p: zhì zhě lè shuǐ, rén zhě lè shān
e: the wise take joy in water; the benevolent take joy in mountains
d: Lúnyǔ 6.23. The locus classicus of the 山水 dyad. 乐 is read lè (to take joy in) here , the older causative/affective reading. The couplet pairs water with 智 (wisdom , adaptive, flowing, responsive) and mountains with 仁 (benevolence , enduring, supporting, still).

e: China is a nation of ritual and propriety
d: A classical phrase of national self-identification: China sees itself as the civilization that most completely developed and transmitted the principles of ritual propriety. Used in cultural pride contexts and historical writing. 礼仪之邦 = "a land of ritual propriety."
中 zhōng (center) + 间 jiān (space). The space in the middle, whether of a row, a room, or a stretch of time: 坐在中间 "to sit in the middle," 在两座山中间 "between two mountains."

The Mid-Autumn Festival (中秋节 Zhōngqiū Jié), 15th day of the 8th lunar month, centers on honoring the moon (月亮 yuèliàng) and the moon goddess 嫦娥 Cháng'é, who fled to the moon after drinking the elixir of immortality.

中文 zhōngwén (Chinese language) + 系 xì (department). The Chinese department of a university. The bare 系 is the academic department itself, so any field plugs in front of it: 数学系 math department, 法律系 law department.

中 zhōng (middle) + 心 xīn (heart). Lit. "middle heart." The conceptual and physical center of something: a city, an argument, an organization. Used freely in both spatial and abstract senses. Extremely productive in compound formation: any institution can become a 中心 by adding its domain.

中 zhōng (Chinese) + 药 yào (medicine; drug). Chinese herbal medicine: the pharmacological branch of TCM. The classical formulary contains thousands of substances: plant-based (ginseng 人参 rénshēn, astragalus 黄芪 huángqí, wolfberry 枸杞 gǒuqǐ), mineral (cinnabar 朱砂 zhūshā), and animal-derived.

e: the Ghost Festival — Daoist name for the 15th of the 7th month
d: 中 zhōng (middle) + 元 yuán (origin; first; primary) + 节 jié (festival; season). The Daoist name, derived from the Three Officials calendar: 上元 (upper prime, 1st month, 15th), 中元 (middle prime, 7th month, 15th), 下元 (lower prime, 10th month, 15th). Each 元 is the birthday of one official.

The Central Plain , the heartland of the Yellow River basin, corresponding broadly to modern Henan province and adjacent areas. To "take the Central Plain" (逐鹿中原 zhú lù Zhōngyuán, "chase the deer across the Central Plain") is a classical idiom for competing for control of China.

e: loyalty and sympathetic understanding — the two-sided practice of 仁
d: 忠 zhōng: doing one's utmost , putting full effort into one's duties toward others. 恕 shù: sympathetic understanding , "considering others from one's own position" (like 如 rú, "as if," + 心 xīn, "heart"). Together they name the positive and negative expressions of the Golden Rule.
终点 (zhōngdiǎn, end point) + 站 (stop): the final stop on a route, where the line ends and everyone gets off. Its opposite is 起点站 qǐdiǎnzhàn, the first stop.
种 zhǒng (kind; to sow) + 子 zi. The seed sense of 子 made explicit. By extension it names a "seeded" competitor in a tournament, the one expected to grow into a winner.

A foreign court judgment is hard to enforce in China, while an arbitration award can be enforced under the New York Convention. Many contracts name 中国国际经济贸易仲裁委员会 (CIETAC) or the Hong Kong (HKIAC) or Singapore (SIAC) centres. 管辖 (guǎnxiá) is jurisdiction; 适用法律 (shìyòng fǎlǜ) the governing law.

e: the gate of all wonders (Daodejing 1, closing)

d: 重 zhòng (heavy; important) + 点 diǎn (point). The heavy point, the part that matters most. 重点大学 "key universities," 划重点 "to mark the key points," the things to underline.
