e: "The point is" or "the main thing is
d: "The point is" or "the main thing is." Close cousin to 关键在于, slightly more conversational. Often used to refocus a discussion that has drifted: 重点是, 我们要不要去 ("the point is, are we going or not").

e: to re-read (chóng); to stress (a syllable, zhòng)
d: 重 + 读 , but 重 is a polyphone. chóngdú = "again-read," to re-read a book or article. zhòngdú = "heavy-read," to stress or accent a syllable in pronunciation. Same characters, different reading, different meaning entirely.
重 chóng (again) + 复 fù (to return; again). To do or say the same thing over: 重复一遍 "to repeat once more." Note the chóng reading: a common error is to read it zhòng.
重 zhòng (heavy) + 量 liàng (quantity; measure). The amount of heaviness, weight as measured: 重量很轻 "the weight is light." The bodily version is 体重 tǐzhòng, one's body weight.

e: to value; to attach importance to; to take seriously
d: 重 zhòng (to weigh heavily) + 视 shì (to regard; to view). To treat something as carrying weight, to give it due attention: 重视教育 "to value education." Its opposite is 忽视 hūshì, to overlook.

重 zhòng (heavy; weight) + 心 xīn (heart; center). A physics term that has crossed fully into metaphorical use: where the weight of attention, effort, or strategic priority lies. Used in business planning, policy discussions, and personal goal-setting.

e: anew; afresh; once more (from the start)
d: 重 chóng (again) + 新 xīn (new). To do something over from a fresh start: 重新开始 "to start anew," 重新考虑 "to reconsider." Stronger than a plain 又, it implies a clean slate.

e: Double Ninth; Double Yang — the festival name
d: 重 chóng (double; repeated; layered) + 阳 yáng (yang; the masculine creative principle; odd numbers; heaven). The name describes the cosmological condition of the date: two nine-yang numbers coinciding.

e: Double Ninth cake — the city dweller substitution
d: 重阳 Chóngyáng (the festival) + 糕 gāo (cake; steamed or baked confection). The cleverest detail of the festival: 糕 (gāo, cake) is homophonous with 高 (gāo, high).

重 zhòng (heavy; weighty; important) + 要 (essential; necessary). 重要 means "important" in the sense of having significant weight or consequence. One of the most common adjectives in Chinese. 非常重要 (extremely important) · 最重要的是… (Most importantly…).

e: zhuyu; Japanese cornelian cherry — the apotropaic sprig
d: 茱萸 is the Chinese name for Cornus officinalis (Japanese cornelian cherry) and related Zanthoxylum species. The plant is pungent and strongly scented, which in Chinese folk medicine and ritual practice made it repellent to malevolent forces and disease.

Abacus mental arithmetic: performing suanpan calculations by visualizing the instrument in the mind. Neurologically distinct from verbal mental arithmetic: brain imaging shows practitioners use visuospatial rather than language regions.

e: Zhuge Liang — the archetype of wisdom and loyalty
d: Liu Bei's chancellor and strategist, raised by the novel into the very image of genius: master of stratagems, weather, and the hearts of men, faithful to a losing cause to his last breath. His feather fan and calm became shorthand for the brilliant, devoted minister.

e: feudal lords — the Zhou-enfeoffed nobility who held the states
d: 诸 zhū (all; various) + 侯 hóu (marquis; noble). The 诸侯 were the lords of the Zhou-enfeoffed states, holders of hereditary titles (Duke, Marquis, Earl, Viscount, Baron , 公侯伯子男 gōng hóu bó zǐ nán) ranked in a hierarchy below the Zhou king.

e: Zhu Bajie — the pig, comic appetite
d: A former marshal of Heaven banished into a pig's body for misconduct, ruled by his appetites for food, sleep, and women, lazy, cowardly, and always scheming to abandon the quest. Yet he is also warm, funny, and ultimately faithful.
猪 (zhū, pig) + 肉 (meat). The most-eaten meat in China, so common that 肉 alone often means pork by default in recipes.

e: Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove
to host; to preside over; to chair
d: 主 zhǔ (to preside) + 持 chí (to hold). To run an event from the chair: to host a show, chair a meeting, or take charge of a project. The host of a broadcast is a 主持人 zhǔchírén.

e: to take the initiative; proactive; of one's own accord
d: 主 zhǔ (master; to take charge) + 动 dòng (to act). To move first and on one's own, rather than waiting to be pushed. Its opposite is 被动 bèidòng (passive). 主动帮忙 "to help without being asked."
主 zhǔ (master) + 人 rén (person). The one who owns a thing or receives a guest: an animal's owner, a house's master, the host of a gathering. Its pair is 客人 kèrén, the guest.

Staple food: the rice, noodles, or dumplings served at the end of a Chinese meal. The late arrival of the staple signals that the banquet was generous enough that no one needed to fill up on carbohydrates.

主 zhǔ (main; principal) + 题 tí (theme). The central idea that organizes a work, an event, or a piece of music: 电影的主题 "the theme of the film," 主题公园 "a theme park." It is the heading that everything else serves.

e: The seat of honor at a table
d: The seat of honor at a table: typically facing the door, with one's back to the kitchen or wall. Assigning the 主位 to the senior guest or the person being celebrated is a face-giving act.
主 zhǔ (presiding) + 席 xí (seat; mat). Literally "the presiding seat," the one who sits at the head of a meeting or a state. Used for the chair of a committee and for a head of state.

主 zhǔ (master; host; main; primary) + 要 (essential). "The main/essential one." Used to identify the principal element among several: 主要问题 (the main problem) · 主要原因 (the primary reason) · 主要目标 (the primary goal). Common in analysis, journalism, and academic writing.
主 zhǔ (governing) + 意 yì (intention). The plan one settles on, the idea one acts by: 好主意 "a good idea," 拿主意 "to make up one's mind." Note the neutral tone on yi.

e: to advocate; to maintain; a stance; a position
d: 主 zhǔ (to decide) + 张 zhāng (to stretch; to spread). As a verb, to put forward and stand by a view; as a noun, the view itself: 我主张和平 "I advocate peace," 这是我的主张 "this is my position."
住 (live, stay) + 院 (the hospital courtyard). Separable: 住了三天院 is three days in the hospital. Its exit is 出院 (be discharged), the phone call every family waits for.
注 zhù (to annotate; to gloss) + 脚. Annotation at the foot of the page. A more elegant alternative to the modern compound 脚注 jiǎozhù (which has the same components in reverse order).

e: to fix one's gaze; to give attention to
d: 注 (to pour into; to concentrate) + 目 (eye). To concentrate the eye on something. A formal register word for focused attention: 引人注目 yǐn rén zhùmù means "eye-catching" or "attention-drawing."

e: to pay attention; to take note; to watch out
d: 注 zhù (to pour; to fix) + 意 yì (notion; attention). To pour the mind onto something, that is, to pay attention: 注意安全 "mind your safety," 请注意 "please take note."

e: to bless; to wish someone well; best wishes
d: 祝 zhù (to wish; to pray for) + 福 fú (blessing). To send blessings to someone, as a verb or noun. 送上我的祝福 = "I send you my best wishes." Standard in holiday messages, weddings, and farewells.

e: grasp firmly; make the most of (time)
d: 抓 (zhuā, to grab) + 紧 (tight). To grab and hold with no slack. Literally to grip something hard, figuratively to seize time and not waste it: 抓紧时间 (zhuājǐn shíjiān), make the most of the time.
China has three kinds: 发明专利 (fāmíng zhuānlì) invention patents, 实用新型 (shíyòng xīnxíng) utility models for structural improvements, and 外观设计 (wàiguān shèjì) design patents for appearance.

专 zhuān (focused; sole) + 门 mén (field). Concentrated on one doorway. As an adjective, specialized: 专门知识 "specialized knowledge." As an adverb, specially or on purpose: 我专门来看你 "I came specially to see you."

专 zhuān (to specialize; sole) + 业 yè (field of study). As a noun, the major one studies: 我的专业是历史 "my major is history." As an adjective, professional or specialized: 专业知识 "specialized knowledge," 很专业 "very professional."

e: to turn; to shift; to transfer
to transform; to convert; to change from one form into another
d: 转 zhuǎn (to turn; to shift) + 化 huà (to transform). 转化 names a conversion across a boundary: one form, type, or state turning into another. It is the standard word in science, philosophy, and economics for systematic conversion, the conditions under which A becomes B.
Prayer wheel: a cylindrical object containing mantras, rotated clockwise by practitioners. Each rotation is considered equivalent to reciting the mantra contained within.

Entrepôt , a port where goods are imported, stored, and re-exported without significant processing. Hong Kong's entire colonial economic logic was entrepôt trade, and it retains this function today as a major transshipment hub alongside its role as a financial center.

e: reincarnation; transmigration; rebirth into a new form
d: 转 zhuǎn (to turn; to shift; to transmit) + 世 shì (lifetime; generation; world). The specific act of being reborn into a new form, the individual instance of the larger cycle of 轮回.

e: To make money, to be profitable
d: To make money, to be profitable. The opposite pair is 赔钱 (péiqián) or 亏本 (kuīběn). 这个生意不赚钱: this business doesn't make money, the verdict that ends ventures.

e: Zhuangzi, the Daoist text and its author
top scorer; the imperial exam's first graduate
d: The palace examination's number one, personally ranked by the emperor, paraded through the capital on horseback. The word now crowns any field's best: 高考状元 (top gaokao scorer), 行行出状元 ("every trade produces its zhuangyuan," the proverb that dignifies all work).
Prepare + brought-to-good-state. 准备好了吗? ("ready?") starts every race, road trip, and presentation in the language. The reply 好了 borrows the complement alone, an answer made of pure result.

e: The existential pattern: place + 有 + thing
d: The canonical existential 有 structure. Place word or place phrase comes first, followed by 有, followed by the indefinite thing being asserted to exist. The place functions as the topic , the frame within which existence is being asserted.
桌 zhuō (table) + 子 zi. A textbook example of the bare suffix: the root 桌 rarely stands alone, and 子 makes it a usable noun.

p: zǐ fēi yú, ān zhī yú zhī lè?
e: You are not a fish — how do you know the happiness of fish?
d: From 秋水 (Autumn Floods), one of the Outer Chapters. Huizi challenges Zhuangzi's claim that the fish are happy. The exchange is a philosophical demonstration of perspectivism: every claim about the inner states of others is made from outside those states.
子 zǐ (sons) + 女 nǚ (daughters). A formal, collective term for one's children as a group, common in writing about family and law. Here 子 keeps its full third tone.

e: purple clay teapot — the Yixing treasure

d: Purple Forbidden Enclosure, the innermost of the Three Enclosures, surrounding the North Celestial Pole and representing the emperor's innermost palace in the sky. The name echoes 紫禁城 (Zǐjìn Chéng, the Forbidden City): both derive from 紫微, the ancient name for the pole star region.

字 zì (individual character) + 典 diǎn (canon; standard reference; classic text). A dictionary organized by radical, stroke count, or pronunciation that defines individual characters. The 典 suffix appears in 经典 jīngdiǎn (canonical classics); a 字典 is a canonical reference for individual characters.

字 zì (character) + 母 mǔ (mother; source; matrix). Literally: "character-mothers," the foundational elements of an alphabetic system from which all words are born. The term applies to any alphabetic system: the English alphabet, the pinyin romanization system, the Cyrillic alphabet.

字 zì (character; text) + 幕 mù (curtain; screen, as in 银幕 yínmù, the silver screen). Literally: "character-curtain." The text that appears across the screen like writing on a curtain. A modern compound that elegantly extends the ancient components into a contemporary context.

字 zì (character) + 体 tǐ (body; form; style). The physical form a character takes, whether in print, on screen, or in handwriting. Covers both digital fonts and handwriting styles. The same character can appear in multiple 字体: the same 字, different bodies.

e: the key word; the word one fastens on
d: 字 zì (character; word) + 眼. The eye of the phrase , the single word that carries the weight, that you pivot a sentence on, that an opponent picks at. 抠字眼 kōu zìyǎn "to pick at the wording" (often pejoratively, like English "splitting hairs over phrasing").
自 zì (self) + 传 zhuàn (a life record). A biography written by its own subject, the story of a life told in the first person: 写自传 "to write an autobiography." Like 传记, it takes the zhuàn reading.

e: ever since; from the time that
d: 自 zì (from) + 从 cóng (from; since). A conjunction marking a starting point in the past, paired with a later clause: 自从他来了以后 "ever since he arrived." Used only of time already begun, never the future.

e: self-aggrandizing; thinking oneself greater than one is; conceited
d: 自 zì (self) + 大 dà (great; large; important). Consistently negative , the failure of accurate self-assessment in the direction of inflation. Where 骄傲 can sometimes be legitimate pride, 自大 always describes a distortion: the person who claims more importance than they possess.

e: automatic; automatically; of one's own accord
d: 自 zì (self) + 动 dòng (to move). Moving by itself, without anyone working it: 自动门 "automatic door," 自动售货机 "vending machine." Also of people acting unprompted: 自动报名 "to sign up on one's own."

e: oneself; myself, yourself, himself (etc.); one's own
d: 自 zì (self) + 己 jǐ (oneself). The everyday reflexive word, flexing to whatever person the sentence needs: 我自己 "myself," 你自己 "yourself." It also marks possession, 自己的房间 "one's own room," and stresses doing a thing without help.

e: one of us; an insider; our own people
d: 自己 zìjǐ (oneself) + 人 rén. Someone who belongs to your group: your team, your family, your circle of trust. The implied contrast is always 外人 wàirén (outsider). 都是自己人，不用客气 "We're all family here, no need for formality" is an expression of warmth that lowers the social register instantly.

自 zì (self; one's own) + 家 jiā (family; home). Marks something as belonging to or originating from one's own household. Central to the Chinese social concept of insiders vs. outsiders: 自家人 (one of our own) vs. 外人 wàirén (an outsider).

e: complacent; self-satisfied; smug; resting on one's laurels
d: 自 zì (self) + 满 mǎn (full; satisfied). The state of being full , too full to receive more, too satisfied to keep improving. The classical warning 满招损 is precisely directed at 自满.

e: naturally and inevitably; of its own accord
the natural world; the realm of nature
to turn oneself in; to confess to the authorities
d: 自 zì (oneself) + 首 shǒu (to bow the head, to confess). To give oneself up to the law of one's own accord, before being caught. A legal term: voluntary surrender that often earns a lighter sentence. The head bows itself before justice.

e: the self; the ego; self- (in compounds)
d: 自 zì (self) + 我 wǒ (I; me). The self as an inner concept, the "ego" of psychology and philosophy. As a prefix it forms self-directed actions: 自我介绍 "self-introduction," 自我批评 "self-criticism."
自 zì (self) + 信 xìn (to trust; believe). To trust in oneself: 他很自信 "he is very self-assured." A close cousin is 自尊 zìzūn (self-respect), another of the many self- compounds built on 自.
The most prototypical 被 sentence. Theft is unwanted, the subject (bicycle) is the victim, the agent (the thief) may or may not be named. The 了 marks the completion of the unfortunate act.
自 zì (self) + 由 yóu (to follow; from). Literally "following from oneself," to act from one's own will rather than another's: 言论自由 "freedom of speech," 行动自由 "freedom of movement."
宗 zōng (ancestor; lineage) + 教 jiào (teaching). The general word for religion, the handed-down teaching that a community is built around: 宗教信仰 "religious belief."

宗族 is the term for the patrilineal descent group: all those who share a common named male ancestor and who collectively maintain the ancestral hall and genealogy. In rural China, entire villages are often single-lineage settlements (单姓村 dān xìng cūn), with all residents sharing a surname.
综 zōng (to gather; to sum) + 合 hé (to join). To draw many parts into one comprehensive whole: 综合考虑 "to consider comprehensively," 综合大学 "a comprehensive university."
"In short" or "all in all." Conclusion marker that wraps up an explanation. Signals you have said your piece and are now landing the summary: 总之, 我觉得不错 ("all in all, I think it's fine").

Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves, traditionally triangular or cylindrical. Made with various fillings: red bean paste, salted egg yolk, cured pork. The characteristic food of the Dragon Boat Festival, eaten to commemorate Qu Yuan.

e: to travel the whole world; to have been everywhere
d: 走遍 zǒu biàn (to walk/travel all over; to cover thoroughly , 遍 is a comprehensive coverage complement) + 天下 (all under heaven; the whole world). The ambition of the traveler: to have seen everything, to have left no corner of the world unvisited.

e: to walk out of; to emerge from
d: 走 zǒu (walk; leave) + 出 (exit complement). The most neutral directional compound: walking across a threshold from inside to outside. Used for physical exits and metaphorical ones , 走出困境 (walk out of a difficult situation), 走出阴影 (emerge from the shadow of something).

走 zǒu (walk; go) + 道 (way; path). The path you walk: a corridor between rooms, an aisle on a plane or train, a narrow walkway between structures. Practical and architectural: the space designated for movement through an enclosed or constrained area.

e: to use personal connections to get something done
d: 走 zǒu = to go through; to travel via. 走关系 means to go through the channel of personal connections to accomplish something that might otherwise be difficult or slow.

Literally "going through the back door": using gifts and personal relationships to obtain favors, preferential treatment, or access that would not be available through formal channels. The phrase acknowledges the reality of this practice without fully endorsing it.

e: to travel the roads making a living; to hustle; to work itinerantly
d: Traditional use: traveling performers, fortune-tellers, medicine sellers, acrobats , people who made their living moving from town to town, outside the settled economy.

走 zǒu (to walk/go) + 路 lù (road; path). To walk , the action of foot-travel. 走路去 = to walk there (contrast: 开车去 to drive, 坐地铁去 to take the subway). Also used metaphorically: 走上了一条不归路 "walked a road of no return" · 走对了路 "took the right path (in life)." 请走路 = "please use the footpath" (on signs).

e: to move toward; trend; the run or layout of something
d: 走 zǒu (to go) + 向 xiàng (toward). As a verb, to head toward an outcome: 走向成功 "to head toward success." As a noun, the trend or physical run of a thing, as in the 走向 of a mountain range or a market.

Concession , the zones of extraterritorial foreign governance established in Shanghai and other treaty ports. The foreign concessions in Shanghai operated from 1843 to 1943, when wartime politics prompted their formal retrocession to China.

e: to lease, to rent on loan
d: 租 (to rent) + 借 (to borrow). A bound compound for taking something for temporary use, often with a fee: leasing land, chartering equipment, the historical "leased territories" (租借地) of treaty-port China.

足 (foot) + 迹 (trace, mark). The imprint a foot leaves , both physical footprints and the metaphorical traces left by a life or a civilization. 留下足迹 (to leave one's footprints); 遍布全国的足迹 (footprints spread across the whole country).
足 (foot) + 球 (ball). The foot-ball: soccer in China and Taiwan. The Chinese Football Association (中国足球协会) governs 足球 nationally.

e: clan genealogy — the lineage's living memory
d: 族谱 (also 家谱 jiāpǔ or 宗谱 zōngpǔ) is the written genealogical record of a lineage. It records birth, death, marriage, official appointments, and notable achievements of every member, generation by generation.
祖 zǔ (ancestor, forebear) + 父 fù (father). The father's father, in formal register. Spoken Mandarin uses 爷爷 yéye for the same man, the way 爸爸 stands in for 父亲.

e: best; had best, it would be best to

d: 最 zuì (most; superlative) + 后 (behind; last). The furthest back position in a sequence: the final item, the last moment, the ultimate outcome. Functions as both an adverb before a verb (最后他同意了 , in the end he agreed) and as an adjective modifying a noun (最后一页 , the last page).

With 最 zuì (most), 喜欢 expresses a favourite. The attributive pattern 最喜欢的 + Noun gives "favourite X": 我最喜欢的电影 (my favourite film). This is the standard way to say "favourite," since Chinese has no single adjective for it.
"Most importantly." Marks the top-priority item in a list or argument. 最重要的是健康 ("the most important thing is health"). Useful for ranking points by significance.

昨 zuó (yesterday; past) + 天 tiān (day). The 昨 character is rarely used outside this compound and 昨晚 zuówǎn (last night) in modern Chinese. Note the tonal transition: 昨 zuó is tone 2, 天 tiān is tone 1, two rising pitches in sequence, which requires attention in spoken practice.

h: 昨天 · 今天 · 明天
e: the day series, and its symmetric siblings
d: The day series runs 前天 (day before yesterday) · 昨天 · 今天 · 明天 · 后天 (day after tomorrow). Years mirror it exactly: 前年 · 去年 · 今年 · 明年 · 后年. Weeks and months use 上/下 (above/below) instead: 上个星期 (last week), 下个月 (next month).

e: the left side; on the left
d: 左 (left) + 边 (side; edge). The most neutral, everyday word for "the left side." Used in directions, descriptions of position, and navigation. 在左边 (on the left), 左边的门 (the door on the left). Paired with 右边 yòubiān (the right side) for balanced descriptions of both sides of something.

e: the Zuo Commentary — the primary narrative source for the Spring and Autumn period
d: Traditionally attributed to Zuo Qiuming (左丘明 Zuǒ Qiūmíng) and covering 722–468 BCE, the 左传 is the great narrative expansion of the Chūnqiū chronicle.

e: heterodox sects and methods; unorthodox ways
d: 左道 (the left way, the deviant path) + 旁门 (a side gate, a door off to the side). 道 is the orthodox central path; 左道 is the path that veers left of it. 旁门 extends the spatial metaphor , not the main gate, but a side entrance used by those who cannot or will not use the front.

左 (left) + 手 (hand). Straightforward compound for the left hand. 左撇子 zuǒpiězi is the colloquial word for a left-handed person (撇 piě is the name of the left-falling stroke in calligraphy; 子 nominalizes).

e: to assist; an aide; subordinate official
d: The cognate character: 人 (person radical) + 左 (left, the assisting hand). 辅佐 fǔzuǒ means "to assist a ruler or superior" , the two characters are near-synonymous, both meaning to support from a flanking position.

作 (do) + 弊 (fraud, malpractice). Exam cheating is a criminal offense in China for national exams, policed with metal detectors and signal jammers, which measures how much the tests are worth. The honest sibling 打小抄 (crib notes) covers the classroom misdemeanor.

作 zuò (to create; to make; to compose) + 家 jiā. The term implies literary seriousness and sustained creative output, not just anyone who writes. The 家 suffix distinguishes this from 记者 jìzhě (journalist) or 编辑 biānjí (editor), which are professional roles without the mastercraft implication.
作 zuò (to compose) + 品 pǐn (article; item). A finished creative work: 文学作品 "a literary work," 这是他最好的作品 "this is his finest work."

e: to act as; in the capacity of; conduct; achievement
d: 作 zuò (to do; to act) + 为 wéi (to be; to serve as). Two near-synonyms combined for emphasis on role or capacity. As a preposition phrase: 作为一个老师 (in the capacity of a teacher / as a teacher). As a noun: 他很有作为 (he has accomplished a great deal; he is a person of achievement).

作 zuò (to do; to make) + 业 yè (coursework). The schoolwork a student is assigned: 做作业 "to do homework," 家庭作业 "home assignment." In technical contexts it also means a work operation, as in 水下作业 "underwater operations."

e: the homework was criticized by the teacher
d: Here the agent (老师, teacher) is explicitly named , the full 被 structure. The subject (homework) is criticized; criticism is typically unwanted. Note the result element 了 marking completion. Compare: 老师批评了作业 (teacher criticized the homework , SVO, neutral) vs.

作 zuò (to do; to make; to act) + 用 yòng (function; use). The most abstract 用 compound: not the act of using, but the role or effect that something exerts. 作用 describes what an entity does in a system , its causal contribution.

e: author; writer; the one who made it
d: 作 zuò (to compose) + 者 zhě (the one who). The maker of a work, most often a writer but usable for any creator. Compare 作家 zuòjiā, which specifically means a professional writer or author by trade.

e: sitting meditation — the formal practice of Chan
d: 坐 zuò (sit) + 禅 chán (dhyāna). Extended periods of seated meditation , in Japan called zazen 坐禅. Chan monasteries typically structure the day around multiple periods of 坐禅, sometimes lasting hours in intensive retreats (禅七 chán qī, seven-day intensive).
做 zuò (to make) + 菜 cài (dish). To cook, in the sense of making the dishes for a meal. 他很会做菜 "he is a good cook." Its near-neighbor 做饭 zuò fàn frames the same act around the staple rice.

e: to accomplish; to achieve; to manage to do
d: 做 zuò (to do; to make) + 到 dào (arrive at the result). Doing that reaches its endpoint: the task is completed, the goal achieved. Carries a sense of managed difficulty , you worked until arrival.

e: to observe the seven-day mourning rites
d: 做 zuò (to perform) + 七 qī (seven, a seven-day period). The funeral custom of holding rites for the dead every seventh day for seven cycles, forty-nine days in all. Each 七 marks a stage in the soul's passage; the seventh and final period (七七 or 满七) closes the formal mourning.

e: working the green — the oxidation control step
to conduct oneself; to be the kind of person one should be
d: 做 zuò (to do; to act as; to make) + 人 rén. The verb that captures the Confucian view that being human is an achievement, not a given. 做人 is learned: how to navigate relationships, honor obligations, maintain dignity, and treat others with genuine consideration.

e: to handle matters; to work; to conduct oneself in action
